refbjerg.z: A Danish workshop founded by Søren Refbjerg Rasmussen in 1969; known first for selling more than a million semi-freehand pipes, then for its Corsican briar and meticulous craftsmanship.

ivan-holst-nielsen.z: A Danish pipe master known from the late 1960s through the 1970s, who, according to records, returned to the bench around 2008 after a long hiatus. His pipes are shaped through hand drilling and hand sanding.

turkiyede-pipo-mevzuat-cercevesi.b: Pipe Smoking in Türkiye: The Regulatory Framework
turkiyede-pipo-mevzuat-cercevesi.z: In Türkiye, pipes and pipe tobacco fall under a framework set by Law No. 4733, which regulates the market, and Law No. 4207, which restricts consumption. This entry summarizes the basic rules, including the indoor smoking ban, age limit, and advertising ban, in general terms.

pipes-by-wolfgang.z: A small workshop founded by Wolfgang Blazejewski in the Canadian province of Ontario, known for pipes shaped entirely by hand without a lathe.

kiraz-ve-armut-agaci-pipolar.z: Before briar took over, European turners relied on cherry and pear wood; the two fruitwoods still form the bowls of cheap, light pipes today.

pipo-patentleri-tescil-kayitlarinin-tari.b: Pipe Patents: What Registration Records Tell Us About Dating
pipo-patentleri-tescil-kayitlarinin-tari.z: How the distinction between invention patents, design registrations, and trademarks matters for dating pipes; the scope and limits of 19th-century US records, and how a stamp gets tied to a document.

amerikan-baskanlarina-armagan-edilen-pip.z: A tradition that began in 1881 with the meerschaums William Demuth presented to President Garfield and closed in 1984 with a Peterson pipe given to Reagan: a century-long record of gift pipes the tobacco industry sent to the White House.

erken-donem-dunhill-od-pipolari.z: The obscure origin of the OD stamp that appeared in the 1920s, the 800-series shapes launched in 1950, and the emergence of the modern ODA line in 1953.

tobias-hose.z: A German maker who set up his bench in 2016, presents his pipes under the name Bonsai Pipes, and is known for his hand-cut ebonite stems.

tonni-nielsen.z: A Danish freehand master trained at the W.Ø. Larsen workshop in Copenhagen, who began producing under his own name in 1978 and has worked in Kentucky since 1983.

irmismarbel-meerschaum.z: A brand name once used in export channels for the work of Eskişehir meerschaum master Ahmet Gövem. This single-bench workshop, rooted in four generations of family craft, produces both figural carved bowls and classic pipe shapes.

apple-ailesi.z: The collective name for classic pipe shapes with a round bowl: Apple, Tomato, Egg, Acorn, and Brandy. The family's members are all variations on the same soft silhouette, stretched and pressed in different proportions.

sam-adebayo.z: American pipe maker Sam Adebayo, working in Nashville, produces handmade pipes under his own name alongside his role at the BriarWorks workshop.

corrado.z: A small-output line of handmade pipes signed by Italian maker Corrado Frignani, a designer by background, known for a detachable "Hoof" condensation piece.

brgart.z: The bench of self-taught Dane Leo Børgart, who worked as a police officer in Copenhagen for twenty-five years before moving into full-time pipemaking in 1991.

olsen.z: A Danish workshop founded in 2006 in Grevinge by Henrik Olsen, who retired after a workplace accident; produces small-scale work in classic shapes.

rossi.z: An Italian pipe factory founded in 1886, which grew up in Barasso in the province of Varese. It was considered the world's largest producer between the two world wars, turning out tens of thousands of pipes a day, and closed in the mid-1980s.

pipo-temizligi-ve-bakimi.z: A guide covering the stages of post-smoke, regular, and deep cleaning for a pipe, the classic salt-and-alcohol method, and how care differs by material.

yeti-pipe-co.z: The brand of Micah Cryder, who works alone in Montana; named after the legendary mountain creature, it produces American-made pipes shaped entirely by hand.

tabako-bon.z: Tabako-bon is the tray, box, or small chest of drawers that gathered everything needed for kiseru smoking into a single set, used in Japanese homes, shops, and tea rooms. Developed from the incense ceremony's tray, it became a fixture of nearly every household during the Edo period.

downie-pipes.z: The one-man workshop of Stephen Downie, who works in British Columbia, Canada; known for figural and sculptural pipes alongside classic molds.

wiener-kaffeehauspfeife.z: A composite-build pipe type from 19th-century Viennese coffeehouses, lent to patrons: a six-sided white clay bowl fitted with a long cherrywood stem.

pipedia-pipo-bilgisinin-ortak-arsivi.b: Pipedia: The Shared Archive of Pipe Knowledge
pipedia-pipo-bilgisinin-ortak-arsivi.z: An English-language online collaborative reference site running on MediaWiki, holding thousands of pages and tens of thousands of photographs on pipe brands and makers.

briyarda-damar.z: The grain pattern arising from briar's water-carrying capillary channels: how it forms, its main patterns such as straight grain and birdseye, and its place in pipe evaluation.

sommer.z: Sommer is a French pipe house founded in 1855 by Jean Sommer that stayed in business for more than a century. With its shop Aux Carrières d'Écume in the Passage des Princes, it is counted among Paris's iconic addresses for meerschaum pipe making.

pipas-soler.z: A Spanish briar business based in Amer, Girona, with roots going back to 1890, which moved from exporting rough blocks to making handmade freehand pipes.

nils-thomsen-pipes.z: The Berlin workshop and shop of Nils Thomsen, whose path ran from the East German army through construction contracting to the pipe bench.

porselen-pipo.z: A pipe type born in 18th-century German and French porcelain manufactories, valued as a display piece for its painted bowl, whose smoking quality has been debated since the 19th century because of its non-porous surface.

celtic-tobacco.z: The brand Czech maker Dušan Doubek gives to the hand-shaped briar pipes he produces at his workshop near Třešť, drawing inspiration from Celtic mythology.

letonya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in Latvia; it contains short, factual entries for two independent makers working in the capital, Riga.

sakurai.z: The Ken Pipes workshop, run by Japanese pipe maker Kenichiro Sakurai in the Niigata region, known for his path from graphic design to the pipe bench and for hand-painted stems.

masta.z: A British patented pipe brand founded in London around 1900, which passed to Parker in 1946 and dissolved into Parker-Hardcastle in 1967.

shurewood-pipes.z: The brand of Texas-based master Colin Rigsby, working alone at his bench; handmade briar pipes blending classic forms with the American artisan tradition.

david-gerstel.z: American writer of pipe-culture short stories and historical fiction, known for the narratives he publishes on Pipedia.

mariner.z: The workshop Joe Mariner opened in Napa, California in 1972 became one of the most-awarded names in 1980s American freehand pipes; the maker suspended production in 1987 to move into computer work.

dura-pipes.z: The one-man workshop of Swedish maker Dura Semjaniv, which grew out of a tobacconist's shop in Malmö; his pipes, known for their bamboo, boxwood, and horn inlays, bear the stamp "Dura Sweden."

fuhr-don-fuhrun-missourideki-yari-zamanl.b: Fuhr: Don Fuhr's Part-Time Missouri Workshop
fuhr-don-fuhrun-missourideki-yari-zamanl.z: Handmade American pipes Don Fuhr produced part-time at his home near Springfield, Missouri; what is known about him rests largely on a single source.

cemih-pipes-moldovadan-tek-kisilik-bir-t.b: Cemih Pipes: A One-Man Bench from Moldova
cemih-pipes-moldovadan-tek-kisilik-bir-t.z: The signature of Moldovan Mihail Cebanenco, who finishes each piece one by one on the lathe in his garage, with a strong emphasis on engineering detail in his handmade pipes.

benaderets.z: San Francisco's long-established tobacconist Benaderet's is known for house-branded pipes commissioned from English factories; when it closed in 1980, it was counted among California's oldest pipe and tobacco shops.

samuel-gawith.z: A historic tobacco house tracing its roots to 1792, producing in the English town of Kendal. Legendary for the flake tobaccos it presses using traditional methods.

ferndown.z: An English handmade pipe brand founded in the early 1980s by Dunhill's silver-mounting master Leslie 'Les' Wood and his wife Dolly Wood. Known for its distinctive 'Bark' rustication and silver bands individually fitted to each pipe.

zimpara-diskiyle-bicimlendirme.z: Shaping a drilled briar stummel on a rotating sanding disc: disc setup, grit sequence and speed, and the maker's stance relative to the disc.

tabago.z: A short-lived handmade pipe line that appeared in Denmark in the early 1970s, whose name was later also used by a Norwegian maker.

barney-suzuki.z: The life and work of Barnabas T. Suzuki, the collector, researcher, and club leader who is the most visible link between Japan's pipe circles and the international community.

bir-briyar-kesim-atolyesi-ziyareti-sasse.b: A Visit to a Briar Sawmill: Sassetta, the 1980s
bir-briyar-kesim-atolyesi-ziyareti-sasse.z: R.D. Field's travel piece, published in 1987, gives a firsthand account of the Sassetta cutting mill in Tuscany — a rare period record of one of the least-known links in the briar trade.

kaywoodie-koleksiyoncu-kilavuzu-ve-tarih.z: The scope and limits of a compiled guide that dates Kaywoodie pipes by cross-referencing factory catalogs, the clover-leaf stamp on the mouthpiece, and shape-number conventions.

porselen.z: A vitrified ceramic obtained by firing kaolin, feldspar, and quartz at high temperature, used for pipe bowls in Central Europe from the 18th century until the First World War.

ukrayna-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in Ukraine; contains short, factual entries for workshops around Kyiv and Kharkiv and for one-person benches.

storm.z: Frank Storm, working out of Minnesota, is an American craftsman known since the 1970s for pipe repair; after retiring he also made bespoke pipes to order in his own workshop.

henrik-kroll.z: A German pipemaker who taught himself the craft and set up his workshop in the early 2010s, known for hand-shaping all of his mouthpieces.

kiess-pipes.z: The workshop of Robert C. Kiess, who ran medicine and the pipe bench side by side for years; known for its Patriot, Heritage, and Ambassador grades and its distinctive rustication.

agizlik-isciligi.z: The process by which a pipe's mouthpiece turns from rod-form raw material into a finished piece: opening the tenon, rough shaping, and final hand-filed workmanship.

kumlamada-yuvarlaklik-ve-sap.z: On deeply sandblasted pipes, it's often noted that the bowl doesn't come out perfectly round and that the shank ends up thinner than the mouthpiece. Both come from the nature of the process and depend on decisions the maker makes ahead of time.

baldi.z: Pipes bearing the name of Genoese architect Baldo Baldi (1947-2021). Known for Ligurian briar, hand-filed sculptural bodies, and an annual output kept narrow from start to finish.

tabako-ire-ve-tonkotsu.z: Two containers used to carry tobacco in the Japanese smoking set: the soft leather or fabric pouch tabako-ire, and the hard-bodied, wood-carved tonkotsu. Their forms, metal clasps, and the miniaturizing trend of the late 19th century.

kj-pipes.z: The one-man workshop of Kadesh J. Swanson, working in Washington State; since late 2013 it has produced hand-shaped collector's pipes that pair Italian briar with German ebonite.

tyler-lane-pipes.z: The workshop of American part-time pipe maker Tyler Beard; his real influence on the community comes less from the pipes he made than from the Pipe Makers Forum he founded and the construction videos he published.

john-seiler-pipo-kurmacasi-yazan-koleksi.b: John Seiler: The Collector Who Wrote Pipe Fiction
john-seiler-pipo-kurmacasi-yazan-koleksi.z: American collector John P. Seiler, an engineer by profession, has worked since 2000 to give the pipe community its own literature through his Emperor Leopaldo stories.

karlheinz-joura.z: Karlheinz Joura (b. 1942), a former diver who fled East Germany and settled in Bremen, is counted among the most sought-after German pipe makers in international collector circles, producing only a few hundred straight-grain briar pipes a year.

balkan-harmani.z: A blend family dominated by Latakia and oriental tobaccos, named after the legendary Balkan Sobranie mixture. Its boundary with the English blend is still debated in the pipe world.

knights-briar-pipes.z: An American handmade pipe brand founded by Rick Knight in Monongahela, Pennsylvania, in the mid-2000s, operating at one-man workshop scale.

dremel.z: A high-speed rotary hand tool and brand used in pipe workshops for everything from drilling the mouthpiece slot to engraving a signature.

yil-kodu-oncesi-dunhill-tarihlendirmesi.b: Dating Dunhill Before the Year Code (1907-1921)
yil-kodu-oncesi-dunhill-tarihlendirmesi.z: How to date Dunhill pipes made before 1921, when the brand began striking a small year digit on the shank, using the city line, patent number, finish name, and secondary stamps.

guney-kore-pipo-markalari-dizini.b: Directory of South Korean Pipe Brands
guney-kore-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe makers documented in South Korea; it currently contains a single workshop record.

pellegrini.z: A small-scale American bench under which Ron Pellegrini carved pipes by hand and sold them under the Sovereign stamp at his shop on Staten Island, New York; ended in the mid-1980s.

perry-white-pipes.z: An American handmade briar pipe brand produced by maker Bob Swanson at his Florida workshop, known for the white ring repeated on every mouthpiece.

jhw-pipes.z: JHW Pipes, founded by a retired lawyer in the basement of his New Jersey home, became one of the leading workshops of American freehand pipe making in the 1970s; the young makers who came up through it went on to found the brands of the next generation.

white-dog-freehand-pipes.z: The brand of hand-shaped pipes Richard Baggenstos has produced alone in Inner Switzerland since 2004. The bench started with walnut and soon moved to Saint-Claude plateau briar.

leadwood.z: Combretum imberbe is a long-lived tree of the South African savanna; its wood is dense enough to sink in water, and in pipe making it's mostly a rare choice for accent parts like shank extensions and decorative rings.

t-hamilton.z: The story of a tobacconist's shop founded in Cambridge in the late 1880s, which its founder's elder sister ran for roughly twenty more years after his early death.

js-pipes.z: A small-scale American handmade pipe bench run by Joel Shapiro in California, known for its no-fill approach to briar imperfections.

colossus-pipe-factory.z: An American brand run by Kaufmann Bros. & Bondy in New York, known by its C.P.F. stamp on pipes, which fell out of circulation by the late 1910s.

d-mostras-pipes.z: A one-man Greek workshop that began in 2011 in a mountain village, using only Greek briar and olive wood. The four-digit number on its stamp gives the year of production and that year's sequence.

danimarka-pipo-markalari-dizini-2.z: The second and final part of the alphabetical directory of Danish pipe brands. Twenty-five brands from Peer Import to Zodiac, given as short entries with their recorded basic facts.

the-room-bir-aksam-iciminin-anlatisi.b: The Room: A Narrative of One Evening's Smoke
the-room-bir-aksam-iciminin-anlatisi.z: David Gerstel's short 2023 essay recounts a single evening in a windowless library, framed by the meerschaum figural chosen that night and a late-16th-century travel compendium it opens.

erdogan-ege.z: A meerschaum carver from Eskişehir. He began his apprenticeship under Raşit Aktaş in 1967 at age thirteen, spent many years supplying carved bowls to workshops, and is known for figurative work on portrait and animal themes.

sahin-pipo.z: Based in Istanbul's Eminönü district, Şahin Pipo is the best-known brand carrying on the mass production of briar pipes in Türkiye. Known for its Yıldız (Star) series and pipe accessories.

peterson-house-pipe-bir-asiri-boy-gelene.b: Peterson House Pipe: A Tradition of Oversized Bowls
peterson-house-pipe-bir-asiri-boy-gelene.z: The story of the large-bodied pipes designed to be smoked at home rather than carried by hand, running from the oversized System pipes in Peterson's 1896 catalogues to today's House Pipe series.

sos-ve-aromalandirma.z: The two-stage process that gives pipe tobacco its taste and scent: casing, which works deep into the leaf, and topping, applied to the surface just before packaging.

brian-levine-sektorun-her-halkasinda-cal.b: Brian Levine: A Host Who Has Worked Every Link of the Industry
brian-levine-sektorun-her-halkasinda-cal.z: The career of Brian Levine, who has worked across nearly every level of the American pipe industry — retail, importing, trade-association management, magazine publishing — and is best known as the host of The Pipes Magazine Radio Show.

pipas-martin.z: A Spanish workshop founded in the back room of a Valencia tobacco shop, known for freehand briar pipes with an unpainted, natural finish.

glen-ben-freehand-pipes.z: A freehand pipe line shaped by Richard Baggenstos on a grinding wheel, working only in free forms and stamping the shank with a grade mark on a zero-to-nine scale.

castello.z: A workshop brand founded in 1947 by Carlo Scotti in the Italian town of Cantù, where every pipe is finished by hand. It is regarded as the pioneer of post-war Italian pipe making's rise to international prestige.

mountbatten.z: A London-origin pipe brand associated with the Charatan workshop, long considered a second-quality line but also described as apprentice output.

faribault-piposu-pipo-tasindan-bir-bilme.b: The Faribault Pipe: A Riddle Carved in Pipestone
faribault-piposu-pipo-tasindan-bir-bilme.z: A figurative pipestone carving in the Minnesota Historical Society collection is one of the rare cases where a donation letter and the archival record don't agree; both its carver and its date of manufacture remain in dispute.

tutun-kurleme-yontemleri.z: Describes the four basic curing methods that turn fresh tobacco leaf into a smokable form, and which tobacco variety each is paired with.

missouri-meerschaum-model-rehberi.z: A comparative guide to the shape, size, and construction differences among the main models in Missouri Meerschaum's corncob pipe line.

buyuk-britanya-pipo-markalari-dizini-1.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in Great Britain; this first part introduces the 93 brands between A. Frankau & Co. and Page in short entries.

hedegaard.z: The brand under which Danish master Peter Hedegaard (1951-2007) produced pipes under his own name. Trained at the W. Ø. Larsen workshop, he was known for low, voluminous freehand shapes that visually set the bowl apart from the shank.

pipo-haznesi-olcusu.z: The diameter and depth of a pipe's bowl determine how much tobacco a single packing holds, how long the smoke lasts, and how much the bowl tends to heat up. This entry covers the archaeological origins of the measurement, its definitions, and why it has never been tied to a standard.

jan-harry-seiffert.z: Jan Harry Seiffert, son of a Kassel tobacco-trading family, trained in Denmark, Italy, and Ireland before founding his own workshop and turning out roughly a hundred pipes a year as a German maker.

servi.z: A Turkish meerschaum brand mentioned in pipe compilations. The record about it is thin; what sets the brand apart is its Signature line, where each pipe is signed with the name of the carver who made it.

talbert-pipes.z: An American workshop founded by Trever and Emily Talbert in 1998; after seven years working in France, they returned to the US, and work bog oak alongside briar.

bech.z: A small workshop founded by Knud Bech in the northern Danish town of Tårs; known for engraving his signature into the shank and stem instead of stamping.

kuziel-pipes.z: A small American workshop bearing the name of Connecticut-based painter and photographer Paul Kuziel, who made every pipe from his own drawing; its documented record is limited to 2008-2009.

misir-kocani-pipo.z: A pipe with a bowl turned from dried corncob, known for its lightness and dry smoke. Mass production has continued in Missouri since 1869.

jeremiah-sandahl.z: The workshop of American handmade pipe maker Jeremiah Sandahl, working in Minnesota; known for the briar pipes of a self-taught maker who started without a ready-made pipe-making kit.

crawford-pipes.z: An American handmade pipe brand crafted piece by piece by Jerry Crawford in his southern Oregon workshop, known for soft lines and a flared button.

cellini.z: A shared title for two separate pipe stories: a classically shaped line still in Pipe Brebbia's catalog in Italy today, and the Cellini Pipe Shop, which operated in Chicago for much of the twentieth century. The two branches are linked by trade, but they were never the same business.

isvicre-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe workshops and brand names founded in Switzerland: seven entries from Egloff to WR Freehand Pipes.

bugunun-briyar-pipo-piyasasi.z: The present-day shape of a scattered field where factory brands and one-person workshops, the local tobacconist and the online seller, the trade show and the auction, all stand side by side.

ikebana.z: The hand-worked top line of Japanese maker Tsuge. Led by Kazuhiro Fukuda for over forty years, the stamp passed to Asami Kikuchi after the master's retirement in 2024.

kapp-petersonin-yeni-internet-sitesi-duy.z: The announcement of the catalog-focused new website Kapp & Peterson launched at peterson.ie in the spring of 2020, and this step's place within the brand's corporate transformation.

italya-pipo-markalari-dizini-2.z: The second part of the alphabetical directory of Italian pipe brands: eleven short, factual entries for brands, workshops, and sub-labels, from Salmastro to Voyageur.

lane-limited.z: A pipe tobacco maker tracing its roots to 1890 Dresden, now headquartered in the US. Known for its Captain Black series and aromatic blends, chief among them 1-Q.

tom-palmer-soylesisi-peterson-of-dublini.b: Tom Palmer Interview: Peterson of Dublin's Managing Years
tom-palmer-soylesisi-peterson-of-dublini.z: An interview with Tom Palmer, the long-serving managing director of Peterson of Dublin, that records the brand's production scale, workshop training, and new-line policy in its 140th year.

sira-disi-pipolar-cift-hazneli-tasarimla.b: Unusual Pipes: A History of Double-Chamber Designs
sira-disi-pipolar-cift-hazneli-tasarimla.z: Pipes that step outside the classic bowl-and-stem arrangement: ornamental pieces never meant to be smoked, 19th-century patents for a chamber within a chamber, Africa's double-bowled pipes, and today's twin-chambered briars.

alan-brothers-pipes.z: An American brand founded in 2015 by brothers Jeff and Jeremy Gracik, known for a "benchmade" approach that leaves rough shaping to machine and finishing to the maker's hand.

madao-3000.z: The alias of Beijing-based maker Wang Tieyuan; a contemporary Chinese workshop that brings measured asymmetry to pipe shape informed by classical Chinese painting and poetry.

micoli-robert-burnsun-dremel-isciligiyle.b: Micoli: The American Bench Known for Robert Burns's Dremel Work
micoli-robert-burnsun-dremel-isciligiyle.z: The brand of American carver Robert "Mic" Burns, who set up his bench in 1968; known for the distinctive rustic texture cut with a hand rotary tool and for its E. Oslo sub-line.

gambier.z: Gambier was a clay pipe manufactory that operated in the French town of Givet from 1780 to 1928. With its bowls molded as portraits and figures, it is considered the best-known clay pipe brand of the nineteenth century.

eltang.z: A Danish workshop founded under his own name in 1980 by Tom Eltang, known for contrast staining and the Snail grade.

frank-axmacher.z: A contemporary German maker who moved from stone and wood sculpture into pipemaking, producing pipes one at a time by hand since 2004.

tornada-delme.z: Drilling the three holes in a pipe body on a lathe instead of a drill press: the mounting setup, drilling order, and the differences between bent and straight pipes.

strano.z: The name of the Strano brothers, who left their mark on the New York pipe scene in the mid-twentieth century; a family story combining Joe Strano's bench in Queens with Al Strano's role at Wally Frank Ltd.

manfred-hortig.z: The workshop of German master Manfred Hortig, who took up pipe making only after retirement and became known for a style built on carving and freehand forms, and his place within the Grainstorm circle.

provenzano.z: A handmade pipe workshop run by Cosimo "Mimmo" Provenzano in the town of Maglie, in the Salento region of southern Italy; known for thin-walled, Danish-influenced shapes and heavy use of bog oak.

sigara-paketi-kartlari-ve-pipo-konulu-di.z: How small cardboard cards inserted into cigarette packs as stiffeners turned into collectible objects, and the place of pipe-themed series within these sets.

memo-handmade-pipes.z: A one-person workshop run by Iranian craftsman Mehdi Aghdam; known for shapes close to the Danish line, clean surface finishing, and a craft education acquired through online sources.

pipo-muzayedeleri-ve-acik-artirma-kultur.z: As collectible pipes change hands at auction, house estimates, provenance, and condition reports become decisive. This article explains, through known estate sales, why auction results are so hard to predict.

altinok.z: A meerschaum brand based in Ankara, founded in 2002. Rather than a workshop with its own bench, it is a structure that brings together the work of independent carvers working in Eskişehir under a single name.

fransa-pipo-markalari-dizini-2.z: The second part of the alphabetical directory of French pipe brands: twelve brands, from SEG to Èmile Vuillard, presented in short, factual entries.

andrew-marks.z: The bench of American maker Andrew Marks, working in Vermont since 1969 and carving pipes one at a time from long-rested briar blocks.

baier.z: An American workshop run solo by Alfred Baier in Vermont, known for figurative carvings and hollowed-out freehand bodies.

il-duca.z: An Italian handmade pipe workshop run by Massimiliano Rimensi near Ferrara, known for a grading system drawn from noble titles.

kalumet-amerikan-yerlilerinin-kutsal-pip.b: The Calumet: The Sacred Pipe of Native Americans
kalumet-amerikan-yerlilerinin-kutsal-pip.z: The calumet is the sacred ceremonial pipe North American Indigenous peoples smoked for prayer, treaty-making, and important communal decisions. Known in the West as the 'peace pipe,' its function ran far wider than that name suggests.

totemstar-bir-gorsel-sanatcinin-los-ange.b: TotemStar: A Visual Artist's Los Angeles Bench
totemstar-bir-gorsel-sanatcinin-los-ange.z: TotemStar, the brand of Los Angeles-based visual artist Gunnar Weber-Prada, is a personal American bench marking quality grades with metal dots inlaid on the stem.

speden-pipes.z: The small-scale freehand pipe making that New Zealander Don Speden carried on using only hand tools after settling in Japan.

sirbistan-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands from Serbia, currently containing a short, factual entry for the single brand on record.

jan-pietenpauw.z: A South African handmade pipe brand under which Jean du Toit signs his work in the name of a maker who never existed; a father-and-son bench in Pretoria producing briar pipes with flowing lines.

japon-kisisel-icim-takimi.z: Because the kimono had no pockets, the Japanese smoking ensemble was hung from the sash: this arrangement of pipe case, tobacco pouch, bead, and toggle was both an everyday tool and a marker of status.

eski-pipo-ve-tutun-kitaplarinin-yeniden-.b: Reprints of Old Pipe and Tobacco Books
eski-pipo-ve-tutun-kitaplarinin-yeniden-.z: How pipe and tobacco literature out of print for a century has returned to circulation through print-on-demand, and where these reprints can be trusted and where they should be treated with caution.

lindner.z: The brand of American maker Michael Lindner, who began in the Michigan estate-pipe trade before starting his own line in 2000; known for a funnel-shaped bit and concave bite surface.

rosengren.z: A small-scale workshop run by Jonas Rosengren, who works in Halmstad on Sweden's west coast and moved from teaching woodworking to pipe making.

cesare.z: Cesare is the second brand carrying its own name used by the Cesare Barontini factory in Livorno, and it represents the export-facing wing of Italian series production.

morgan-pipes.z: An American brand founded by Chris Morgan in California in 2006; known for a handmade top line finished at his own bench alongside series lines made in Italy, and for the patented Briar Cigar design.

mergenler.z: A meerschaum pipe brand reportedly based in Istanbul, owned by Oksan Mergen. It closed in the 1990s; because its carvers worked unsigned, its pipes do not bear the makers' names.

ruetz-pipes.z: The brand of handmade pipes produced by Christian Ruetz in Silz, in Austria's Tyrol region; known for a style that places briar's untouched bark at the center of the design.

owl-shop.z: An American tobacconist business sharing the same name in two cities from a common family origin, founded in New Haven in 1934 and later branching into Worcester; known for its own blends and private-label pipes.

garfinkel-washingtonin-pipo-ve-tutun-duk.b: Garfinkel: Washington's Pipe and Tobacco Shop
garfinkel-washingtonin-pipo-ve-tutun-duk.z: A. Garfinkel, founded by Arnold Garfinkel after he fled Germany and settled in Washington, was a capital tobacconist known for the imported blends and pipes it sold under its own name.

imp.z: IMP is a brand name for block meerschaum pipes hand-carved in Türkiye and distributed mainly through the United States; the founding year and founder do not appear in public records, and registration of the brand name has changed hands over time.

zenz-pipes.z: A handmade pipe workshop run single-handedly by Klaus Zenz in Wiener Neustadt, Austria; known for Italian briar, hand-shaped mouthpieces, and wood-and-brass ornamentation.

ahsap-torna.z: The wood lathe, considered the pipe workshop's first major machine: its use in bowl drilling, turning, sanding, and polishing, along with the chucks, tools, and drill bits it requires.

r-quagliata-pipes.z: A one-man American pipe workshop based in Phoenix, Arizona, run by Ryan Quagliata, with records dating back to the late 2000s.

gbd-seri-adlari-ve-kalite-kademeleri.b: GBD Line Names and Quality Grades
gbd-seri-adlari-ve-kalite-kademeleri.z: How to read the line names stamped on the shanks of GBD pipes, the distinction between first and second grade, the grade order drawn from catalogues, and clues for dating.

royal-house-ltd.z: A brand name registered in the early 1960s to the American Pinkerton Tobacco Company and used on pipes made from imported briar. The US registration was cancelled in 2004.

bessai-cleveland-arcadede-iki-kusaklik-b.b: Bessai: A Two-Generation Pipe Shop in the Cleveland Arcade
bessai-cleveland-arcadede-iki-kusaklik-b.z: The pipe-making, repair, and tobacco shop John Bessai opened in the Cleveland Arcade in the late 19th century, run for nearly eighty years together with his son Herb Bessai.

jack-the-piper.z: A fictional name used by Giulliano Spitaletti, a jeweler and pipe maker working in England, for his bench; an example of the new generation of workshop identities produced by the online pipe community.

mummert.z: The workshop of self-taught German pipe maker Werner Mummert, based in Otterbach; known for sharp-edged bulldogs, glass-shanked designs, and deep sandblasting.

bantli-zimpara.z: Belt sanders used in the pipe workshop for shaping bodies and mouthpieces: benchtop combination machines, long-belt workshop rigs, and belt selection.

leo-pipes.z: A small South African workshop founded in 2001 by painter and pipe maker Leon du Preez, known for freehand pipes hand-shaped from native African woods.

peterson-deluxe-system-pipolarina-yakind.b: A Closer Look at Peterson Deluxe System Pipes
peterson-deluxe-system-pipolarina-yakind.z: The silver band, P-Lip mouthpiece, shape numbers, and collector standing of the Deluxe series, which forms the top tier of Peterson's System pipe family.

gasparini.z: Gasparini, a family workshop producing in the village of Luvinate in the Varese area of northern Italy, is known for working with naturally dried briar, its handmade \"Fatta a Mano\" series, and pipes fitted with meerschaum bowls.

xin-li.z: A Chinese pipe maker who has worked alone in Hangzhou since 2018, known for bamboo shanks and unusual body colors.

temperances-temporal-detective-agency-fi.b: Temperance's Temporal Detective Agency, Finding Time: A Serialized Pipe Fiction
temperances-temporal-detective-agency-fi.z: A steampunk science-fiction narrative published in serialized installments on Pipedia by a writer from the pipe community under the pen name "Professor Stanwell P. Briar"; its characters, pipe-smokers all, continue a time-travel series.

manhattan-briar-pipe-co.z: An American pipe company founded in New York in 1902, which operated for a time as the pipe-manufacturing arm of the American Tobacco Company and joined S. M. Frank & Co. in 1922.

radice.z: An Italian family workshop founded by Luigi Radice in Cucciago in 1980, descending from the Castello and Caminetto tradition; known for oil curing and its own distinctive surface finishes.

tutun-kutusu-kavanozu-ve-tenekesi.b: The Tobacco Box, Jar, and Tin
tutun-kutusu-kavanozu-ve-tenekesi.z: The history of an accessory family running from pocket horn boxes to the Delft jars on the tobacconist's shelf, from Bohemia's figural vessels to mass-produced pocket tins. Objects that have today lost their function and passed into the realm of collecting.

osmanlida-cubuk-kulturu.b: Chibouk Culture in the Ottoman Empire
osmanlida-cubuk-kulturu.z: The place of the long-stemmed tobacco chibouk in Ottoman society: a cultural history spanning more than two centuries, from the years of prohibition to coffeehouse pleasure and from hospitality customs to the chibouk-makers' guild.

jirsa.z: A Czech family workshop founded by Oldřich Jirsa in 1994, producing in Rynholec near Prague; known for combining CNC-assisted batch production with hand craftsmanship and its own house-made stems.

pipo-hazne-malzemeleri.z: An overview entry comparing the main materials used for pipe bowls — briar, meerschaum, clay, corncob, morta, calabash, and porcelain — against common criteria.

dino-da-campione.z: A handmade-pipe mark started in 1969 by Milan-born Leonardo Airaghi, taking its name from Campione d'Italia, an Italian enclave inside Switzerland. Its production, never exceeding a few hundred pieces a year, is known for its snail-marked internal grading and pursuit of an unbreakable mouthpiece.

idskov-piber.z: A small-volume Danish pipe workshop run at hobby scale by Carsten Idskov, a mathematics and woodworking teacher in Aarhus.

the-briar-workshop-vermontta-kurulan-bir.b: The Briar Workshop: An American Bench Founded in Vermont
the-briar-workshop-vermontta-kurulan-bir.z: A shared bench founded in Vermont in the 1970s by Elliott Nachwalter and Jorg Jemelka, where many American pipe makers learned bench discipline.

lester-c-garlow-taninmayan-bir-amerikan-.b: Lester C. Garlow: An Unsung American Briar Carver
lester-c-garlow-taninmayan-bir-amerikan-.z: An amateur maker who carved figural briar pipes in New York in the 1950s and never entered pipe literature in his own lifetime. He left behind about twenty-three pipes.

abd-pipo-markalari-dizini-2.z: The second part of the alphabetical directory of pipe brands, workshops, and makers in the United States: ninety entries from Glamp to New Jersey Briar Pipe Co.

kriswill.z: A brand founded in Kolding, considered one of Denmark's two largest pipe factories through the 1960s and 1970s. Known for its compass-rose stamp, its Bernadotte-signed series, and its export-oriented designs.

piponun-dunya-tarihi.b: The World History of the Pipe
piponun-dunya-tarihi.z: The history of pipe smoking, from its ceremonial roots in the Americas through Europe's clay and briar eras to the Ottoman çubuk and Eskişehir meerschaum.

johs.z: A brand carrying the name of Danish pipemaker Mogens Johansen; after years spent producing unsigned work for Bjarne, the workshop began appearing under its own stamp after 2008.

teipen-handmade-briar-pipes.z: An American handmade briar workshop run by Wayne Teipen in the town of Cloverdale, Indiana, limited to a few dozen pipes a year.

mullenbach-thewald.z: Founded in 1830 in Westerwald on clay pipes and pottery, this German firm later moved into briar and made pipes until 1972.

romeo-pipe.z: Hand-shaped Italian pipes produced under his own name by Domenico "Mimmo" Romeo, who grew up as a briar cutter in the Ligurian town of Taggia.

jose-rubio.z: The pipes of Jose Rubio, a workshop master working in Oviedo, in northern Spain, known for classic shapes and deep sandblasting.

pasargadtabac.z: A Tehran-based production and education venture, Pasargadtabac was founded in 2011 and is known for launching domestic briar pipe making in Iran. The name behind the brand is Amirhossein Rahimi.

mitch-kalter-s-m-pipesin-tezgah-tarafi.b: Mitch Kalter: The Bench Side of S&M Pipes
mitch-kalter-s-m-pipesin-tezgah-tarafi.z: Mitch Kalter is an American craftsman by profession a physician, who turned to pipe making in retirement. Working under the S&M Pipes name with his college friend Steve, he produces briar pipes one at a time.

giordano.z: The Giordano workshop, founded in the town of Badalucco in Liguria, supplying briar blocks to pipe makers around the world, and the story of its founder, Domenico Giordano.

peterson-pipolarini-tarihlendirme-bir-ka.b: Dating Peterson Pipes: A Rule-of-Thumb Guide
peterson-pipolarini-tarihlendirme-bir-ka.z: A rough dating guide for placing Peterson pipes into approximate periods using their origin stamps, silver hallmarks, and lettering style.

star-meerschaum.z: A relatively new Turkish brand based in the Üsküdar district of Istanbul, known for its pipes carved from block meerschaum. It highlights a push-fit mouthpiece connection borrowed from briar pipe making.

p-zhan-pipes.z: One of the first artisan pipe workshops from China to gain recognition abroad, founded in 2011 by Ping Zhan of Dalian. Produces around a hundred handmade briar pipes a year.

trever-talbertin-kesme-ve-bicimlendirme-.b: Trever Talbert's Sawing and Shaping Method
trever-talbertin-kesme-ve-bicimlendirme-.z: American pipemaker Trever Talbert's working order, which shapes the block with a band saw and a coarse grinding disc before drilling any holes.

weingott.z: A London brand founded in 1883 by Fleet Street tobacconist Samuel Weingott, regarded as an early milestone in the domestication of briar pipemaking in England, and absorbed into history after passing to Cadogan in 1980.

1970ler-ve-1980lere-tarihlenen-kutu-tutu.b: Tinned Tobacco Dating to the 1970s and 1980s
1970ler-ve-1980lere-tarihlenen-kutu-tutu.z: John C. Loring's compilation gathering pipe tobacco tins from these two decades in a single table, by maker, tin type, weight, and date, along with the special date abbreviations found in the Dunhill and Rattray's rows.

kemperling.z: Austrian pipe factory founded in Vienna in 1834 and continued in Mattsee after 1944; known for its briar pipes as well as Tyrolean pipes and carved wooden figures.

hirvatistan-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in Croatia, with short entries based on documented facts about two one-person workshops.

emiliano.z: The eponymous workshop of Brazilian master Emanuel Emiliano; produces handcrafted briar pipes in Curitiba and is known for shapes that lean close to the Danish line.

reichert.z: A German handmade-pipe signature Axel Reichert has produced, piece by piece, in the town of Merzig in Saarland since 1998.

pipo-onarimi-ve-agizlik-bakimi.z: A guide covering the cause and removal of oxidation on a vulcanite mouthpiece, adjusting a tenon that fits too loose or too tight, and the particular maintenance needs of a meerschaum pipe.

evan-handmade-briars.z: A small-scale pipe workshop in Rozel, Kansas, run by Mark "Evan" Schloemer using only hand tools; its signature became the local limestone inlay set into the mouthpieces.

tarp.z: The pipes of Danish maker Karsten Tarp, who trained at the Bari factory before setting up his own bench in Faaborg, and his grading system named after Viking ships.

c-kent-joyce.z: An American part-time pipe maker working out of a small outbuilding in his backyard in Noble, Oklahoma; known for freehand designs drawing on the Danish, Japanese, and Russian schools.

lips-pipeworks.z: A one-man American pipe workshop run by Thomas J. Lips of Portland, who worked exclusively in briar in the mid-2000s and drew every model he made himself.

rinaldo.z: An Italian pipe workshop founded in Pesaro in 1987 by brothers Elio and Guido Rinaldo, who make every pipe with their own hands. Known for its Y-based grading system and its Lithos, Sahara, and Triade finishes.

antonio-lancellotti.z: An Italian pipe maker working in the town of Oppido Lucano in Basilicata, who gained recognition quickly after taking up the lathe in 2021.

fe-ro.z: An Italian pipe factory working in Oltrona al Lago near Varese, named after its founder Federico Rovera. Alongside its own brand it does contract manufacturing for European firms; olivewood pipes and pipe accessories are also part of the production line.

yang-kun-pipes.z: A one-man workshop founded in 2012 by Chinese maker Yang Kun, working in Liuzhou; known for its footprint stamp, four-tier quality ranking, and grain-driven approach to shaping.

cubuk.z: The traditional long-stemmed pipe of the Ottoman world, sometimes reaching a length of a meter and a half; known for its three-part construction of a clay bowl, a wooden stem, and an amber mouthpiece.

j-k-pipes.z: A one-man pipe workshop founded on Denmark's Ærø island by Johan Kock in 1992, known for its morta mouthpieces and inlays and silver work.

pipolar-ve-insanlar-sarnanoda-bir-koleks.b: Pipes and Men: An Essay on a Collection in Sarnano
pipolar-ve-insanlar-sarnanoda-bir-koleks.z: A short 2023 essay by David Gerstel, published in Italics Magazine, that treats a thirty-piece figural meerschaum pipe collection in the Italian town of Sarnano through a literary lens.

morel.z: A French handmade pipe name carried across two generations in Saint-Claude, father and son; Pierre Morel Junior received the Meilleur Ouvrier de France title in the pipe category in 2007.

ingo-garbe.z: An independent pipe maker who began production in 1967, is considered Germany's first freehand pipe maker, and later settled on the Danish island of Læsø.

vesz-pipes.z: The Canadian workshop founded in Toronto in the late 1950s by Hungarian-born Julius Vesz, known for using long-buried "dead root" briar.

bonaquisti.z: An American handmade briar pipe brand made in limited numbers by Paul Bonacquisti at his one-man workshop in upstate New York, known for its Lustro, Ruvido, and Sabbia surfaces.

lule-tasinin-adlari-meerschaum-ecume-de-.b: The Names of Meerschaum: Meerschaum, Écume de Mer, Sepiolite
lule-tasinin-adlari-meerschaum-ecume-de-.z: The scientific, German, French, and Turkish names of the same mineral each arose from a different observation; the result has been a naming muddle that has persisted since the nineteenth century.

bennington-tobacconist.z: A family tobacconist business founded in 1965 in Sarasota, Florida, that commissioned its own-name pipe lines from well-known European makers.

yunanistan-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands made in Greece or documented as Greek-made; short, factual entries for four brands.

reiner-thilo-bindschadel.z: A German bench maker who signs his pipes "Reiner Thilo"; working out of his workshop in Kraichtal, he produces a limited number of hand-shaped pipes each year with a Danish influence.

shepherd-brothers.z: A brother-run hand-carving pipe workshop founded by Darren and Greg Shepherd in Elk Creek, in southwestern Virginia, based on a division of labor.

santaroko-pipes.z: A brand producing handmade pipes at a one-man workshop, founded by Taiwanese maker ST Kuo after a long career in IT.

marchetti-pipes.z: The name Philip S. DeFant of Michigan gives to the small run of handmade pipes he makes and to his pipe-restoration service; a bench brand blending American, Italian, and Danish lines.

missouri-meerschaum-fabrika-gezisi.z: A look at the structure, floors, old machinery, and production flow of the Missouri Meerschaum factory in Washington, Missouri.

strambach.z: An Austrian workshop founded in Vienna in 1904, known for meerschaum and calabash pipes; it closed in the mid-2010s after more than a century of production.

tekel-pipo-tutunleri.z: Türk Pipo Tütünü and Yayladağ, produced during Türkiye's state tobacco monopoly, were the country's own domestic pipe tobaccos for many years; after production stopped, they became objects of nostalgia within the pipe community.

peter-stokkebye-pipo-tutun-ve-sigara-ada.b: Peter Stokkebye: Pipe, Tobacco, and Cigarette Man
peter-stokkebye-pipo-tutun-ve-sigara-ada.z: The story of Peter Stokkebye, third-generation representative of a Danish tobacco family founded in Odense in 1882. This entry also covers the blender's unsuccessful venture into the tobacco-free "Free" cigarette in the early 1980s, alongside the pipe blends and shag-cut tobaccos for which he is known.

serova.z: A one-woman pipe workshop founded in 2016 by Ukrainian Irina Serova, known for its poker and tomato bodies.

neerup.z: The brand made by Danish pipe maker Peder Christian Jeppesen at his workshop in Lejre, known for balanced proportions and shank ornamentation.

falcon.z: A pipe brand known for its detachable briar bowls that screw onto an aluminum stem, patented in America in 1936, with production moved entirely to England after the 1960s.

silver-lining-briar.z: The bench Silver Gray runs alone in the Applegate area of southwestern Oregon; the signature of one of the still very few women pipe makers, following a long career in accounting and needlework.

mr-groum.z: The name James H. Margroom, who worked in Hanover, Pennsylvania, gave to the pipes he hand-carved over more than thirty years; known for classic shapes alongside unusual figurative carvings.

sren-eric-andersen.z: A Danish master who has made pipes since 1968 and set up his own workshop in 1975; he follows a persistent line of handcraft in classic shapes.

1960lar-ve-oncesine-tarihlenen-kutu-tutu.b: Tinned Tobacco Dating to the 1960s and Earlier
1960lar-ve-oncesine-tarihlenen-kutu-tutu.z: John C. Loring's compilation of pipe tobacco tins from the 1930s through the late 1960s, organized by maker, tin type, weight, and date; the condition codes on knife-lid tins and the cardboard and glass packaging of the war years stand out.

martelo.z: The one-man pipe workshop Brazilian designer Gustavo Cunha founded in April 2014 upon moving into full-time production, blending Danish and Greek workshop traditions.

dulger-meerschaum.z: A two-generation meerschaum pipe workshop in Eskişehir where father and son work together. Known for figural carvings, it sends most of its production abroad.

tutunun-osmanliya-gelisi.b: Tobacco's Arrival in the Ottoman Empire
tutunun-osmanliya-gelisi.z: The story of tobacco's arrival on Ottoman soil in the early 17th century, Murad IV's harsh bans, and its transformation from a forbidden vice into a source of state revenue.

vanroy.z: An American pipe brand that emerged in New York during World War II, known for its Ajustomatic screw-in mouthpiece connection, which passed to Henry Leonard & Thomas in the 1950s.

canadian-ailesi.z: A pipe family covering the long-shanked derivatives of the Billiard — Canadian, Lumberman, Liverpool, and Lovat — whose members are distinguished by the combination of shank cross-section and stem type.

eski-pipo-ve-tutun-kataloglari.z: The printed trade catalogs of the late 19th century are the most detailed documents that survive of the pipe and tobacco products of their era; the Demuth, Zorn, and Salmon & Gluckstein catalogs are the leading examples of this type of document.

genod.z: The brand name adopted in 1970 by a workshop that has operated continuously in Saint-Claude since 1865; a chain of succession running from the Comoy, Vincent-Genod, and Craen families to Sébastien Beaud.

duncan-briars.z: A British pipe manufacturer founded in Manchester in 1899 that remained under its founding family's management for nearly a century. Known for the Duncan Dental mouthpiece developed for denture wearers and the metal-shafted Delta line.

missouri-meerschaum.z: Missouri Meerschaum is the world's oldest and largest corncob pipe manufacturer, founded by Henry Tibbe in Washington, Missouri, in 1869.

ilk-pipo-secimi.z: A guide to how newcomers can weigh basic criteria — bowl material, shape, bowl size, filters, and new versus secondhand — in choosing their first pipe.

iyi-bir-briyar-pipoyu-ne-belirler-ikinci.b: What Makes a Good Briar Pipe: Part Two, Making
iyi-bir-briyar-pipoyu-ne-belirler-ikinci.z: The second installment of a 1985 Pipe Smoker series: period criteria on hand-turning versus lathe-cutting the stummel, mouthpiece craftsmanship, post-cut curing, and tolerance for flaws.

shekita.z: The path and production philosophy of Konstantin Shekita, one of Ukraine's first-generation pipe makers, from factory work in Kyiv to an independent workshop.

hollywood-briar.z: A small American pipe-making bench founded by David Hopper in southeastern Missouri, following a production line that began with hand tools and became known for sandblasted surfaces.

vladimir-grechukhin.z: A Russian pipe master working in Saint Petersburg since the 1970s, known for renewing classic shapes with measured departures; a founding member of the PS Studio workshop.

irlanda-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands made in Ireland or documented as Irish-made, with short, factual entries for three brands.

jopp.z: German pipemaker Uwe Jopp, working in the Saxon village of Dorfhain, brought his background in civil engineering to pipemaking and is known for his curved smoke channel (Bogenbohrung) technique.

tsutsu.z: A case made to carry the Japanese kiseru pipe; as the most visible part of the smoking kit hung from the sash, it was worked in forms grouped under five names and in a wide range of materials from deer antler to lacquer.

block-pipes-tornasiz-calisan-kisa-omurlu.b: Block Pipes: A Short-Lived American Bench That Worked Without a Lathe
block-pipes-tornasiz-calisan-kisa-omurlu.z: A small-scale pipe workshop that Jonathan Block ran out of his own garage in the United States in the early 2000s, shaping pipes with hand sanding rather than a lathe, and which quietly ended in the summer of 2003.

peterson-mark-twain-ozgun-pipo-ve-yeni-k.b: Peterson Mark Twain: The Original Pipe and the New Collection
peterson-mark-twain-ozgun-pipo-ve-yeni-k.z: Peterson's Mark Twain series was born from measurements taken off the author's worn pipe held at the museum in Hannibal; the story runs from the limited runs of the 1980s to the two-pipe collection of 2010, showing how a single object became a series.

mastro-beraldi.z: An Italian handmade pipe brand produced by Aldo Pierluigi and his family in Rome; a workshop line aimed mainly at the North American market.

pinocchio-pipe.z: Cafe Artin's Yerevan-based pipe sub-brand, known for briar pipes made in Italy alongside hand-sculpted figural tampers.

davidoff.z: A Swiss brand that grew out of a tobacconist's shop opened in Geneva in 1911, made its name in cigars, and has had pipes made to order under its own name since the mid-1970s.

dunhill.z: An English pipe brand that grew out of the shop Alfred Dunhill opened in London in 1907, recognized worldwide by the white dot on its bit and regarded as the pinnacle of the English school.

tsugenin-otesinde-japon-pipo-yapimi.z: For years, the international community associated Japanese pipe making with a single brand. Yet the same country was home to makers working under their own names, such as Smio Satou, Hiroyuki Tokutomi, and Tsutomu Fukashiro.

s-r-pipes.z: An American bench run by a husband-and-wife team in Columbus, Ohio, known both for handmade briar pipes and for their own tobacco shop.

perrin.z: A small French business founded by Roger Perrin, who returned from London's pipe industry to Saint-Claude, spanning metal accessory manufacture to patented filtered pipes, closing around 1975.

lorenzo.z: An Italian pipe manufacturer founded in Gallarate in 1900 as Fratelli Lana, known as Lorenzo after 1969. Regarded as one of the emblematic brands of the 1970s for its thick-walled, matte-finished, brightly colored models.

nrding.z: The Danish brand founded by Erik Nørding in Slangerup in the mid-1960s, known for its freehand pipes. Production ended before February 2026.

charatan-milan-2014-donem-ve-damga-sinif.b: Charatan - Milan 2014: Period and Stamp Classification
charatan-milan-2014-donem-ve-damga-sinif.z: A period scheme compiled in Milan in 2014 for dating Charatan pipes. It divides ownership changes into three eras, and production details into eight periods.

demuth-ve-dunhill-besinci-caddede-kesise.b: Demuth and Dunhill: Two Paths Crossing on Fifth Avenue
demuth-ve-dunhill-besinci-caddede-kesise.z: Was there a genuine rivalry between New York's homegrown giant William Demuth & Company and London's Alfred Dunhill? What the record shows about the ties between them, and the similar fate of two great pipe collections.

a-petersen-pipes.z: A one-person pipe bench run by Andrew R. Petersen in Davenport, Iowa; first known as Quad City Pipes, later carrying the maker's own name.

uhles.z: An American tobacconist and pipe shop operating in Milwaukee since 1939, known for preparing its own blends.

guild-pipes.z: A small-scale American pipe workshop run single-handedly by John Fordham in Melbourne, Florida, registered in 2013.

laughingmoon-pipes.z: The brand of the one-man briar pipe workshop American maker Robert Vacher founded in northeastern California, known for its crescent-moon-and-star stamp.

lemonwood.z: A very rarely used wood in pipe making; known through Sardinian maker Tommaso Spanu's pipes stamped "LIMONE." Noted for its pale yellow color and heat behavior close to briar's.

dantonian-pipe-works.z: A short-lived Danish workshop founded in 1970 by the Knudsen brothers, Sven and Teddy, in Tappernøje, opened to export markets with a 1971 English-language catalogue.

pipo-tutunu-uygulamalari-icin-xml-standa.b: XML Standards for Pipe Tobacco Applications
pipo-tutunu-uygulamalari-icin-xml-standa.z: Three open XML schemas proposed so that pipe collections, cellar records, and smoking notes can be stored independently of any particular application.

dunhill-dead-root.z: The origin of the DR stamp applied to Dunhill's straight-grain pipes, the objections raised against the 'dead root' claim in its name, and the grading system running from letters to stars.

quinton-wells.z: An American maker working in Overland Park who turns out a small number of pipes a year, known for organizing the Kansas City pipe community and for founding a pipe-making competition dedicated to American makers.

le-nuvole.z: An Italian workshop founded by Maurizio Tombari in Pesaro in 1996, named after clouds. Known for its distinctive grading system that counts clouds.

sot-weed-ve-little-ladell-unutulmus-iki-.b: Sot Weed and Little Ladell: Two Forgotten Tobacco Terms
sot-weed-ve-little-ladell-unutulmus-iki-.z: Sot weed was a disparaging name attached to the tobacco plant; little ladell was a description of the implement's shape used before the word "pipe" took hold. Both remain confined to 16th-18th century texts.

sims.z: The signature of a master who worked in London through the 1960s and 1970s, producing Danish-style freehand pipes within the English workshop tradition.

weber-pipe-co.z: An American pipe company founded in New Jersey in 1938 by Bavarian-born Carl B. Weber, producing at scale in the mid-price tier and supplying countless tobacconists with private-label pipes.

awat-handcrafts.z: A small-scale workshop run by Awat Ghasemi, known for hand-shaped pipes. According to the record it is based in Iran and produces 9 mm filter models.

oldenkott-model-ve-sekil-numaralari.z: A reference entry explaining how to read the model (quality) names and shape numbers used on Oldenkott pipes, together with the 1973 catalogue breakdown recorded by collectors.

brog.z: A workshop working in the Polish city of Przemyśl, with roots tracing to a 1947 wooden-accessories business, now considered the country's largest pipe manufacturer.

arlington.z: An American workshop founded in Brooklyn in 1919 that spent nearly sixty years producing pipes mostly as a subcontractor for other brands.

j-alan-pipes.z: The brand of handmade briar pipes American master Jeff Gracik produces single-handedly in his workshop in San Diego; known for stamping every piece with its production sequence number and year, with Wave as its top tier.

pipo-kitaplari-ve-yayinlari.z: A survey of the major books and bibliographies written on the history, brands, and craft of the pipe, mapping a reading trail from the literary essays of the 1890s to today's brand monographs.

macaristan-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in Hungary, containing three short entries based on documented facts.

the-doodler.z: An American pipe model introduced by Tracy Mincer after losing the Custom-Bilt name, designed to cool the smoke through vertical holes drilled around the bowl and connected by horizontal grooves.

gh-zhang.z: A Chinese pipe brand that moves designs licensed from master carvers around the world into series production at its workshop in Zhejiang.

karaca.z: Karaca is the signature used by meerschaum carver Ramazan Karaca, who works in the Eskişehir region; the master is known for animal figures and human portraits covering the entire bowl.

wojtek-pastuch.z: Polish maker Wojtek Pastuch, born in Katowice, makes nature-themed freehands at the workshop he founded in Silesia in 2011; he stamps his pipes with a four-digit code that treats 2011 as its starting point.

gotoh.z: The mark stamped on his pipes by Japanese master Kei-ichi Gotoh. Trained at Tsuge's Ikebana workshop, Gotoh is known for his bamboo shank work and asymmetric bodies that give briar a sense of movement.

chacom.z: Chacom is a well-established pipe brand born of the partnership between the Chapuis and Comoy families, produced in France's Saint-Claude region. It is counted among today's most recognized representatives of the French pipe-making school.

antika-pipo-ve-briyar-koleksiyonculugu-i.b: Antique Pipe and Briar Collecting: Two Separate Cultures
antika-pipo-ve-briyar-koleksiyonculugu-i.z: The split among pipe collectors into two distinct communities, one around antique pieces and the other around briar pipes; the history of this divide and its criteria in terms of material and sources of knowledge.

maurizio-tombari-ile-soylesi-le-nuvoleni.b: A Conversation With Maurizio Tombari: Founder of Le Nuvole
maurizio-tombari-ile-soylesi-le-nuvoleni.z: Bear Graves's interview with Maurizio Tombari, published on Smokingpipes.com, is a frequently cited record for the founding of the Le Nuvole workshop, Stefania Tombari's role in its design, and the Zed series.

en-pahali-pipo-tartismasi.z: A history entry examining, through examples ranging from world's-fair showpieces to one-off jewelled creations, what criteria decide the "most expensive pipe" title that has changed hands for a century and a half.

ikinci-dunya-savasi-yillarinda-dunhill.b: Dunhill During the Second World War (WWII Phase)
ikinci-dunya-savasi-yillarinda-dunhill.z: From the 1941 bombing of the Duke Street shop to the completed repair in 1953, the period in which Dunhill production was squeezed by raw-material shortages and stamps grew sparse.

reiner-pipe-art-design.z: A German pipe brand founded by Bremen designer Reiner Klein in the 1980s, passed to Rüdiger Lutz Will in Bünde in 1988, and split across two distinct periods.

stich.z: A Swiss family workshop founded in 1941 as one of Kleinlützel's three pipe factories, whose work extended from traditional Swiss types to freehand shapes, ending pipe production after a 2008 fire.

romagnolo.z: A one-man Italian workshop founded by Ivan Romagnolo in Piedmont, bringing nearly twenty-five years of experience as a furniture restorer to handmade briar pipes.

pipo-dunyasinin-cevrim-ici-agi-muzeler-f.b: The Online Network of the Pipe World: Museums, Forums, and Clubs
pipo-dunyasinin-cevrim-ici-agi-muzeler-f.z: A map of the pipe community online, built from Pipedia's link directory: museum collections, national forums, blogs, and club sites.

mccoy-pipes.z: American-made pipes signed with his own name by Will McCoy; the only documented record about him dates to 2018, a small one-person bench.

pipas-o-felix-masso-milleironun-galicya-.b: Pipas + O: Félix Massó Milleiro's Galician Workshop
pipas-o-felix-masso-milleironun-galicya-.z: The one-person workshop in Galicia of Félix Massó Milleiro, who took up pipe making after retirement, known for freehand pipes drawing on ideas from film and literature.

gb-pipes.z: A one-man workshop founded in 2005 by Bulgarian craftsman George Boyadjiev, producing mostly freehand briar pipes.

pamplin-virginianin-kil-pipo-kasabasi.z: The story of the Pamplin workshops in Appomattox County, which began as a home industry and grew into a factory around 1879, at one time the largest clay pipe maker in the United States.

pipo-literaturunun-kuresellesmesi.z: The circulation of pipe and tobacco books across languages: nearly a century of translation traffic, multilingual classics, bilingual museum and workshop books, and the uneven direction this traffic takes.

bartoli.z: A briar pipe workshop founded in the Tuscan town of Massa Marittima, run by the same family for three generations.

harcourt.z: A brand whose pipes were carved in Copenhagen at the height of the Danish freehand vogue and sold through British and American distribution networks; most were made at the Preben Holm workshop, with a portion also made by Erik Nørding.

dunhill-482-billiard.z: A large, straight billiard shape from Dunhill dated to the 1930s, known almost exclusively in Shell finish, with very few examples on record.

norse.z: The brand of Vermont maker Steve Norse; his real renown, however, comes from Vermont Freehand, a business that stocks a broad range of pipe-making materials.

penguin-briar.z: A small-scale American workshop run by Kim Kendall in Phoenix, Arizona, making handmade briar pipes.

rccellarworks.z: A small workshop known for the pipe tampers Robert Carmell makes one at a time; each piece is designed differently from the last.

woolsey-boynuz-bilezikli-amerikan-el-yap.b: Woolsey: American Handmade Pipes with a Horn Band
woolsey-boynuz-bilezikli-amerikan-el-yap.z: Woolsey is the stamp a part-time California maker put on his handmade briar pipes. Known for the horn band between bowl and mouthpiece and its individually struck stamps.

trent.z: The American bench of Philip A. Trent, who lived in South Bend, Indiana, and stamped his pipes with his own name; known for wide-drilled, lightweight briar pipes.

roman-kovalev.z: A Russian maker who turned to pipe making after sixteen years as a pediatric neurologist, and who developed his own sandblasting rig at his workshop in Petersburg.

catterall-pipes.z: The brand of briar pipes individually shaped by hand by Van Catterall in Greensboro, North Carolina; known for its special series with teak collars dedicated to the battleship USS North Carolina.

olie-sylvester.z: American maker Olie Sylvester, who moved from a visual-artist identity to the pipe bench, and the Monstrosity Pipes series born in 2008.

wombaroo-pipes.z: A small-scale pipe bench pipemaker Marty Simm set up in Toronto; a 2000s example of handmade production learned through the American seminar tradition.

blakemar-briars.z: A small-scale English workshop making handmade briar pipes in the Northamptonshire countryside since 1890, run within the same family line.

estate-pipo-temizligi-ve-restorasyonu.z: The process followed to bring a secondhand pipe to a smokable condition: disinfection, reaming the bowl, clearing the airway, and removing oxidation from the mouthpiece.

tutunun-yillandirilmasi.z: The practice of storing pipe tobacco in airtight containers for years to let its flavor mature. It gives especially pronounced results with Virginia-heavy blends.

whitehall.z: A pipe brand named after the seat of London's government, used by several unrelated makers; its best-known arm is the Whitehall Pipe Co., marketed by American tobacco companies in the mid-20th century.

pipo-yapiminda-kullanilan-alternatif-aga.b: Alternative Woods Used in Pipe Making
pipo-yapiminda-kullanilan-alternatif-aga.z: The tree species that became pipes when briar was unavailable, why cherry endured, and the place of borderline materials like morta.

juds-pipe-shop.z: An American tobacconist shop that operated in Houston, also offering pipes and blends stamped with its own name; what is known about it rests largely on surviving catalogue pages.

agizlik-yariginin-acilmasi.z: A pipemaking entry on how the flat air slit at the mouthpiece tip is cut, what tools shape it, and its effect on draw.

james-foster.z: An American pipe smoker and certified tobacconist known for his leadership of the Austin Pipe Club, his organization of the Texas Pipe Show, and his online projects for pipe enthusiasts.

papa-bears-pipes-tim-beaumontun-kuzeydog.b: Papa Bear's Pipes: Tim Beaumont's Northeast Ohio Workshop
papa-bears-pipes-tim-beaumontun-kuzeydog.z: Tim Beaumont's Northeast Ohio operation, which turned from a furniture workshop into a pipe bench in 2018; known for sandblasted surfaces and exotic wood shanks.

mcgimpsey-pipes.z: An American workshop brand run single-handedly by Matt Brannon in Tulsa, Oklahoma; known for individually made pipes combining Italian briar with German ebonite.

gutta-percha-ve-redmanol.z: Two materials tried in pipe mouthpieces from the 19th century to the mid-20th: the natural thermoplastic gutta-percha, drawn from Southeast Asian trees, and Redmanol, a synthetic resin developed by a company founded in Chicago in 1913.

fugitive-slaves-pipe-bir-muzayede-kaydin.b: The Fugitive Slaves Pipe: Anatomy of an Auction Record
fugitive-slaves-pipe-bir-muzayede-kaydin.z: A meerschaum pipe signed F. J. Kaldenberg, carved with a scene of fugitive slaves. Known for its February 2016 auction sale, the differences between the catalog description of this piece and its present-day museum record show how auction texts need to be read.

hackert.z: A handmade pipe workshop run by Jake Hackert in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, known for briar as well as deer antler and corn cob bodies.

merchant-service-bing-crosbynin-ince-sap.b: Merchant Service: Bing Crosby's Slender-Stemmed Billiard
merchant-service-bing-crosbynin-ince-sap.z: A British brand founded in London by Herbert Merchant, known for its long, slim-shanked billiard associated with Bing Crosby's name, and its second life revived in America in the 21st century.

johns-pipe-shop.z: A tobacconist that opened in Los Angeles in 1908, had its pipes made at European factories under its own name without a workshop of its own, and stayed in business until the 1980s.

gigliucci-pipe.z: An Italian workshop run single-handedly by Andrea Gigliucci in Tuscany's Maremma region, producing a limited number of handmade pipes.

mortadan-pipo-yapimi.z: How semi-fossilized bog oak becomes a pipe: hand extraction in autumn, years of drying, high wastage, and a finish that won't take stain.

tom-dunn.z: The American publisher who founded The Pipe Smoker's Ephemeris magazine and The Universal Coterie of Pipe Smokers, linking the world's pipe community by mail for forty years.

turner-pipes-denverda-bir-bodrum-atolyes.b: Turner Pipes: A Basement Workshop in Denver
turner-pipes-denverda-bir-bodrum-atolyes.z: Simeon Turner's one-person briar pipe bench in Denver, Colorado; known for small bowls and stems entirely hand-cut from vulcanite rod.

selmec-pipolari.z: A tradition of brightly glazed clay pipes descended from the Ottoman chibouk, produced in the mining town of Selmecbánya, now in Slovakia.

j-rinaldi-pipes.z: A one-man American pipe workshop run by Arizona-based photographer Jon Rinaldi, self-taught. Production has ended.

seniak.z: A one-man briar pipe workshop run by Ukrainian-born Zinovi Seniak near Moscow; a limited-output craft operation that sources material from several countries.

anton-co-pipes.z: A Ukrainian workshop run by the father-and-son Antonenko team in Lviv, making pipes mainly from maple. It began working imported briar as well after 2020.

libre-real-briar.z: A Lebanese pipe manufactory founded in Beirut, using an internal steel filter in all of its products and selling mainly into the Middle East market.

howell.z: An American handmade pipe workshop built on classic shapes and sandblasting, run part time since 1999 by Jack Howell, bass clarinetist of the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra.

sven-knudsen.z: One of the first-generation masters of Denmark's freehand tradition. He trained at Suhr's, headed W. Ø. Larsen's pipe workshop, and founded Dantonian PipeWorks with his brother Teddy.

steve-morrisette-pipes.z: The brand of handmade briar pipes American maker Steve Morrisette produces at his one-man workshop. A signature that grew out of collecting, shaped through work with American masters of his generation, and known for its small-scale, Danish-inspired work.

purdy.z: The bench of American pipe maker Will Purdy, who works in Colorado, taught himself the craft, and turns out a small number of pipes each year.

pipo-tutunu-tadimi-daha-disiplinli-olmal.b: Tasting Pipe Tobaccos: Should We Become More Disciplined About This?
pipo-tutunu-tadimi-daha-disiplinli-olmal.z: Fred J. Hanna's essay comparing pipe tobacco tasting to the method of wine tasting; grouping the variables that determine taste under the headings of tobacco, pipe, and smoker.

jens-steuler.z: One of the last workshops in Germany still carrying on the clay pipe tradition, working the 'pipe baking' craft in the town of Hilgert in the Westerwald region.

netsuke.b: Netsuke (the Toggle of the Japanese Personal Smoking Set)
netsuke.z: The small Japanese toggle that held a tobacco pouch and pipe case in place, hanging from the sash; a simple utility item that turned into a branch of miniature sculpture in the Edo period, with special varieties developed for lighting fire and carrying embers.

abd-pipo-markalari-dizini-3.z: The third part of the alphabetical directory of pipe brands, workshops, and makers in the United States: 86 entries from Norwalk Pipe Co. to Zeus.

pipo-anatomisi.z: An entry introducing all the parts of a pipe, from bowl to mouthpiece, along with their Turkish and international names — the basic terminology.

gesualdi.z: The brand of handmade Italian pipes Antonio Gesualdi, who comes from a background in bonsai and sculpture, has produced alone in his workshop in Cava de' Tirreni since 2017.

savinelli.z: A pipe house founded in Milan in 1876. Known for its balsa filter system and Italian design elegance, this established brand is run today by the family's fourth generation.

pipo-kuluplerinin-tarihi.z: A short history of how pipe clubs grew out of English coffeehouses and the tobacco rooms of gentlemen's clubs to become chartered, independent communities in the 20th century.

ewa-pipe.z: The final name of a family business in Saint-Claude that ran across four generations of the Waille workshop, founded in 1860; a French brand known for its horn, acrylic, and Cumberland mouthpieces.

buyuk-britanya-pipo-markalari-dizini-2.z: A short introduction to 29 recorded brands in the British pipe industry between Paget & Paget and York House. This part gathers names whose records are too thin for a standalone entry.

bellezia.z: A tobacco shop Milton Kalnitz opened near Buffalo in the 1970s, and the name of the limited number of briar pipes he hand-carved under the same roof.

dr-grabow-kronolojisi-linkmandan-spartay.b: Dr. Grabow Chronology: From Linkman to Sparta
dr-grabow-kronolojisi-linkmandan-spartay.z: The chain of events used as the basis for dating Dr. Grabow pipes: from M. Linkman & Co., founded in Chicago in 1892, through the move to North Carolina in 1943, to the last change of ownership in 2006.

maigurs-knets.z: The workshop of a maker born in Latvia who has lived in the US since 1990 and moved into full-time pipemaking in 2010; known for sculptural, Art Nouveau-inspired shapes.

ingiliz-harmani.z: A classic blend family built from Latakia, oriental tobaccos, and Virginia, prepared without added artificial flavoring. Its smoky, layered character makes it one of the most established categories in the pipe world.

brebbia.z: An Italian pipe manufactory founded by Enea Buzzi in the Lombardy town of Brebbia, which split off from its partnership with Savinelli to continue under its own name.

christie-pipes.z: An American handmade pipe brand made piece by piece by Eric Christie in the town of Waynesboro, Pennsylvania; also known as a well-established repair workshop.

belcika-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in or connected to Belgium; contains short, factual entries for eight brands.

dejarnett-pipes.z: DeJarnett Pipes is the name of the American briar pipes Horace DeJarnett made one at a time by hand at his workshop in Glendale, Arizona, from the late 1990s until his death in 2013. A widely opened smoke channel and a pre-applied carbon coating on the bowl are the brand's known features.

tsutomu.z: The stamp of Tokyo-based master Fukashiro Tsutomu. Known for shapes close to the Danish line, the brand has an unusually high annual output for Japanese handmade pipes.

cavicchi.z: Founded on a farm near Bologna by Claudio Cavicchi in 1974, this Italian workshop is known for its meticulous grain selection, its C-to-CCCCC grading scale, and its record-setting finishes in slow-smoking competitions.

eyland.z: A small family business founded in 1963 by the couple Ernst and Elisabeth Lanius in the town of Rees on the Lower Rhine; it produced carefully finished briar models for seven years before ending in a fire in early 1970.

gawith-hoggarth-co.z: A traditional pipe tobacco and snuff maker founded in 1887 in the English town of Kendal, with roots reaching back to 1792. Known for its rope (twist) tobaccos, Kendal Kentucky blends, and Lakeland-scented products.

ardor.z: A handmade briar pipe workshop in Gavirate, northern Italy, named after its founders Angelo and Dorelio Rovera. The family's pipe-making tradition dates back to 1911; known for quality grades named after celestial bodies and its scaled Meteora rustication.

edwin-pipes.z: The brand of Kris Edwin Barber, working in northeastern Minnesota, known for churchwarden-length freehand pipes, dragon-themed shapes, and custom-made display stands.

kaywoodie.z: American pipe brand rooted in the Kaufmann Bros. & Bondy firm founded in New York in 1851; known for its screw-in Drinkless stem and clover-leaf emblem.

kumlama-sanati-makine-asindirici-ve-usta.b: The Art of Sandblasting: Machine, Abrasive, and the Maker's Hand
kumlama-sanati-makine-asindirici-ve-usta.z: Sandblasting is a surface finish that migrated from industry into pipe making. Machine setup, abrasive type, the wood's structure, and curing combine to shape the result.

soborg.z: A secondary stamp used at the workshop of Søren Refbjerg Rasmussen in Søborg; known for plateau-top, short-shanked pipes mostly finished by employees.

edebiyatta-lule-tasi-siirin-ve-nesrin-go.b: Meerschaum in Literature: A Favorite of Poetry and Prose
edebiyatta-lule-tasi-siirin-ve-nesrin-go.z: In the 19th century, meerschaum was not just a bowl material but the subject of guidebooks, poems, stories, and still-life paintings. This article surveys the printed texts devoted to the material and the reasons behind this interest.

artebano.z: A handmade pipe workshop in Bologna's historic center that continued through several changes of hands, its products staying almost entirely within its own city.

zehnder-pipes.z: An American handmade pipe brand founded by Yosef S. Zehnder in 2019 and run out of a one-person workshop in the American Midwest.

briyar.z: A wood, extraordinarily heat-resistant, obtained from the root burl of a Mediterranean tree heath. It has been the standard material of pipe making since the 19th century.

vincent.z: The workshop and craftsmanship of Roger Vincent, who carved portraits and figures in Saint-Claude and is regarded as France's last pipe sculptor.

arne-ljung.z: A short portrait of Swedish master Arne Ljung, who took up pipe making after turning fifty and whose output went largely abroad.

franz-pipes.z: The brand of Italian maker Roberto Franzini, produced since 2012 in a garage workshop in Saronno. Known for the work of an Italian-trained maker whose style leans close to the Danish idiom.

turkiyenin-tutun-bolgeleri.z: With the heritage of İzmir, Samsun-Bafra, and Rumelia, Türkiye's Oriental tobacco-growing regions have fed the world's pipe blends with their "Turkish" component for centuries.

duke-street-damgali-drler-dunhillin-ilk-.b: Duke Street–Stamped DRs: Grading in Dunhill's First Decade
duke-street-damgali-drler-dunhillin-ilk-.z: How straight-grain DR pipes were stamped, how grades were marked, and what became of flawed bodies during Dunhill's 1910–1918 Duke Street stamp era.

endonezya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands from Indonesia, currently containing a short, factual entry for the single brand on record.

calabria-pipe.z: An Italian workshop run by the Carlino family in the town of Mandatoriccio in Calabria, spanning production from briar blanks to finished pipes.

tajima.z: Tokyo-based Tatsuo Tajima's workshop, begun as a second career in the mid-2000s and kept to about sixty pipes a year, stamped Tatu Pipe.

brigham-pipes.z: A family company founded in Toronto in 1906, known for its maple filter system and long regarded as Canada's largest pipe manufacturer.

hamric.z: Danish-influenced freehands from American maker Zack Hamric, who learned pipe carving as a young carpenter and returned to the bench after a thirty-year gap.

eskisehir-lule-tasi-oymaciligi.z: The craft tradition that turns block meerschaum into pipes and figural works in Eskişehir; the story of the craft from its first workshops through the raw-stone export ban to successive generations of masters and geographic-indication registration.
