von-erck.z: An American handmade pipe brand made by Lee von Erck at his one-man workshop in Michigan's Upper Peninsula; known for an undisclosed oil-curing method, large-chambered organic shapes, and a detailed stamping system.

pipesmd-pipes.z: A small-scale American pipe signature produced by Charles "Charlie" Sharp at his workshop in New Mexico, drawing on a background in tool-and-die work.

waughtel.z: A small-scale signature carried by Robert Waughtel, who began making pipes in the late 1980s in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. Considered the last link in a family tobacconist tradition.

davorin.z: A workshop carrying the signature of Croatian pipe maker Davorin Denović, known for pipes made from bog oak, that is, morta, left in a swamp for thousands of years, and for a stamp drawn from the Glagolitic alphabet.

bbj-piber.z: A one-person workshop founded in 1996 by Danish maker Børge Blume-Jensen in southern Sjælland. A small-scale signature brand producing a few dozen pipes a year, working classic shapes with a jeweler's discipline.

kil-pipolarin-kisa-tarihi.b: A Short History of Clay Pipes
kil-pipolarin-kisa-tarihi.z: The three-century arc of the clay pipe, from its birth in late-16th-century England to its 20th-century decline: bans, taxes, production peaks, and the fashion for ornate pipes.

jeantet.z: One of Saint-Claude's oldest pipe dynasties, Jeantet grew from a workshop turning cherry-wood shanks into a briar factory and joined Cuty Fort in 1988.

moretti.z: A handmade pipe workshop founded in 1968 by Igino Moretti in Recanati, Italy, today carried on by the founder's son-in-law Marco Biagini and Biagini's son Luca. Known for working olive wood and bog oak alongside briar.

dunhill-tutun-harmanlari.z: A historic tobacco line born from the shop Alfred Dunhill opened in London in 1907; identified with classics such as My Mixture 965, Nightcap, and Early Morning Pipe. Production under the Dunhill name ended in 2018, and the blends have continued under the Peterson label since 2019.

bulldog-ve-rhodesian.z: A pair of classic pipe shapes recognizable at first glance, with a body resembling two cones set base to base and a beadline; a diamond-section shank is generally taken as Bulldog, a round one as Rhodesian.

sanatta-ve-edebiyatta-pipo.b: The Pipe in Art and Literature
sanatta-ve-edebiyatta-pipo.z: From Dutch tavern scenes to Magritte's famous canvas, from Sherlock Holmes to Middle-earth: a brief map of what the pipe has meant in painting and literature.

sydney-p-ram.z: An American tobacconist and pipemaker who worked in Chicago in the 1930s and early 1940s, and also wrote a handbook on pipe smoking.

damiano-rovera-ile-soylesi-ardor-atolyes.b: A Conversation with Damiano Rovera: A Voice from the Ardor Workshop
damiano-rovera-ile-soylesi-ardor-atolyes.z: A written interview conducted by email with Damiano Rovera, fourth-generation maker at the Italian brand Ardor, entered into the archive in 2007, along with the history of the family workshop behind it.

professor-stanwell-briar.z: A short-story writer and publisher known by a pen name within the pipe community; author of the Black Hart stories that grew out of the Agricultural and Mechanical Gazette, a private newspaper he began publishing in 1988.

roland-briars.z: The brand of the one-man workshop that German pipe maker Roland Schwarz founded in the early 2000s. His pipes carry the ROLAND HANDMADE stamp and are known for their technical craftsmanship.

zimparalama.z: The stage after rough shaping in pipe making, where the body and mouthpiece are smoothed with progressively finer sandpaper grits; it takes up the largest share of workshop time.

johny-pipes.z: A handmade pipe workshop founded by Meysam Jahani in Babol, Iran, known for its calabash and reverse-calabash chamber arrangements.

co-pipes.z: A German workshop in Westphalia run jointly by Kelvin Pohler and Thorsten Klemme since 2015, producing freeform pipes in the Danish line.

japonya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: A collective directory of makers and brands that have produced pipes in Japan, giving a short, factual introduction for each.

bueschers.z: An American workshop in Washington, Missouri, that made corncob and hardwood pipes for half a century and sold its products under the "World Famous Pipe" stamp.

yeni-pipoyu-alistirma.z: Breaking in a new pipe means building up a protective layer of cake in the bowl in a controlled way. This guide covers the debate over gradual filling, pre-carbonized bowls, and the differences by material.

curtz-salt-lake-cityde-tamirci-tezgahind.b: Curtz: A Brand Born at a Repair Bench in Salt Lake City
curtz-salt-lake-cityde-tamirci-tezgahind.z: The one-man Utah workshop of Arley G. Curtz, who turned to pipe making after retiring from arts administration; a bench that grew from repair work into around seventy handmade briar pipes a year.

e-andrew-briars.z: A small-scale American pipe workshop born at a machinist's bench in Milwaukee. Its lineage of craft reaches back two generations to Achille Savinelli.

phil-rivara.z: The workshop and work of American independent pipe maker Phil Rivara, who moved to the bench after the Navy and is known for his long-stemmed classic shapes.

meissen-porcelain.z: The Saxon manufactory that produced Europe's first hard-paste porcelain; in its early years it also made pipe bowls from Böttger stoneware, placing it at the very start of the porcelain pipe tradition.

hynick.z: The workshop of American maker Tim Hynick, working in the greater Boston area, known for Danish-influenced freehand pipes and a distinctive rusticated surface finish.

innerschwyzer-pfeifen.z: A family workshop carrying on the traditional plaster Yps pipe of the Muota valley in central Switzerland; production, interrupted in the 1990s, was later revived by Andreas Heinzer.

pipo-koleksiyonculugu-merak-mi-meslek-mi.z: The path from hobby to expertise in pipe collecting: the criterion that separates a collection from a mere pile, history's great collectors, and the fact that this pursuit still lacks a settled name of its own.

learned.z: Sam Learned, a patent attorney who practiced in York, Pennsylvania, took up pipe making at fifty-nine and became known for his horn shapes and his Hunter pipes crowned with deer antler.

metal-torna.z: The place in the pipe workshop of the lathe on which the cutting tool runs on a slide-mounted carriage rather than by hand: how it differs from a wood lathe, its size range, and the jobs it handles from turning the mortise to drilling the bowl.

britanya-pipoculugu.z: The history of British pipemaking, running from clay-pipe guilds to the briar workshops of London, and on to the mergers under the Cadogan umbrella.

pipes-jas.z: A handmade pipe brand in which Juan Antonio Salhus produces pipes single-handedly in Curicó, Chile, from the native espino wood.

barling.z: An English pipe house born in 1812 when a London silversmith began fitting mounts onto meerschaum bowls. Counted among the most closely studied brands in collecting for its aged Algerian briar and its family-era stamps.

ailarov.z: The pipes of Sergey Ailarov, born in Vladikavkaz and working in Moscow, bringing a sense of form shaped by a background in music and photography to Russia's young pipe craft.

salim-sener.z: A meerschaum pipe carver raised in the Eskişehir region. He entered the craft in 1970 working at a quarry, and records show he has carved his flower ornaments since 1985 and his reverse-claw arrangement since 1989.

cornell-diehl.z: An American pipe tobacco blender known for small-batch production and hands-on methods. Founded in the early 1990s by Craig and Patty Tarler, it has operated under Laudisi Enterprises since 2014.

lorenzetti.z: A workshop founded by Otello Lorenzetti in 1934 in the Italian town of Recanati with a few rented lathes, which grew across later generations into a family business producing tens of thousands of pipes a year and exporting to many countries. Records indicate production has since ended.

pipo-malzemeleri-ve-yapisi.z: An overarching entry that treats the two variables shaping a pipe's look and smoking behavior — bowl material and body construction — together, ranging from natural materials to metal and synthetic experiments.

faders.z: An American tobacconist chain founded in Baltimore in 1891, kept in the same family for nearly four generations, and known for having its eponymous pipe lines made to order by other makers.

sms.z: SMS is a family company that brings meerschaum pipes carved in Eskişehir to the United States; founded in 1980 by Şamil and Beth Sermet, it also handles US distribution for the Italian brand Lorenzo's briar pipes.

novak.z: The workshop of Czech pipe maker Michal Novák in Prague; a small-scale operation, launched after a path that began in journalism, known for its sharp facets and unstained briar.

italyan-pipoculugunun-iki-okulu-pesaro-v.b: Two Schools of Italian Pipe Making: Pesaro and Como
italyan-pipoculugunun-iki-okulu-pesaro-v.z: Italian briar pipe making matured in the second half of the 20th century in two distinct locales: Pesaro on the Adriatic coast, and the Como–Varese line north of Milan. This entry summarizes the founding stories of both schools and the points where they diverge.

g-l-pease.z: An American boutique pipe tobacco brand founded by Gregory L. Pease in California in 2000, aiming to bring the classic English blending tradition to the contemporary pipe smoker.

celius.z: A Danish pipe workshop founded by Svend Axel Celius on the island of Bogø in 1963. Known for its Chess series, graded after chess pieces, its life spanned several interrupted periods.

graces-guide-britanya-sanayi-arsivinde-p.b: Grace's Guide: Pipe and Tobacco Records in the British Industrial Archive
graces-guide-britanya-sanayi-arsivinde-p.z: The structure of Grace's Guide, an online archive that collects Britain's industrial history through company, product, and personal records, and what it offers tobacco and pipe researchers along with the limits of its scope.

red-hat-pipes.z: A Roskilde workshop founded by Kjeld Sørensen of Denmark in 2003 after he moved from economics to the pipe lathe; it produces around one hundred pipes a year.

oppenheimer-pipe.z: The history of the Oppenheimer group, founded in London in 1860 as an import-export house, which brought together the bulk of the British pipe industry under one roof in the first half of the twentieth century.

askwith-pipes.z: A contemporary English pipe brand run by Chris Askwith, a silversmith by training, from his workshop in Plymouth, freely reinterpreting classic English shapes and using bog oak nearly as often as briar.

ian-fisher.z: An American maker working out of New York who turned to handmade pipe making after many years as a foreign and war correspondent.

trever-talbertin-tasarim-yaklasimi.z: American maker Trever Talbert's view of pipe design: a flexible method that selects from an accumulated sketchbook on the block itself, rather than following rigid pre-drawn plans.

poker-ve-cherrywood.z: Two related shapes with a flat-bottomed bowl that lets them stand on a table unaided: the upright-shanked Poker and its curved-shank counterpart, the Cherrywood.

arnavutluk-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands recorded as originating in Albania, containing a short, factual entry for a single brand name.

heiner-nonnenbroich.z: A German pipemaker working in the Lower Rhine region whose actual profession was piano teaching; through the 2000s he produced small numbers of hand-shaped freehand pipes.

old-pal.z: A French pipe brand stamped on the shank with a bird figure with wings spread; the maker cannot be firmly established, though it is linked to Marechal, Ruchon & Cie., the owner of GBD.

icilemeyen-pipolar-cam-ve-pratt-ware.b: Pipes That Won't Smoke: Glass and Pratt Ware
icilemeyen-pipolar-cam-ve-pratt-ware.z: Covers two groups of English-made objects shaped like pipes but never meant to be smoked — glass pipes and Pratt Ware puzzle pipes — along with their production methods and museum examples.

aldo-velani.z: A brand designed for the American market, with pipes made at the Barontini workshop in Livorno, whose name rests not on a real maker but on an invented Italian identity.

alden-pipes.z: An American workshop run solo by Ryan Alden of Texas, known mainly for classic shapes finished with sandblasted surfaces.

trever-talbertin-yuzey-bitirme-yontemi.z: An overview of the sanding, layered staining, carnauba buffing, and stamping sequence American pipemaker Trever Talbert applies in his own workshop.

biltor.z: An early filtered-pipe brand based in London, resting on Swiss maker Emil Alexander Wüterich's 1889 absorbent-tube patent; according to company records, Biltor Ltd was dissolved in 1934.

dr-grabow-pipolarinda-kullanilan-briyar.b: The Briar Used in Dr. Grabow Pipes
dr-grabow-pipolarinda-kullanilan-briyar.z: How briar blocks are sorted at the Dr. Grabow factory in Sparta by flaw count and grain criteria, and which grade is routed to which model line and finish.

steinhart.z: Vic Steinhart is a maker who trained at the JHW workshop in New Jersey and produced first as SK Pipes and then as Briar Originals (BOI); his short-lived workshop is linked to the founding circle of American handmade pipe making.

pipolu-bastonlar.z: Walking sticks with a pipe bowl, mouthpiece, tobacco, snuff, or matches hidden in their shaft or handle. A forgotten accessory of 19th-century Europe, today a subject of collecting.

sparta-industries.z: A pipe factory operating since 1943 in the town of Sparta, North Carolina; it brings the manufacture of many American brands, foremost among them Dr. Grabow, together under one roof.

cek-cumhuriyeti-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in the Czech Republic, containing brief profiles for eleven recorded workshops and makers.

eells.z: John H. Eells, who worked in Richmond, Virginia, is known for handmade pipes that interpret classic English shapes on an above-average scale, and for the American makers he mentored.

briyar-blogu-tedariki.z: The ebauchon and plateaux forms of briar blocks used in pipe making, and how much the channels through which blocks reach the workshop reveal about the wood's history.

italya-pipo-markalari-dizini-1.z: The first part of the alphabetical directory of Italian pipe brands: ninety-one short, factual entries for brands, workshops, and house labels, from AAA to Roverart.

briyar-pipo-ustalarinin-kuresel-yayilisi.b: The Global Spread of Briar Pipe Makers
briyar-pipo-ustalarinin-kuresel-yayilisi.z: A briar pipe made entirely by a single maker was, half a century ago, confined to a handful of European towns. According to a count compiled in 2025, briar pipe makers now work in sixty-two countries.

lakeland-tarzi.z: A pipe tobacco tradition carried on for two centuries in the town of Kendal in northwestern England, top-flavored with floral, soap-like essences.

j-b-b.z: A stamp seen on the pipes of Joseph B. Brown's tobacconist-goods business, run in Kingston upon Hull from the 1870s to the 1920s.

j-m-boswell.z: An American family workshop founded in 1980 in the town of Chambersburg, Pennsylvania, making handmade briar pipes for two generations now.

richard-dunhillin-ardindan.z: Richard Dunhill, grandson of founder Alfred Dunhill, was among the last family members to serve for decades in the company's management. With his death in 2016, the family's direct link to the brand that bears its name also came to an end.

lanatra.z: An Italian handmade pipe workshop that has worked in Pesaro since 1998, known for the silver duck's head on its mouthpiece and its neoclassical shapes that answer to no fixed mold.

tiffany-company-bir-gumus-evinin-tutun-e.b: Tiffany & Company: A Silver House's Tobacco Accessories
tiffany-company-bir-gumus-evinin-tutun-e.z: New York's jewelry and silver house Tiffany & Company sold, for many years, cases, lighters, amber mouthpieces, and even a handful of pipes under the heading of what it called "fancy goods." Trademark records and collection catalogs make it possible to trace this small line.

dunhill-large-billiard-variations.b: Dunhill Large Billiard Variations (LB and 835 Variants)
dunhill-large-billiard-variations.z: The slender-shanked variations that Dunhill's two large billiard shapes, LB and ODA 835, showed over the years, along with collector observations on the stampings of these variants.

heather-coleman.z: The workshop of English craftswoman and collector Heather Coleman, working in Exeter, who makes mold-cast reproductions of historic clay pipes at Dawnmist Studio.

gloredo.z: A China-based handmade briar pipe brand founded by Leslie Ng and his partners, known for the unusually long shanks it favors as a nod to the kiseru tradition. Its corporate entity was registered in Hong Kong in 2007 and struck from the register in 2012.

malaga-pipe-company.z: An American family workshop founded in 1939 in Royal Oak, Michigan, that made pipes from Algerian briar in the same shop for sixty years.

hilson.z: A factory pipe brand born in the town of Bree, Belgium, taking its name from the Hillen family surname, and continued in the Netherlands under the Gubbels umbrella since 1980.

j-mouton-pipes.z: An American maker Jason Mouton's handmade briar pipe workshop in Gueydan, Louisiana; known for a craft background rooted in carpentry and duck-call turning, exotic material accents, and the Chantilly stamp marking its top tier.

portland-pipe-co.z: A British workshop active in London's Camden district, which sold pipes under dozens of sub-brand names and closed in the early 1960s. Its relationship with Barling is still debated.

bacigalupi.z: Bacigalupi is an Italian handmade pipe brand produced in limited numbers by Genoa-born Marco Bacigalupi at his one-man workshop in Gavi.

wagner-pipes.z: The one-man workshop Swiss maker Michael Wagner founded in 2002, known for Spanish briar, tagua shank fittings, and a filter-free approach to pipe-making.

varsayimsal-bir-ikinci-dunya-savasi-pipo.b: A Hypothetical World War II Pipe
varsayimsal-bir-ikinci-dunya-savasi-pipo.z: The dating puzzle that arises when an uncoded Dunhill Shell stamp specific to the war years appears on the same pipe alongside a later-struck year code.

axel-glasner.z: German pipemaker Axel Glasner, born in Trier, combined a self-taught craft with the shape language of the Danish school to develop a pipe known for its geometric precision.

sparkys-pipes-el-aletleriyle-oyulan-amer.b: Sparky's Pipes: American Pipes Carved with Hand Tools
sparkys-pipes-el-aletleriyle-oyulan-amer.z: The one-man American bench of Scott "Sparky" Harris, known for pipes whose surfaces are carved from end to end with hand tools such as knives, chisels, and files.

brigham-pipolarinda-nokta-damga-ve-tarih.b: Dots, Stamps, and Dating in Brigham Pipes
brigham-pipolarinda-nokta-damga-ve-tarih.z: Pipes from the Canadian brand Brigham carry no production year; dating instead relies on the shape of the shank stamp, the three-digit shape number, and the arrangement of the brass dots on the mouthpiece.

briarworks.z: An American pipe manufacturer founded by Todd Johnson and Pete Prevost in Tennessee in 2013, combining machine-worked bowls with hand finishing to blend mass production with workshop craftsmanship.

mr-andersen.z: A house brand released by Copenhagen pipe seller Remo Sørensen, resting not on a single workshop but on several Danish masters.

hava-akisi-piponun-duman-kanali-tartisma.b: Airflow: The Pipe's Smoke Channel Debate
hava-akisi-piponun-duman-kanali-tartisma.z: The cross-section of the channel running from the chamber to the tip of the mouthpiece in a pipe has been one of the community's most contentious technical topics since the late 1990s. The case for an open channel and the objections to it are compared here.

henry-tibbe.z: A Dutch wood turner who transformed the corncob into a durable pipe material in Washington, Missouri, and founder of Missouri Meerschaum.

stanwell-sekil-numaralari-ve-tasarimcila.z: Explains how the shape numbers stamped on the shanks of Stanwell pipes work, which Danish designer each number is linked to, and why numbers were reused for different shapes over the years.

bennie-joe-pipes-cakartadan-el-aletleriy.b: Bennie Joe Pipes: Handmade Pipes from Jakarta with Hand Tools
bennie-joe-pipes-cakartadan-el-aletleriy.z: The Jakarta workshop of Prasetya Tri Wibowo, who moved from architecture to pipe making; known for soft-lined shapes built without a lathe, using files and sandpaper instead.

estonya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating from Estonia; contains a short, factual entry for the single independent maker on record.

domenico-grenci.z: The workshop and briar philosophy of Italian maker Domenico Grenci, known for his hand-shaped smooth-surface pipes made in the village of Brognaturo in Calabria.

corsellini.z: An Italian pipe workshop founded in Florence in 1880 and kept in the same family for three generations; its third-generation representative, Alessandro Corsellini, is also a well-known name in slow pipe-smoking contests.

uwe-maier.z: German master Uwe Maier, who shaped every pipe from a block of wood without ready-made blanks, running his one-man workshop alongside his day job.

seles-pipes.z: A one-man workshop in Ontario run by Canadian Stefan Seles, who trained at the Brigham factory; the work centers mainly on briar pipe repair.

dunhill-patent-damgalari-ve-tarihlendirm.z: A method for narrowing a Dunhill pipe's production year using the patent numbers struck on the shank, the shape of the brand stamp, and the year code introduced in the early 1920s.

pedro-ferrizzo.z: A carver working in Uruguay who shapes coronilla roots gathered from riverbanks into sculptural pipes entirely by hand, using no machinery. Published biographical information about him is very limited.

hartmann.z: A workshop founded self-taught in the 1950s by Danish maker Hans Hartmann; it became known in the 1960s through Copenhagen's Pibe-Dan, and production grew sparse after the master moved into representation work in 1970.

bbb.z: A brand born under Adolph Frankau & Co in London, known for its three-letter stamp set inside a diamond, and counted among the oldest names in English pipe making.

matzhold.z: A pipe brand from Austrian master Peter Matzhold's one-man workshop in Styria, known for unfilled briar and hand-cut ebonite mouthpieces.

walther.z: A one-man handmade briar pipe workshop in the USA, run by Bill Walther, which became full-time after his retirement and is known for finishing each part in sequence.

monterey.z: An American pipe series made from California manzanita root during the Second World War by Kaufmann Bros. & Bondy, known as "Mission Briar."

lule-tasi.z: A white, porous stone native to Eskişehir soil, made of the mineral sepiolite. It's the jewel of pipe craft for its cool smoke, workability, and the golden patina it develops over time.

fassi.z: Coming from a career in dentistry, Italian maker Angelo Fassi's one-man workshop in Appiano Gentile. Known for hybrid interpretations of classic shapes and a preference for deep sandblasting.

don-carlos.z: The Italian workshop Bruto and Rosaria Sordini founded in Cagli in 1990, grading their handmade pipes with musical-note stamps.

filipinler-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands from the Philippines, currently containing a short, factual entry for the single brand on record.

trypis-pipes.z: The Canadian workshop of Greek-born master Phillip Trypis, founded in Ontario, whose path led from running production at the Brigham factory to his own handmade brand.

negoita.z: The one-man workshop of Transylvanian-born designer Rolando Negoita, founded in New York; known for its walnut-shell-like rustication and freehand shapes combined with metalwork.

african-blackwood.z: Dalbergia melanoxylon, growing in the arid savannas of East and Central Africa, is considered one of the densest woods in the world; used in pipe making for mouthpieces, shank extensions, and decorative bands.

shigeyoshi-yanagihara.z: Tokyo-based Japanese pipe master Shigeyoshi Yanagihara produced handmade pipes over a career spanning, according to records, 1975 to 2005, blending Danish formal language with Japanese proportion.

pipoya-islenen-portreler-liderler-unlule.b: Portraits Carved onto Pipes: Leaders, Celebrities, and Legends
pipoya-islenen-portreler-liderler-unlule.z: The commemorative pipe tradition, in which clay, meerschaum, wood, and porcelain masters carried the faces of rulers, politicians, artists, and folk-tale heroes onto the bowl.

b-o-b.z: A small British workshop founded by Bob Hinton, its pipes hand-shaped in Wales; its name comes not from its founder but from the reader community called the "Brotherhood of the Briar."

wilke.z: An American firm founded in New York in 1872 that for years made pipes and blended tobacco out of its Madison Avenue shop and today survives only as a tobacco brand.

crable-hawaiide-kendi-kendine-ogrenen-bi.b: Crable: A Self-Taught Pipe Maker in Hawaii
crable-hawaiide-kendi-kendine-ogrenen-bi.z: The small-scale pipe bench Joseph M. Crable set up on Hawaii's Big Island, learning from books; it became known in the early 2000s and was later paused for a time.

harem-pipe-masaya-konan-bir-amerikan-ici.b: Harem Pipe: An American Tabletop Smoking Apparatus
harem-pipe-masaya-konan-bir-amerikan-ici.z: The Harem Pipe is a tabletop smoking apparatus that appeared on the US market in the mid-20th century, joining a metal ashtray base to a braided flexible hose. The patent it rests on was registered in 1937.

holmgaard.z: The short story of Jens Holmgaard, a Danish amateur maker who learned pipe making as Sixten Ivarsson's neighbor and friend, and who never sold or stamped a single pipe he made.

wolfgang-becker.z: A self-taught German pipe maker based in Duisburg who produces fewer than eighty pipes a year and is known for his signature 'Wespe' shape.

tine-balleby.z: A contemporary Danish artisan, daughter of Danish master Kurt Balleby, who began making pipes in her father's workshop in 2021.

briyar-kalabas-sekilleri-ust-hazne-ve-go.b: Briar Calabash Shapes: The Top Bowl vs. Sunken Cup Distinction
briyar-kalabas-sekilleri-ust-hazne-ve-go.z: Terms proposed for classifying calabash-style pipes carved from briar: top bowl, sunken cup, bell, and straight body. The criterion is the height at which the bowl sits on the gourd-and-meerschaum pipe's body.

thomas-allan-dunn.z: American compiler who founded The Pipe Smoker's Ephemeris and The Universal Coterie of Pipe Smokers, single-handedly producing the magazine for forty-one years.

kabik.z: American master Michael V. Kabik produced Danish-influenced freehand pipes under the names CHP-X, Sven-Lar, and Wenhall between 1971 and 1990; the workshops he worked at are counted among the first to bring freehand production to a series scale in the USA.

j-davis-pipes.z: The brand of American pipe master and Newsboys guitarist Jody Davis; known for handmade briar pipes made only a few dozen a year, combining classic English proportions with a Danish sense of form.

slovenya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe names originating in Slovenia; contains a brief, factual entry for the single maker on record.

scottspipes-chicagodan-nashvillee-bir-ci.b: Scottspipes (Scott Klein): An Apprenticeship Story from Chicago to Nashville
scottspipes-chicagodan-nashvillee-bir-ci.z: Scottspipes is the brand of American pipe maker Scott Klein. After a long apprenticeship under Alex Florov in Chicago, Klein settled in Nashville, producing handmade top-tier pipes alongside more accessible lines.

peter-pfeifenbau.z: The brand of R.P.-stamped classic and freehand pipes made by Swiss master Roman Peter, a Zurich native, at his workshop in Affoltern am Albis.

keyers-pipe-shop.z: The story of Keyer's Pipe Shop, which grew out of a turner's bench in Cincinnati and sold pipes, canes, and umbrellas for nearly a century.

mastercraft.z: A New York-based brand that had no factory of its own, commissioning its pipes from European and Middle Eastern workshops and distributing them across the US market. Purchased in 1974 by United States Tobacco and moved to Dr. Grabow's facility in North Carolina.

comoys-damga-tipolojisi-ve-tarihlendirme.z: Comoy's pipes carry no year code; the date is narrowed by reading together the shape of the brand wording, the frame of the origin stamp, the inlaid mouthpiece mark, and, where present, the silver band's hallmark.

sadik-yanik.z: A meerschaum carver from Eskişehir. He signs his figural bowls, adorned with animal, battle and mythological scenes, with the stamp 'S. Yanik'; his work is regarded as a contemporary continuation of the 19th-century Vienna school.

rovera.z: A family name born near Varese in 1911 with four brothers, one of the longest-running lineages in Italian pipemaking; the Ardor and Fe-Ro brands both trace back to this root.

polinski.z: A Polish family workshop passed down through generations in Przemyśl, known for the large-bowled, short-shanked, rustic-surfaced handmade pipes of Tadeusz and Celina Poliński.

volkan.z: An Italian pipe brand handmade by Alberto F. Paronelli in his Gavirate workshop; the second branch of a three-generation pipe-making family.

ak-tas-meerschaum.z: A family workshop operating at the Atlıhan Handicrafts Bazaar in Odunpazarı, Eskişehir, known for classic and figural pipes carved from block meerschaum and for a family history said to span generations.

hollanda-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in or connected to the Netherlands, with short, factual entries for seven brands.

kanada-patentleri-uzerine-bir-duzeltme.b: A Correction on Canadian Patents (Dating Guide Addendum)
kanada-patentleri-uzerine-bir-duzeltme.z: A correction to two Canadian-patent records in the Dunhill dating guides: the registration numbers, grant dates, and validity periods of the Vernon joint and the flanged inner tube.

frazing-machine.z: A copy-milling machine that transfers a shape held on a metal pattern onto a briar block; the rough form of mass-produced pipes is cut on this machine.

lule-tasi-pipo-bakimi.z: Meerschaum pipes call for a different care routine than briar: no cake is wanted, the wax layer is preserved, and coloring is managed with patience.

willmer.z: An English pipe workshop founded in London and later relocated to Essex, known for two generations of handmade freehands, which closed in the mid-2000s.

smokers-haven.z: A well-established tobacconist and pipe brand founded in Columbus in 1940, bringing English pipes and its own house blends to the American market.

vulkanit-cubugun-delinmesi.z: Drilling the smoke channel into vulcanite rod on the lathe for mouthpiece making: centering with a tapered bit, finishing the channel with a fine bit, and controlling heat.

piersel-pipes.z: The bench of Scottie Piersel, working in Kansas City, Missouri; known for pencil-thin shanks reinforced with steel tubing.

alexander-pipes.z: A pipe maker founded by Alexandros Zavvos in Athens in the 1960s, processing Greek briar in-house from raw block to finished pipe and known for its moisture-trapping Hygro system.

yunar-pipe.z: The meerschaum workshop of carver Abdülvahap Yunar, working in Odunpazarı, Eskişehir. Known for classic shapes alongside figural carvings featuring eagle-claw and floral motifs.

isvecte-pipo-yapimi.z: Sweden's pipe-making history begins with a handful of factories founded in the 1930s and continues through single-craftsman workshops that gained worldwide renown in the second half of the twentieth century.

gustav-fischere-atfedilen-sahte-lule-tas.b: The Fake Meerschaum Pipe Attributed to Gustav Fischer
gustav-fischere-atfedilen-sahte-lule-tas.z: The story of a cast-molded pipe, bearing a Gustav Fischer signature but not actually meerschaum at all, that has resurfaced repeatedly at auctions and online marketplaces since the mid-1990s, and the signs that give it away.

dr-grabow.z: Named after a Chicago physician around 1930, one of North America's best-known series-production pipe brands; production has continued since 1943 in the town of Sparta, North Carolina.

leopold.z: Handmade pipes by Danish maker Heinrich Leopold Jensen, working in Jutland, carrying only the "Leopold" stamp; production began as a hobby in 1990 and picked up after retirement in 2008.

sark-tutunu.z: The shared name for small-leaved, sun-cured tobacco varieties with high aroma. Considered the core flavoring tobacco of English and Balkan pipe blends.

jeff-gracik-j-alan-pipolarinin-arkasinda.b: Jeff Gracik: The Maker Behind J. Alan Pipes
jeff-gracik-j-alan-pipolarinin-arkasinda.z: An American artisan pipe maker working under the J. Alan name in California; known for an early interview dated 2007 in which he discussed his mentors, his approach to shape, and his habits at the workbench.

bjorn-of-sweden.z: The brand name Malmö maker Björn Bengtsson stamps on his pipes; known for Copenhagen-rooted classic lines, a single dark-brown finish, and a month-year stamp.

goedewaagen.z: GoedeWaagen is a Dutch firm born as a pipemaker's workshop in Gouda in 1779, producing clay pipes and ceramics for more than two centuries. It is known for its double-walled Baronite pipes.

william-h-hendrikx.z: A Dutch-born pipe maker who worked in New York State between the wars; after managing briar factories in College Point he set up his own bench in Ulster Park, and in 1934 obtained a patent redesigning the smoke path between shank and mouthpiece.

s-m-frank-co.z: A US firm reportedly founded in New York in 1900 that brought the Kaywoodie, Yello-Bole and Medico brands under one roof and markets itself as 'America's oldest pipe house.'

kai-nielsen.z: Kai Nielsen, who grew up at the Bari factory and made Faaborg pipes together with his father Viggo Nielsen, is counted among those continuing the Danish tradition through the pipes he makes under his own name in his workshop on the island of Fyn.

klaus-hahn.z: German pipe maker Klaus Hahn, working in Duisburg, reportedly began as a hobby in the 1980s and turned it into workshop production in 1988; known for medium- and large-sized handmade pipes whose shape is guided by the briar's grain.

sebilo.z: A French workshop founded by Patrice Sébilo in Herbignac in 1987; one of the few makers who worked for years with morta, the blackened oak drawn from the Brière marshes.

edwards.z: A pipe brand that started out producing in Saint-Claude, France, and moved its machines and stock of Algerian briar to America in the 1960s.

j-t-cooke.z: James Tanner Cooke, an American pipe maker working at a one-man workshop in Vermont, is known for his multi-stage sandblasting technique and his hand-poured acrylic mouthpieces.

creative-briar-pipes.z: An American brand making freehand briar pipes in a one-man workshop, founded by Al Perkowski in 1972. It was revived after a long career as a model maker in the automotive industry.

joe-hinkle.z: An American pipemaker who began as a self-taught hobbyist and moved into full-time craftsmanship at the Briarlab workshop in Indianapolis, known for his Icon and Marquee series.

saharov.z: Handmade pipes signed with his own name by Russian pipe master Aleksandr Saharov; known for not using templates and for forms that are never repeated.

zenith.z: Zenith is the brand of the van der Want family business, tracing its roots to 1749, which produces cast ceramic pipes in Gouda, Netherlands. Known for its double-walled bowl construction.

parker.z: An English brand set up by Alfred Dunhill in 1922 to finish and sell, under a separate name, bowls that failed to meet his own standards. Brought under the same corporate roof as Hardcastle with the founding of Parker-Hardcastle Limited in 1967.

b-a-weaver-pipes.z: An American handmade pipe brand bearing the signature of Bruce A. Weaver (1951-2019), who worked in Tennessee; known for fine-textured, hard-blasted surfaces.

frederick-g-pipes.z: A small workshop in Tennessee founded by Frederick Garlinghouse, who moved from violin making to pipemaking; after the maker's death in 2006 his daughter kept the brand's site alive.

holbek.z: The pipes of Danish master Gert Holbek, made under his own name; they represent a signature style known for being completely free of ornament, with slender, tall bowls.

jima.z: Designed in France in the 1960s, Jima is one of the era's most unusual system pipes, with a plastic body, metal frame, detachable clay bowl, and coil-wire filter.

caxra-pipe.z: A one-person workshop run by Indonesian artist Deden Hendan Durahman in Bandung, said to turn out only a handful of pipes a month.

c-p-heininger-company.z: A long-established San Francisco tobacco goods firm, founded in the late nineteenth century, that made its own C.P.H. pipes while also selling imported brands, and lost its premises in the 1906 earthquake and fire.

cpw-calabash-pipes.z: CPW Calabash Pipes is a Turkish workshop working in the Odunpazarı district of Eskişehir, making calabash pipes by combining gourds imported from South Africa with block meerschaum bowls.

wiley.z: The freehand pipes of American pipe maker Randy Wiley, who works in Florida; known for hand-carved rustication and hot-oil curing rather than sandblasting.

zivana-tornalama.z: Turning on the lathe the tenon that seats the mouthpiece into the shank: on dimensional tolerance, cutting-tool sharpness, and fit tightness — pipe making's least forgiving stage.

briyar-disindaki-ahsaplarda-pipo.b: Pipes in Woods Other Than Briar
briyar-disindaki-ahsaplarda-pipo.z: Cherry, apple, olive, walnut, maple, hawthorn and many other hardwoods can be turned into pipe bowls; this article gathers how non-briar species behave in terms of weight, workability, and heat resistance.

non-canta-la-raganella.z: A historic Italian pipe brand founded by Alcide Duranti in the Marche region, known for the moisture chamber built into its shank and for the DAC stamp.

rx-pipes.z: The stamp of a Czech workshop run by Radek Jůza in Prague; known for classically proportioned briar pipes alongside freehand work and pipe repair.

kibris-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical index of pipe brands originating from Cyprus; it contains a short, factual entry for the island's single known workshop.

kanada-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: A combined directory of workshops and brands that have made pipes in Canada, offering a short, factual introduction for each brand.

larrysson-pipes.z: The brand of handmade briar pipes made by Iceland-born, Indiana-raised Paul Hubartt, who settled in southwest England, at his one-man workshop in Cornwall.

robert-l-smith-ve-filto-sistem-piposu.b: Robert L. Smith and the Filto System Pipe
robert-l-smith-ve-filto-sistem-piposu.z: An American inventor who, over three U.S. patents spanning the 1940s to the 1960s, developed a metal-stemmed filter pipe and founded the Filto brand in Burgaw, North Carolina.

geiger-pipes.z: A two-person workshop run jointly by Love Geiger and Sara Mossberg in Sweden's Skåne region, producing a small number of handmade pipes each year since 1997.

carmignani.z: The story of Carmignani, founded in Rome in 1892, which had pipe series made under its own name and is counted among Italy's best-known tobacconist shops.

pipo-muzayedeleri.z: The history of pipes and tobacciana changing hands at classic auction houses: from the first dedicated sale held in New York in 1978 to the major collection dispersals in London, Vienna, and Paris.

montgomery-handmade-pipes.z: A small American pipe bench founded by Jeremiah W. Montgomery in Pennsylvania; known for its MHP mark and four-digit date code.

tobacconist-university.z: An American institution founded in 1996 by Jorge Armenteros, offering online education and certification in tobacco retailing and product knowledge.

ben-wade.z: An English brand founded in Leeds in 1860 that passed through three different ownerships and three different production arrangements; today it is best known for the freehand pipes carved at Preben Holm's Danish workshop between 1971 and 1989.

penkov.z: The bench of Russian pipe maker Aleksandr Penkov, who began as a curiosity experiment in Omsk before moving to briar, taking the Danish and Japanese handmade traditions as his models.

white-spotun-gizemi-dunhill-pipolarini-k.b: The Mystery of the White Spot: What Makes Dunhill Pipes Collectible
white-spotun-gizemi-dunhill-pipolarini-k.z: The origin story of the small white dot on Dunhill mouthpieces, and the stamps, finishes, and shape records that set this brand apart for collectors.

gubbels.z: A family firm born from a tobacconist's shop in Roermond that built the Netherlands' first briar pipe factory after the war and became known for the Big Ben brand.

amadeus-pipes.z: A Greek workshop founded near Patras, one of the world's leading briar block suppliers, which also produced pipes under its own name. It ceased operations at the end of 2016.

1851-londra-buyuk-sergisi-ilk-pipo-sergi.b: The 1851 Great Exhibition: The First Pipe Show
1851-londra-buyuk-sergisi-ilk-pipo-sergi.z: The 1851 Great Exhibition, held in the Crystal Palace, is considered the event where pipes were first displayed side by side on an international stage. The pipe section of the exhibition offers a snapshot of the era's production geography as it stood.

j-j-pipes.z: A joint-workshop brand founded by John Klose and Jared Coles in California, where every pipe was approved by both masters together. The partnership ended in the mid-2010s.

anima-pipes.z: A pipe brand made entirely by hand by American maker Brian McNulty, known for a red catlinite point inlaid in the mouthpiece, a circled cross beneath the bowl, and a date stamp struck on the shank.

piet-binsbergen.z: A South African restorer and pipe maker based in Pretoria who moved from teaching visual arts into pipe repair.

hasso-baudis.z: An entry on the German master who made pipes for only five years in northern Germany between 1977 and 1983, gaining renown for his inventive shapes before abruptly leaving the scene.

roger-wallenstein.z: A German handmade pipe maker who took up the trade at fifty-three, known under the name Blue Lobster Pipes. Recognized for the Driftwood surface treatment, Irish-inspired shape names, and the Jolly Roger series.

denny-souers-dcs-damgali-amerikan-freeha.b: Denny Souers: American Freehands Stamped DCS
denny-souers-dcs-damgali-amerikan-freeha.z: American maker Denny Souers is known for Danish-influenced freehand pipes carved from Greek-sourced briar; his signature is the DCS letters carved rather than stamped under the shank.

poul-ilsted-bech.z: Danish maker Poul Ilsted Bech (d. 2017) was first known for his bulldog interpretations, then for his multi-faceted chambers; called "The Facet Master" in the community.

jim-deschaine-sierra-eteklerinde-bir-bab.b: Jim DeSchaine: A Father-and-Son Bench in the Sierra Foothills
jim-deschaine-sierra-eteklerinde-bir-bab.z: Working in the foothills of California's Sierra Nevada, Jim DeSchaine, by his own account, brought a long background in woodworking to pipe making in 2013; pipes stamped J. Deschaine are made at a small family workshop.

eike-hallmann.z: A one-master workshop founded in Germany in 2023 by Eike Hallmann, whose day job is electronics technician, known for freehand briar pipes with ebonite mouthpieces.

sara-pipes.z: The second brand founded by Danish master Tom Eltang, named after his daughter, which carries the same making philosophy as his top-tier signature pipes into a more accessible production line.

dunhill-ailesi-markanin-arkasindaki-kusa.b: The Dunhill Family: The Generations Behind the Brand
dunhill-ailesi-markanin-arkasindaki-kusa.z: From Alfred Dunhill to his son Alfred Henry, from his brother Herbert to Mary Dunhill, the family leadership spanning these generations and the mark they left on the brand.

gamboni.z: Gian Maria Gamboni's Rome-based one-person workshop, known for an unusual quality-stamp system drawn from golf terminology.

rusya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands made in Russia or documented as Russian-made; contains brief, factual entries for eleven brands.

elliott-pipes.z: Handmade American pipes produced piece by piece by Alabama tobacconist Skip Elliott in a workshop attached to his home, whose volume has never grown.

rainer-barbi.z: A pioneer of the German freehand pipe tradition, producing from 1974 to 2011, and his eponymous workshop.

syring.z: The brand of German handmade pipes carved one by one by Karl-Heinz Syring in his small repair workshop in Flensburg, in the spare hours of his career as a civil servant.

matkap-tezgahi.z: The stationary drilling machine used in the pipe workshop to bore the bowl, smoke channel, and mortise; speed control, table height, and quill stroke are the main features that make it suitable for pipe work.

kapp-petersonin-yeni-fabrikaya-tasinmasi.b: Kapp & Peterson's Move to a New Factory (2022)
kapp-petersonin-yeni-fabrikaya-tasinmasi.z: Dublin pipe maker Kapp & Peterson left the Sallynoggin building it had worked in for fifty years in May 2022, moving to a new facility in the nearby district of Deansgrange.

pipo-filtreleri-ve-sistemleri.z: The history and workings of activated-carbon and balsa filters, along with structural solutions like the Peterson System and Falcon, aimed at reducing moisture and tar in pipe smoke.

rivendell-pipes-levi-zurcherin-kisa-omur.b: Rivendell Pipes: Levi Zurcher's Short-Lived American Workshop
rivendell-pipes-levi-zurcherin-kisa-omur.z: The story of the handmade pipes produced by Arizona university graduate Levi Zurcher under the name Rivendell Pipes in the early 2000s, and of a workshop whose trail went cold.

vauen.z: With roots reaching back to 1848, Vauen is Germany's oldest pipe factory still in production. Its 1934 Dr. Perl 9 mm activated-charcoal filter laid the foundation for the German school of pipe smoking.

american-smoking-pipe-co.z: Founded in New Jersey in 1978 by two friends, American Smoking Pipe Co. deliberately chose its name to set itself apart from a pipe world dominated by European names. The workshop still operates today from Montana, under Mark Tinsky.

vollmer-nilsson.z: A Swedish workshop run by two half-brothers under a single stamp in Malmö; they built a style resting on classic molds, meticulous interior work, and their own registered silver hallmark rather than the Scandinavian freehand trend.

heeschen.z: The signature of Danish master Peter Heeschen (1945-2015), produced in his one-man workshop near Odense; the product of a late-blooming craft career founded after age fifty-three.

pipa-croci.z: An Italian workshop founded in Mantua in 1983, known for hand-shaped plateau briar pipes and a seven-tier quality classification.

pipo-aksesuarlari.z: A survey of auxiliary gear from lighting tools to tampers, ashtrays to stands and storage jars; which items are a functional necessity and which belong to the world of craft and collecting.

rattrays.z: Rattray's is a brand that grew out of a Scottish tobacconist's shop founded in Perth in the early 20th century, first known for its blends. After the Perth business closed in 1981 the brand passed into the orbit of Germany's Kohlhase & Kopp, and its pipes began to be made on contract at workshops in various countries.

balleby-pipes.z: A one-man workshop Danish maker Kurt Balleby Hansen has run in Kolding since 1983, known for its 14-karat gold diamond signature set into the mouthpiece.

pipo-ve-saglik.z: A neutral summary of pipe smoking's relationship to health, drawing on scientific research and public health data. Covers cancer, COPD, and cardiovascular risks along with nicotine dependence.

keresaspa.z: Keresaspa is both the pseudonym and the brand of Tehran-based pipemaker Saeed Nazarli. A self-taught workshop turns out about thirty handmade briar pipes a year; its tier names and year stamp are drawn from ancient Iranian tradition.

trovato-pipa.z: A small American workshop, reportedly founded in Maryland in 2013, that restores unmarked, unclaimed old pipes and stamps them with its own name.

dunhillin-sira-disi-sekilleri-don-duke-v.b: Dunhill's Uncommon Shapes: Don, Duke, and Opera
dunhillin-sira-disi-sekilleri-don-duke-v.z: The differences among three shapes sitting at the margin of Dunhill's standard shape list — Don, Duke, and Opera — their stamp numbers, and their traces in the records.

charles-fairmorn.z: A tobacco trading group made up of American, German, and Dominican companies sharing the same name; in the pipe world it is known for a small number of Danish-made freehands.

f-j-kaldenberg-company.z: The corporate form the New York meerschaum pipe and amber-goods maker Kaldenberg took on in 1887. A short corporate life that closed with the 1893 financial panic, an 1896 fire, and dissolution in 1900.

il-ceppo.z: An Italian handmade pipe workshop founded in Pesaro in the late 1970s by architect Giorgio Imperatori, run since the mid-1990s by Franco Rossi and his sister Nadia. Known for numeral stamps indicating surface finish.

tutun-kesimleri.z: The cuts that define the sales forms of pipe tobacco — ribbon, flake, plug, and rope — affect nearly every aspect of the smoking experience, from burn speed to flavor intensity.

castleford.z: An English pipe brand founded by Kent-based maker Colin Fromm for the American market, known for its estate freehands.

foundation.z: An Italian brand out of Rome, launched by Massimo Musicò in November 2005 after the Becker & Musicò stamp was retired. Known for a year-counting numbering system and designer initials.

fikri-baki.z: A meerschaum pipe master from Eskişehir. Starting as an apprentice in 1969, he moved from figurative carving to classic and contemporary pipe forms, known for bringing briar materials such as silver, bamboo, and hand-cut ebonite into meerschaum.

baris-cubugu-bir-simgenin-deyime-donusme.b: Peace Pipe: How a Symbol Became an Idiom
baris-cubugu-bir-simgenin-deyime-donusme.z: The name "peace pipe," given from outside to North America's ceremonial pipe, shifted over the centuries from a description of a sacred object into an everyday idiom and a popular-culture metaphor.

cao.z: A brand founded in the United States by Istanbul-born engineer Cano A. Ozgener, which began by reworking Turkish meerschaum pipes and later grew in the cigar field.

luna-pipes-yuzuklerin-efendisine-adanmis.b: Luna Pipes: An American Workshop Devoted to The Lord of the Rings
luna-pipes-yuzuklerin-efendisine-adanmis.z: Founded by Tom Johnson in Washington State, Luna Pipes is known for made-to-order freehand briar pipes as well as long-stemmed fantasy models named Hobbit, Strider, and Gandalf.

college-class-pipes-amerikan-universitel.b: College Class Pipes: America's University Class Pipes
college-class-pipes-amerikan-universitel.z: A tradition that lived on American campuses from the late 19th century to the early 1960s, encompassing both the clay pipe smoked communally and broken at graduation and the personal pipe engraved with a school letter and class year.

f-b-bauer.z: The stamp of an Austrian-born master, said to have trained in the master-apprentice system in Vienna, who made his pipes alone in Detroit during the first half of the twentieth century.

millville.z: A small English workshop founded by Dennis Marshall in 1980 and later run by his son John Marshall; known for freehand pipes in the Charatan tradition.

heding.z: The workshop of Danish maker Peter Heding, who left molecular biology research for the bench, known for hand-shaped freehand stummels and a four-tier grading system.

mcclelland-tobacco-company.z: An American pipe tobacco maker that operated in Kansas City from 1977 to 2018. Regarded as the world's reference brand for matured Virginia blends.

ma-colombe.z: A one-person pipe brand founded in 1991 by French maker Jean Masson; known for carved bowls and a nicotine reservoir.

antika-lule-tasi-pipolar.z: Figural meerschaum pipes carved in 19th-century Europe form one of the oldest branches of collecting. This entry covers the history, distinguishing features, and dating criteria of antique meerschaum.

emin.z: Emin is a Turkish brand from Eskişehir, reportedly founded in 1989 by brothers Medet and İmdat Kara, carving densely figured pipes from block meerschaum; after the 2001 split the name stayed with İmdat Kara.

paul-jeantet-sa.z: A mouthpiece factory founded in Saint-Claude in 1905-1906 that freed the French pipe industry from German ebonite imports; today it continues under the name Jeantet élastomères in the rubber sector.

deprey.z: The short-lived workshop of American maker R. James DePrey, who hand-crafted freehand pipes in the second half of the 1980s in Fort Kent, in northern Maine.

yuzuklerin-efendisinde-pipo-ve-pipo-otu.b: Pipes and Pipe-Weed in The Lord of the Rings
yuzuklerin-efendisinde-pipo-ve-pipo-otu.z: In J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, smoking a pipe is not decoration but one of the founding habits of Shire culture. This entry looks at the fictional history of pipe-weed and Tolkien's own pipe habit.

bari.z: A Danish pipe brand founded by Viggo Nielsen in Kolding, combining machine roughing with hand finishing.

clubb-torontodan-los-angelesa-bir-tutunc.b: Clubb: A Tobacconist Name from Toronto to Los Angeles
clubb-torontodan-los-angelesa-bir-tutunc.z: A brief history, compiled from records, of A. Clubb & Sons, founded in Toronto in 1878, and the tobacconist shop of the same trade name operating in Los Angeles in the early 20th century.

reiss-premier-co.z: A company born from the merger of two old pipe firms in Chicago, which carried Kaywoodie and the Drinkless system to the center of the American market.

mcgahey.z: The McGahey tobacconist shop, which operated on Exeter's High Street for nearly a century and a half, and the pipes it stamped with its own name.

viprati.z: The Italian handmade pipe brand founded by Luigi Viprati in the town of Pontoglio, Lombardy, known for its four-leaf-clover grading and silver-adorned series.

burley.z: An American-origin tobacco variety that is air-cured, low in sugar, and high in nicotine. With a leaf structure that holds flavors very well, it is considered the foundation leaf of aromatic blends and the American pipe tradition.

briyar-alistirma-surecinin-bilinmezleri.b: The Mysteries of the Briar Break-In Process
briyar-alistirma-surecinin-bilinmezleri.z: There is no single explanation for why a new briar pipe tends to smoke better over time. This entry gathers the competing views on the carbon cake's role, resin left in the wood, the degree of curing, and the raw material itself.

brandon-brooks.z: The workshop and style of American independent pipemaker Brandon Brooks, working in Georgetown, Kentucky, who came from percussion and drum making.

don-florian.z: Don Florian is the brand of handmade briar pipes Italian maker Matteo Stefani shapes using only a file and sandpaper, without a lathe, in his one-man workshop.

briyar-kurleme.z: The drying and purifying process a briar burl goes through from the moment it's pulled from the ground to the point it becomes a block ready for working; air curing, kiln drying, and oil curing methods.

krisor.z: An American master who took up pipemaking in Northern California after retirement, carving almost exclusively Canadians and stamping his pipes' shanks with their weight in grams.

midas-meerschaum.z: A contemporary meerschaum pipe workshop founded in Eskişehir, focused on classic shapes and hand-made stems.

miscoipipes.z: A one-man handmade pipe workshop founded as a hobby in 2014 by Canadian maker Dimitry Miscoi, working with well-rested Italian briar and hand-cut ebonite mouthpieces.

kum-puskurtme-sanati.z: Sandblasting is an abrasion technique that migrated from industry to the pipe bench. Machine type, abrasive material, the briar's grain, and the curing method together determine the result.

perique.z: A rare tobacco from Louisiana's St. James Parish, pressure-fermented in its own juices inside oak barrels. Its peppery, dried-fruit character has earned it the title "the black pepper of blends."

navy-flake-ve-rom-gelenegi.b: Navy Flake and the Rum Tradition
navy-flake-ve-rom-gelenegi.z: The pressed-tobacco tradition, today known as navy flake, that arose from sailors' habit of binding tobacco with rope and pressure and moistening it with rum or molasses.

mclary-iki-donemde-kurulmus-bir-amerikan.b: McLary: An American Pipe Bench Founded in Two Periods
mclary-iki-donemde-kurulmus-bir-amerikan.z: The one-person workshop Dave McLary rebuilt in Indiana after a long professional career, reviving the pipe-making skills he had learned under Bill Mincer in the mid-1960s.

reum-pipes.z: An American handmade pipe brand Sean Reum runs single-handedly at his bench in Northwest Montana; noted for a craft background in razor restoration, Danish-influenced shapes, and predominantly sandblasted finishes.

lumberman.z: A straight pipe shape joining a long oval shank with a short saddle mouthpiece, considered one of the rarer members of the Canadian family.

peterson.z: An Irish pipe house founded in Dublin in 1865. It brought lasting innovations to pipe design with its moisture-trapping 'System' chamber and P-Lip mouthpiece.

oom-paul-bir-pipo-seklinin-adi-ve-kokeni.b: Oom Paul: The Name and Origin of a Pipe Shape
oom-paul-bir-pipo-seklinin-adi-ve-kokeni.z: The South African statesman behind the name of the full-bent, cylindrical-bowled Oom Paul shape, its place in the Second Boer War, and the unresolved confusion with the name 'Hungarian.'

bazzanelli.z: A handmade pipe workshop founded in 2001 by Mauro Marcos Bazzanella in Timbó, in Brazil's Santa Catarina state, working with native woods such as imbuia and angico.

moritz.z: A German one-man workshop working in Mönchengladbach, whose first pipes appeared in the summer of 2004; known for freehand briar pipes drawing on the Danish school.

svend-hangaard.z: A Danish maker trained in Faaborg who returned to the bench after retiring from prison guard duty, producing around fifty pipes a year.

astleys.z: A tobacconist and pipe brand opened on London's Jermyn Street in 1862, known for high-quality pipes commissioned from other makers rather than produced in its own workshop.

kamensky.z: The one-man pipe workshop of Stanislav Kamensky, who grew up in Russia and settled in Australia after 2014, known for reverse-calabash construction and meticulous interior craftsmanship.

yuz-yillik-briyar-efsanesi.z: The origin of the oft-repeated "hundred-year-old briar" claim in the pipe world, how manufacturers have used the phrase, and maker Rainer Barbi's objection to it.

kuba-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands from Cuba, currently containing a short, factual entry for FC, the single name on record.

ben-rapaport.z: The work, books, and standing within the community of American researcher Ben Rapaport, who has written on antique pipe collecting and tobacco literature for over half a century.

brighton-james-pipes.z: The one-man American bench of Brighton James de los Santos; combines a design-school approach to line with contemporary artisan pipemaking.

ed-burak.z: Ed Burak, who ran the Connoisseur Pipe Shop in New York for forty years, is counted among the influential names in American pipe design for his approach of designing pipes rather than carving them himself.

bruken.z: A Spanish pipe factory operating since 1914 in Aldaia, near Valencia, that has remained in the Navarro family since its founding and produces both its own pipes and semi-finished bowls for other brands.

massis-pipes.z: Belgian maker Nick Ramaekers's one-man workshop in Limburg, known since 2011 for producing only a handful of handmade briar and olive-wood pipes each year.

loewe-pipolarini-tarihlendirme.z: Loewe pipes carry no year code; dating is inferred by layering the layout of the shank stamps, the presence of a series name, the switch from a shape name to a three-digit number, and the assay mark on the silver band.

jerry-zenn.z: A Taiwanese maker who moved from auto repair into pipe making and produces briar pipes inlaid with bamboo and horn in his workshop in Kaohsiung.

robert-mewis.z: An architect by profession, Robert Mewis produced handmade pipes in Germany throughout the 1980s after taking over Hasso Baudis's Oldenburg workshop.

fischer.z: An American pipe workshop of German-descended family, working in Buffalo and Orchard Park, which closed in 1978.

michail-kyriazanos.z: A Greek pipe master working on the island of Paros in the Aegean. Having started production under the Archaggelos mark in 2010, he now continues under his own name; he uses only Greek briar and hand-cut ebonite stems to make classic English shapes.

design-berlin.z: Born from the workshop Hubert Hartmann founded in Berlin in 1948, db - Design Berlin moved from cheap shag pipes to Danish-influenced designs to become Germany's second-largest pipe manufacturer.

general-dawes-ve-captain-warren-pipolari.b: The General Dawes and Captain Warren Pipes
general-dawes-ve-captain-warren-pipolari.z: Two period examples of the 'underslung' arrangement, in which the stem attaches near the top of the chamber: the Chicago-patented General Dawes pipe and the British-made, uncertain-origin Captain Warren.

e-deguingand-son.z: A French-English pipe business founded by the London-based merchant Émile Deguingand, producing at its factory in Saint-Claude from the late 19th century into the 1930s.

prammer-freehand-pfeifen.z: A one-man workshop Austrian Josef Prammer has run in Ungenach since 1993; known for hand-shaped pipes made from bog oak alongside briar.

vagn-nielsen.z: A Danish maker who worked in Korsør and stamped his pipes "Vagn P. Nielsen." Coming from blacksmithing and construction work, he moved into pipe making full time in the mid-1990s after a decade as an amateur.

ershov.z: Ceramicist Vladimir Ershov, working in Rostov-on-Don, is a master who hand-produces clay pipes by reconstructing the 17th-century Anatolian-derived clay pipe tradition from museum examples.

wolfram-benz.z: After nearly thirty years in metalworking, Wolfram Benz moved into pipemaking; he is known for shaping his bodies purely with a file, never putting them on a machine.

ascot.z: A French pipe name rooted in the La Bruyère merger at Saint-Claude, later continued as a sub-brand of Chacom. The same name has also been used on pipes of English and Italian origin.

bjarne.z: A Danish brand Bjarne Nielsen (1941-2008) founded in Copenhagen in 1973; it brought the work of makers gathered under its own name to more than thirty countries, ending with its founder's death.

loewe-co.z: An English pipe brand founded by Emil Loewe in 1856 on Haymarket in London, known for silver spigot fittings and shape names drawn from British place names.

dunhill-curiosities-markanin-az-bilinen-.b: Dunhill Curiosities: The Brand's Lesser-Known Records
dunhill-curiosities-markanin-az-bilinen-.z: Records outside the main narrative of Dunhill history: the cartridge and Vernon-connection patents, the silver bands fitted at the factory, the tobacco license granted to Germany, and the dispersal of the founder's collection.

gabos-pipes.z: A one-person Romanian workshop Costin Gabos founded in the Transylvanian town of Miercurea Ciuc, known for its freehand pipes.

kongre-kutuphanesi-rehberlerinden-amerik.b: American Pipe Manufacturers Compiled from Library of Congress Directories
kongre-kutuphanesi-rehberlerinden-amerik.z: A listing of American pipe manufacturers and distributors compiled by S. Paul Jung in 1991, based on city and trade directories held at the Library of Congress. It covers roughly 1860 to 1930.

benner.z: The name behind pipes signed with the childhood nickname of Danish maker Bent Nielsen (b. 1944); known for moving from the fantasy shapes of the 1970s to classic forms, and for returning to the bench after a thirty-year gap.

butz-choquin.z: Butz-Choquin is a French pipe brand born from the partnership of a tobacconist and his son-in-law in Metz in 1858, which relocated to Saint-Claude after 1951. It takes its name from its two founders' surnames.

danimarka-okulu.z: A school born in Copenhagen during the Second World War years, carrying functionalist design into the handmade pipe and leaving a deep mark on pipemaking worldwide.

canaan-pipes.z: A one-man workshop run by Abi Natur in Bar, Montenegro, known for making moldless pipes from plateau briar as well as from the region's ancient olive trees.

pohlmann-pipes.z: The workshop of American master Brad Pohlmann, who trained at Vermont's Briar Workshop and returned to making pipes under his own name after a long break.

orlik.z: A brand founded in London in 1899 by Louis Orlik, known for affordable yet carefully made English pipes, whose name today lives on in tobaccos produced in Denmark.

il-ciocco.z: An Italian pipe workshop founded in 2011 by Antimo Parolise of Pescara, each piece shaped by hand. Known for freehand shapes and native wood species.

trever-talbertin-delme-yontemi.z: Pipe maker Trever Talbert's preference for a lathe over a drill press when boring a briar body, the order he follows for the holes, and the Saint-Claude-made drilling machine in his workshop.

ulkesi-belirsiz-markalar-pipo-markalari-.b: Directory of Pipe Brands of Uncertain Country (1/2)
ulkesi-belirsiz-markalar-pipo-markalari-.z: Short profiles of ninety-three pipe brands whose country of production is not stated in the records or cannot be reliably determined. The directory's first part, covering AA Pipes through TRG Handcrafted Pipes.

charatan-pipolarini-tarihlendirme.z: A method for reading a Charatan pipe's production period from the shape of the mouthpiece, the CP stamp, the shank wording, and additions to the shape code. Period boundaries and where the sources disagree.

laxey-pipes-ltd.z: A pipe factory founded in the mid-1960s in the town of Laxey on the Isle of Man, which worked East African meerschaum and made bowls for many well-known brands.

rc-sands.z: The signature of American maker Raymond "Chuck" Sands, who made pipes without a lathe in a converted barn workshop in Ohio. Known for thick-walled, unpretentious briar pipes.

savas-oncesi-dunhill-bruyere-drlerinde-k.b: Square Stamp and Grading on Pre-War Dunhill Bruyere DRs
savas-oncesi-dunhill-bruyere-drlerinde-k.z: How are the small square stamps seen around the shank writing on pre-World War II Dunhill DR pipes read, when collector compilations are compared against the era's catalog tiers?

j-l-thompson-bodrum-atolyesinden-cikan-a.b: J.L. Thompson: American Pipes from a Basement Workshop
j-l-thompson-bodrum-atolyesinden-cikan-a.z: The brand of Jason Thompson, who makes close to thirty pipes a year at a small workshop in his basement in the town of Parkville, Maryland. A part-time pursuit begun in 2013 that grew into a signature known for its BriarLab years.

amerikan-kumlama-okulu-2000lerin-kumlanm.b: The American Sandblasting School: The 2000s Sandblasted Pipe Debate
amerikan-kumlama-okulu-2000lerin-kumlanm.z: The assessment put forward by Fred Hanna in 2008, arguing that the best sandblasted pipes of the era came from independent American makers; the workshops named and the technical distinction the debate rests on.

ronni-bikacsan.z: A pipe repair and restoration craftsman working in Nashville under the name NightOwl Pipe Works, known for "blueprinting" — re-dimensioning a pipe's smoke channel from end to end.

gbd.z: A pipe brand founded in Paris in 1850, taking its name from the initials of its three partners' surnames; it passed into British ownership in 1902, with production split between Paris, London, and Saint-Claude.

wahner.z: The workshop of René Wähner, who made no more than twenty pipes a year in Arnsberg in the mid-1990s; a German handmade brand whose total output stayed limited to just over a hundred pieces.

talamona.z: An Italian family brand that grew out of a carpentry workshop near Varese, known across two generations for 9 mm-filtered briar pipes, which closed in 2000.

erik-nielsen.z: Danish pipemaker Erik Nielsen left a railway job after fifty and trained at Kurt Balleby's workshop; since the early 2000s he has produced classically lined pipes under his own name in Vejle.

dunhill-white-spot-garantisi.z: The evolution of Dunhill's replacement pledge, known by the white spot on the stem, from its unlimited 1910 form to its one-year form in the 1920s, and how this change relates to year-code stamping.

asbestli-pipo.z: Pipes made from asbestos fiber in the last quarter of the 19th century, promoted for their indestructibility, shared display cases with briar and meerschaum for roughly a generation before being abandoned entirely. This entry traces the patents and makers.

tom-richard-pipes.z: The brand of pipes individually hand-shaped by Thomas Richard Mehret in northern Germany; work from his workshop just south of the Danish border blends the Scandinavian line with German craftsmanship.

the-kaldenberg-company-new-yorkta-lule-t.b: The Kaldenberg Company: Meerschaum Pipe Manufacture in New York
the-kaldenberg-company-new-yorkta-lule-t.z: New York's most visible meerschaum pipe manufacturer in the 19th century. Its rise from a turner's workshop to a seven-story factory, the advertising language it built on exhibition awards, and its collapse before the century closed.

denicotea.z: An accessory manufacturer founded in Cologne in 1932, known for its silica-gel filter and for the filtered pipes that gave it a foothold in the German market.

enrique.z: The brand of French pipemaker David Enrique, who left an IT career to settle in Saint-Claude and opened his own workshop in 2007. He kept production limited to 120-150 pipes a year and stopped in 2017.

wgm-meerschaum.z: WGM Meerschaum is a Turkish meerschaum brand associated with the name of Eskişehir carver Mustafa Albayrak; its bowls, carved from block stone, are fitted with a pull-out delrin tenon in the manner of briar pipes.

dunhill-christmas-pipe.z: The limited-edition Christmas pipes Dunhill has released each year since 1980, and the twelve-year theme series that link them together.

kulpinski.z: The workshop of Polish master Ryszard Kulpiński in Przemyśl, his path from apprenticeship under Walat to his own signature, and his hand-worked Autograf pipes.

esoterica-tobacciana.z: A private-label pipe tobacco brand made at the J.F. Germain & Son factory on Jersey but built for the American market. Known for its Penzance and Stonehaven blends.

brian-doran.z: An American pipe master reportedly working alone in West Virginia since 2012, known for sturdy everyday-use poker and billiard shapes and for working bog oak alongside briar.

william-braggein-pipo-cizimleri-dagilan-.b: William Bragge's Pipe Drawings: A Scattered Set of Records
william-braggein-pipo-cizimleri-dagilan-.z: Roughly 1,200 scale drawings, hand-prepared and gathered in twenty boxes, documenting what is considered the most extensive pipe collection of the 19th century. Once the collection dispersed, the drawings were split up too.

atin.z: A handmade pipe brand from Bahareh Khosroanjam, an Iranian maker working in Tehran, who reinterprets the Scandinavian and Japanese line through plain surfaces.

oldenkott.z: Rooted in an 18th-century Dutch tobacco dynasty, Oldenkott made pipes in the town of Rees in the Lower Rhine from 1932 to 1992 and was for a time considered Germany's largest pipe factory.

clemons-emeklilikten-sonra-kurulan-bir-a.b: Clemons: An American Bench Built After Retirement
clemons-emeklilikten-sonra-kurulan-bir-a.z: The one-person workshop of Greg Clemons, who took up pipe-making after his long service in the Marine Corps; his large-bodied briar pipes and a year-based numbering system.

dr-plumbs.z: A pipe brand, reportedly founded in 1925, known for the aluminum cooling tube fitted between the shank and mouthpiece; produced in France for many years before shifting to English manufacture under Cadogan.

lubinski-ltd.z: A family company founded in Fermo in 1962 that became one of Italy's largest wholesale distributors of pipes and pipe accessories.

pipo-dilinde-sade-anlatim-tartismasi.b: The Plain-Speech Debate in Pipe Language
pipo-dilinde-sade-anlatim-tartismasi.z: A running debate over how the vocabulary of the pipe and tobacco community has shifted from nineteenth-century slang to today's jargon of abbreviations, and over whether the new terms are even necessary.

schoonmaker-kirk-yili-askin-bir-amator-a.b: Schoonmaker: A Forty-Year-Old Amateur American Workbench
schoonmaker-kirk-yili-askin-bir-amator-a.z: A one-man briar workbench signed with Renny Schoonmaker's own surname, one that never grew into a regular business. Production began in upstate New York in the late 1970s and continued intermittently.

tutun-ve-pipo-sanayisi-tarihi-icin-arast.b: Research Resources for Tobacco and Pipe-Industry History
tutun-ve-pipo-sanayisi-tarihi-icin-arast.z: Archives, private collections, and digital document libraries documenting the history of the tobacco and pipe industry in the United States and Britain; what they offer researchers and where they fall short.

ser-jacopo.z: An Italian handmade pipe workshop founded in Pesaro in the early 1980s by Giancarlo Guidi after he left Mastro de Paja. Known for its Gem line finished with precious stone and metal rings, and its limited yearly Domina models.

pipes-by-cody-perkins.z: A one-person pipe workshop run by Canadian master Cody Perkins in Edmonton, known for unfilled bodies with no bowl coating and hand-cut stems.

wally-frank.z: An American pipe and tobacco brand founded in New York in the 1930s, known for its retail chain and mail-order catalog sales. Known for having its own-name pipes made by a range of different workshops.

jon-david-cole.z: An American tobacconist known for owning Mississippi's storied The Country Squire, blending tobacco, and co-founding Country Squire Radio.

bonfiglioli.z: An Italian handmade pipe brand made in limited numbers by Alberto Bonfiglioli in his own shop in Bologna, from long-rested briar.

tagua-nut.z: Tagua, the hard seed of the ivory palm that grows in South America, is used in pipe shank extensions and occasionally in bowls for its ivory-like texture.

sturgill.z: The short story of Ohio wood-carver Ken Sturgill's briar pipemaking, which began in 1979 and was set aside in the late 1980s.

eyup-sabri.z: Known for the density of carving on his figurative bowls, moving parts, and horn mouthpieces, Eyup Sabri (1948-2005) is one of the most frequently cited masters of Turkish meerschaum carving.

alexander-hasty.z: A Kansas pipe maker who started teaching himself pipe making in 2011 and moved to full-time craft work after gaining experience in Grant Batson's workshop.

malta-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands from Malta, containing a short, factual entry on the one manufacturer documented on the island.

yunas-edge.z: A name found in foreign pipe records as 'Yunas Edge' is believed to refer to Eskişehir meerschaum carver Yunus Ege, who began his apprenticeship in 1965 at the bench of Hüseyin Yanık. Known for figural bowls; also credited with a role in training the master's son, Sadık Yanık.

ahmet-buyukcopur.z: A small-scale meerschaum pipe workshop in Eskişehir where two master carvers and an assistant work. The name reached pipe sources outside Türkiye through the workshop's own website, launched in 2000.

zeytin-agaci-pipo.z: Pipes made from the wood of the Mediterranean olive tree (Olea europaea): known for a wavy grain pattern, high density, and heat behavior that differs from briar.

unlu-pipo-icicileri.z: From Albert Einstein to Mark Twain, from Douglas MacArthur to the fictional Sherlock Holmes, a compendium of figures identified with a pipe, presented with supporting sources.

peterson-sherlock-holmes-serisi.z: The structure and shape list of the pipe series Peterson launched in 1987, dedicated to Conan Doyle's detective, comprising fourteen special shapes.

hydrostone-ve-recine-pipolar.z: Two materials relying on mold-casting rather than carving: plaster-based hydrostone was used in meerschaum copies and repairs, while cast resin became both the material of cheap mass-produced bowls and a tool of forgery in the collector market.

mincer.z: The bench of American Tracy Mincer, founder of the Custom-Bilt brand; known for thick-walled rustic pipes, the perforated Doodler model, and the brand's later change of hands.

lovat.z: A classic pipe shape combining a long, round-shanked neck with a short saddle mouthpiece, considered the most compact member of the Canadian family.

r-ubben-pipes-donem-canlandirmacilari-ic.b: R. Ubben Pipes: American Pipes Made for Period Reenactors
r-ubben-pipes-donem-canlandirmacilari-ic.z: A small bench run by Randolph J. Ubben in Connecticut, recreating 1860s pipe shapes with period materials and tools.

bertram-safferling.z: A German designer and pipe maker who spent over twenty-five years making freehand pipes at his Stuttgart workshop, moving his bench to South Tyrol in 2005.

whidbey-islander-pipes.z: Freehand American pipes made and sold by Travers LaRue and his son-in-law Chuck Whitmore on Whidbey Island, Washington, between 1972 and 1983; today only a small number of examples are known.

semus.z: A brand name listed under Türkiye in pipe reference sources, though the documents behind it trace not to a workshop but to a Bremen-based import business.

del-grano.z: An Italian workshop founded by Parma engineer Alberto Del Grano, combining briar with goldsmithing and diamond work. Its best-known piece is the pipe announced as a numbered series of 999 on the hundredth anniversary of Giuseppe Verdi's death.

don-warren-pipes-albuquerquede-danimarka.b: Don Warren Pipes: A Danish-Influenced Bench in Albuquerque
don-warren-pipes-albuquerquede-danimarka.z: A one-man handmade-pipe bench operating in Albuquerque, New Mexico, combining briar with bog oak and native hardwoods alongside deer antler.

james-upshall.z: An English workshop founded in 1978 in the village of Tilshead, Wiltshire, known for hand-turned, unfilled, straight-grain briar pipes made by craftsmen from the Charatan school.

lars-ivarsson.z: Danish pipe maker Lars Ivarsson (c. 1944-2018), son of Sixten Ivarsson. He is counted among the names who shaped the vocabulary of contemporary handmade pipes, with his teardrop-section shank and shapes such as blowfish.

castello-pipolarini-tarihlendirme-ve-dam.b: Dating Castello Pipes and Reading the Stamps
castello-pipolarini-tarihlendirme-ve-dam.z: The Cantù-based Castello workshop's stamp system: placing a pipe in its period by reading the Mi Reserva wording, the K grading, the number inside the castle, and shop codes together.

gray-mountain-pipes-kankakeede-bir-tek-k.b: Gray Mountain Pipes: A One-Man Bench in Kankakee
gray-mountain-pipes-kankakeede-bir-tek-k.z: An American bench Illinois's Mark Gradberg began as a hobby in 1995 and turned into a full-time pursuit by the late 1990s, known for one-of-a-kind freehand pipes.

ranz-freehands.z: The brand of Ron Smith, who works alone in East Tennessee; a home workshop known for the freehand shapes and colorful finishes of a maker who came to the craft after his working career.

michel.z: A private-label pipe line sold under its own name by a North Carolina tobacconist called Maison Michel, made to order at various factories in England, France, and Denmark.
