sergey-dyomin.z: A Russian pipe maker working in Saint Petersburg, trained under Vladimir Grechukhin and now the senior maker at the PS Studio workshop, known for turning difficult shapes on the lathe.

serit-testere.z: The band saw that reduces a briar block to a rough shape: how it works, the relationship between blade width and turning radius, and its place in the pipe workshop.

pipo-ve-saglik-literaturu-tartismanin-ka.b: Pipe Smoking and the Health Literature: Sources of the Debate
pipo-ve-saglik-literaturu-tartismanin-ka.z: This article examines how the health effects of pipe smoking have been documented in the medical literature, the community's own compilations, and the debate over selective quoting. It is a source survey spanning from institutional reports to recent cohort studies.

trebor.z: A British pipe brand best remembered for an 1912 cooling-chamber patent, which appears in trade records under a succession of different London companies throughout the twentieth century.

prohibition-pipes.z: A small-scale briar pipe workshop run in Virginia under his own name by American wood craftsman Jonathan Lavezzo, after he handed Moonshine Pipe Company over to BriarWorks.

abd-pipo-markalari-dizini-1.z: The first installment of an alphabetical directory of pipe brands, factories, and one-person workshops in the United States: ninety-one entries from Admiral to Gerrard.

agizlik-malzemeleri.z: Introduces current materials used for pipe mouthpieces such as ebonite (vulcanite), acrylic, and Cumberland, along with historical materials like amber and horn, the oxidation problem, and the main mouthpiece shapes.

jacono.z: A one-man workshop Tonino Jacono founded in 1983 in Jesi, in the Marche region, known for quality grades named after chess pieces.

artisan-pipo-ve-fabrika-piposu.z: An entry comparing handmade (artisan) pipes and factory pipes in terms of production philosophy, technical craftsmanship, and terminology.

kybele.z: A Turkish meerschaum pipe brand reportedly founded in 2002 and associated with maker İsmail Özdamar and a company called Kıraç. Documented information about it is limited to a few lines.

nachwalter.z: Elliott Nachwalter's handmade American pipe signature, which began in a Vermont cabin and passed through New York and the Briar Workshop years.

rex-walden-pipes-danimarka-ve-japon-etki.b: Rex Walden Pipes: A Texas Bench Under Danish and Japanese Influence
rex-walden-pipes-danimarka-ve-japon-etki.z: The pipes American pipe maker Rex Walden produces one by one in Texas, drawing on Danish and Japanese traditions and noted for their unusual surface finishes.

bpk.z: A Czech pipe factory whose roots trace back to the town of Proseč in 1842, which under socialism gathered all Czechoslovak pipe production as a state enterprise, and which was privatised in 1993 and took the name BPK.

sevres.z: France's royal porcelain manufactory, Sèvres, also produced a small number of porcelain pipe bowls in the eighteenth century; these pieces are counted among the hardest to identify in collections today.

jrn-larsen.z: Danish master Jørn Larsen (b. 1949), who came from locksmithing, is known for designing and building the machines he uses to make his pipes, not just the pipes themselves.

pollner.z: A German tobacconist and pipe workshop founded in 1878 in Bünde as a wood-turning shop, run by the same family for five generations, known for its OP-Studio pipes.

james-gilliam.z: An American craftsman who settled in Germany after retiring from the U.S. Navy and hand-carves pipes stamped JSEC, one at a time.

koncak.z: Founded in Eskişehir in 1934, one of Türkiye's oldest makers of finished meerschaum pipes. In 1990 the rights to the Vienna-based Andreas Bauer brand also passed to this family.

spanu.z: An Italian pipe workshop founded by Tommaso Spanu in Sardinia in 1979, carried on today in Sassari. Known for briar pipes clad in cork oak bark and for its work with woods other than briar.

g-f-b-damgasi.z: The G.F.B. stamp, read within an oval frame, is not a brand name but a material claim meaning 'genuine French briar'; it appears on American catalog pipes from the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

tabako-japonyada-tutun-ve-kiyim-gelenegi.b: Tabako: Japan's Tradition of Tobacco and Fine-Cutting
tabako-japonyada-tutun-ve-kiyim-gelenegi.z: Tabako is the Japanese word for tobacco. For centuries, the form smoked in pipes across the country was kizami-tabako, sliced hair-thin and consumed in the slender metal pipe called the kiseru.

one-cikan-virginia-harmanlari.z: A rundown of classic blends built around Virginia leaf: a family tree stretching from straight Virginias to Kentucky-, Perique-, and Oriental-enriched branches.

eski-dunhill-ile-yeni-dunhill-briyar-kum.b: Old Dunhill vs. New Dunhill: The Briar, Sandblast, and Mouthpiece Debate
eski-dunhill-ile-yeni-dunhill-briyar-kum.z: The factual basis of the difference between older and newer generations of Dunhill pipes: the shift in briar sources in the 1960s, the shallowing of sandblasting, and the evolution of mouthpiece shapes.

once-bicim-sonra-delme.z: A workshop method in which the pipe body is shaped before its holes are opened: freedom to design around the grain, offset by the alignment challenge of freehand drilling and the solutions developed for it.

dcapo.z: An Argentine brand from Pablo Minotti, working in Buenos Aires, who carries his family's Italian woodworking heritage into hand-carved briar pipes.

eds-hand-made.z: American pipes individually finished by hand by Edward Kolpin Sr. in Santa Monica, California, marked with a scratched signature instead of a stamp.

1976-jumbo-dunhiller-612-ve-622-sekiller.z: Unusually large bent pipes bearing the standard shape numbers 612 and 622, seen only in Dunhill's 1976 production. Discussed alongside the shape-numbering system's change and the production fluctuations at the end of the decade.

tobey-nevadada-tas-pipo-yapan-bir-kuzey-.b: Tobey: A Northern Paiute Stone Pipe Maker in Nevada
tobey-nevadada-tas-pipo-yapan-bir-kuzey-.z: Hilman Tobey, a Northern Paiute master living at the Reno-Sparks Indian Colony in Nevada, made ceremonial pipes; a short 2015 documentary filmed him passing the craft on to his apprentice.

manger.z: A German pipe maker founded by Anton Manger in 1957 in the village of Wollbach in Lower Franconia, spanning plain series models to hand-shaped freehand pipes.

fribourg-treyer.z: A long-established tobacconist house founded on London's Haymarket, traditionally dated to 1720, known for its snuff and its tobacco, and also remembered for pipes made under its own name.

klasik-pipo-sekilleri.z: An umbrella entry covering pipe making's classic shapes from Billiard to Oom Paul, the straight-bent distinction, and factory shape numbers.

sesa.z: Croatian-born Branko Sesa's one-man workshop in Turin; an Italian handmade pipe brand shaped by repair work, working briar, morta, and olive wood.

almanyada-uretilen-vintage-dunhill-tutun.b: Vintage Dunhill Tobaccos Made in Germany
almanyada-uretilen-vintage-dunhill-tutun.z: Some old Dunhill tobacco tins bear the words "Hergestellt in Deutschland" on the bottom. These tins are not fakes — they are German versions produced under license by the Hamburg firm Joh. Wilh. von Eicken.

royal-copenhagen.z: Copenhagen's royal porcelain factory, dating to 1775, also produced porcelain pipes for a short stretch from around 1970 into the mid-1980s.

dunhill-factory-white-spot-pipolarinin-y.b: Dunhill Factory: Where the White Spot Pipes Are Made
dunhill-factory-white-spot-pipolarinin-y.z: The journey of the workshop that produced Alfred Dunhill pipes, from Duke Street to Walthamstow in northeast London, and the stages applied there.

briyarin-kesfi-ilk-briyar-pipo-tartismas.b: The Discovery of Briar: The First Briar Pipe Debate
briyarin-kesfi-ilk-briyar-pipo-tartismas.z: There is no single inventor who turned briar into a pipe material. This article summarizes the rival answers to who first carved a briar pipe, and the sources these claims rest on.

tutun-nemi-ve-icim-oncesi-kurutma.z: A guide to the ideal moisture range for pipe tobacco, how pre-smoke drying is done, and how to revive tobacco that's dried out too much.

paronelli.z: An Italian family workshop founded in 1945 by Jean Marie Alberto Paronelli, making handmade briar pipes in Gavirate for three generations and founding a pipe museum in the same town.

brezilya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in Brazil, containing brief, factual entries for three brands.

civic.z: A London-based English pipe company born in 1921 out of Imperial Tobacco's fancy-goods division, which in 1928 spearheaded the founding of Cadogan Investments.

edwards-pipes.z: A one-man handmade pipe workshop founded in the early 2000s by Edward Czerny in Villach, Austria.

cope-bros-company-tutun-ureticisinden-ya.b: Cope Bros & Company: From Tobacco Maker to Publisher
cope-bros-company-tutun-ureticisinden-ya.z: Founded in Liverpool in 1848, Cope Bros & Company is remembered less for the tobaccos it made than for the magazines, booklets, and cards it printed; the firm left behind the widest body of documentation on Victorian tobacco culture.

ph-vigen.z: The signature of Danish master Jes Phillip Vigen Gertsen, whose pipes under his own name are a minority within his output, having spent many years producing top-tier lines for other brands.

dunhill-sekil-numaralari.z: The compiled list of shape numbers in Dunhill catalogues and how these numbers are read: group size, bit type, shape family, and the ODA/800 series.

bugunun-pipo-tutunu-piyasasi.z: The current shape of the pipe tobacco market, caught between the access the internet has opened up, closing blenders, and tightening regulation.

richard-carleton-hacker.z: Hacker, one of the most widely read names in pipe writing, is an American author and collector known for his books as well as a small signature series of pipes bearing his name.

prevost-pipes.z: A line of handmade pipes made in Tennessee by Pete Prevost, who moved from a career in music to the pipe bench; the same maker also serves as president of BriarWorks.

alfred-dunhillin-the-pipe-booku.z: Alfred Dunhill's 1924 book The Pipe Book brings the history of the pipe worldwide together in a single volume. Its being in print for over a century, and the gap between what readers expect from it and what they find, have made it the most talked-about title in the literature.

gajin.z: The brand Japanese pipe master Masato Hayafune uses for his handmade pipes. With an output of thirty to forty pieces a year, he is counted among the well-known names of independent pipe making in Japan.

stanwell.z: A Danish pipe brand founded in Copenhagen in 1942. By carrying shapes designed by renowned Danish masters into mass production, it brought the Danish school to a wide audience.

pipsan-pipolari.z: A business operating in Istanbul's Mercan district, counted among Turkey's earliest addresses for series pipe production. It added a briar series called Dapper in 2005 alongside its wild-pear pipes.

fransa-pipo-markalari-dizini-1.z: The A-to-S records of French pipemaking: ninety-two brief entries running from the factories of Saint-Claude to the clay and meerschaum houses of Paris. The second part of the directory covers the remaining brands.

sanchopipa.z: Sanchopipa, a Chilean maker of handcrafted pipes from native woods, is a small-scale example of the place non-briar woods and reclaimed timber hold in pipemaking.

hardcastle.z: A brand founded in Walthamstow, London, one of the well-known names among mid-tier English pipes, which eventually came under the Dunhill umbrella.

nate-king-yaris-pistinden-tezgaha-uzanan.b: Nate King: From the Racetrack to the Pipe Bench
nate-king-yaris-pistinden-tezgaha-uzanan.z: American pipe maker Nate King, based in Indianapolis, brings the precision habits he built in motorsport and aviation to the briar bench.

chicago-pipo-yapim-semineri-programi.b: The Chicago Pipe Making Seminar Curriculum
chicago-pipo-yapim-semineri-programi.z: The written outline of the pipe-making seminar held as part of the Chicagoland pipe show; a one-day course in which participants finish a pre-drilled briar block while learning basic workshop skills.

micah-redmond.z: An American pipe craftsman born in Jacksonville and now settled in Nashville, who makes pipes under his own name while working at BriarWorks.

tinder-box.z: Founded in 1928 in Santa Monica and later expanded across America, the Tinder Box tobacconist chain is known for having pipes stamped with its own name made to order by workshops in various countries.

dark-fired-kentucky.z: A dark American tobacco variety cured with oak and hickory smoke in closed barns. It is used as a component that adds strength and a smoky note to pipe blends.

tim-west.z: American briar pipe maker Tim West, working in Columbus, Ohio, is known for his plateau-topped freehand shapes and the TIMWEST stamp; the pipe-repair parts firm J. H. Lowe & Co., founded in 1947, is also under his company today.

kaywoodie-sekil-numaralari.z: The periods, letter suffixes, and production ranges that can be inferred from the shape numbers stamped on the shanks of Kaywoodie pipes.

joao-reis.z: A carpenter by training who trained under Danish makers and put Portugal on the map of contemporary artisan pipe making, working out of Lisbon.

comoys.z: A British briar pipe brand founded in London by a family originally from the Jura region of France, known by the mark "London Made"; it came under the Cadogan umbrella after 1929.

ross-arundel.z: The name Peter Ross, a tobacconist in the town of Arundel in Sussex, gave to the briar pipes he sold by mail; the bodies were made largely at the Orlik workshop in London.

santambrogio.z: An Italian pipe workshop founded near Varese in Gavirate, which began production powered by a water mill and has remained in the hands of the same family for three generations.

bertram.z: An American pipe workshop founded in Washington, known for making pipes for the capital's political and artistic circles, which closed in 1977.

churchwarden.z: Churchwarden is a pipe type in which the bowl shape is left open but the mouthpiece is kept unusually long. The long stem lets the smoke cool before reaching the mouth.

renaissance-pipes.z: A small-scale American briar bench run by theoretical physicist Thomas Bahder, reportedly born in Maryland in 1999 and developed under the remote guidance of Trever Talbert.

layton-pipes.z: An American handmade pipe workshop Clark Layton runs alone in Pennsylvania, in production since 2012; known for hard sandblasts paired with contrast staining.

morta.z: Morta is semi-fossilized oak wood that has lain buried in a peat bog or riverbed for thousands of years without oxygen; a pipe bowl material known for its neutrality of taste and high resistance to burning.

dunhills-blends-harman-katalogu-ve-ambal.b: Dunhill's Blends: The Blend Catalogue and Packaging History
dunhills-blends-harman-katalogu-ve-ambal.z: The lesser-discussed side of the Dunhill catalogue: tobacco presented in unusual forms such as cartridges and travel packs, how bespoke recipes were written into the ledger, and what changed when blending moved to Belfast in 1981.

lcs-briars.z: Simon Bosko's one-man workshop in London, known for specializing in 9 mm filtered pipes and for its star-based grading system.

dil-isirmasi.z: A guide explaining the thermal and chemical causes of tongue bite — the burning and irritation felt on the tongue during pipe smoking — along with prevention techniques and the effect of blend choice.

svenska-rokpipfabriken.z: A family business founded in Lerum in 1931, regarded as Sweden's first briar pipe factory, which ended production in 1979; known by the abbreviation SRF.

portekiz-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands made in Portugal or signed by Portuguese makers; contains short, factual entries for five brands.

dr-grabow-serileri-yillar-icinde-degisen.b: Dr. Grabow Lines: How the Model Names Changed Over the Years
dr-grabow-serileri-yillar-icinde-degisen.z: A summary of the naming system running from Dr. Grabow's numbered series of the Chicago era to the model names of the Sparta years, such as Viscount, Eldorado, and Westbrook.

batiya-dogru-amerikan-el-yapimi-pipo-sah.b: Go West: The American Handmade Pipe Scene
batiya-dogru-amerikan-el-yapimi-pipo-sah.z: A magazine article by Erwin Van Hove that introduces European readers to the birth of artisan pipe making in the USA; its central argument is that American pipe making has no single national style.

mcguire-kaliforniyanin-az-bilinen-bir-pi.z: The brief story of American master Mac McGuire, who worked around Los Angeles in the 1970s and early 1980s, with output limited to a few hundred pipes.

porsche-design.z: The pipe line of the design company founded by Porsche 911 designer Ferdinand Alexander Porsche; produced first by Oldenkott, then in the 2000s by the Dutch firm Gubbels.

avustralya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands made in Australia or directly linked to the country, with short, factual entries for five brands.

florov-pipes.z: The one-man workshop in Illinois of Alex Florov, who trained as a furniture restorer in Moscow, settled in the USA in 1992, and took up pipemaking in 2004.

danimarka-pipo-markalari-dizini-1.z: An alphabetical directory of Danish pipe brands, workshops and sub-brands: 90 entries running from A. H. to Ove Jensen, each given as a short profile.

wagner-brick-church-pipo-dukkani-ve-kend.b: Wagner: The Brick Church Pipe Shop and Its Own-Name Pipes
wagner-brick-church-pipo-dukkani-ve-kend.z: The Brick Church Pipe Shop that Irving Wagner founded in New Jersey, its own-name pipes, and its importing business in the 1970s.

invicta-briars.z: An English workshop whose origins trace to a postwar pipe repair shop in Chatham, which began making its own pipes after 1974.

jason-patrick-fotografciliktan-briyar-te.b: Jason Patrick: An American Maker Who Traded Photography for the Briar Bench
jason-patrick-fotografciliktan-briyar-te.z: Working in Illinois, Jason Patrick turned what began as a hobby in 2019 into a full-time craft within a few years, making him a contemporary American maker.

klein-pfeifendesign.z: The workshop of German-born master Peter Klein, who began as a hobby in 1988 and moved it to Denmark in 2007, producing a few hundred one-off pipes a year.

briyar-ticaretinin-unutulan-ureticileri-.b: The Forgotten Makers and Brands of the Briar Trade
briyar-ticaretinin-unutulan-ureticileri-.z: Hundreds of workshops and factories that made pipes from briar closed, leaving behind little more than a few letters stamped on a shank. This article looks at which records the trail of that lost industry can be traced through.

giacomo-penzo.z: The handmade pipe workshop founded in 2015 by Vicenza-born industrial designer Giacomo Penzo, and the pipe-specialist role the maker has held at Peterson since 2019.

constantinos-zissis.z: A self-taught Greek pipe maker working on the island of Corfu, crafting pipes one at a time from Greek briar and the island's own olive wood.

meksika-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in Mexico or manufactured and distributed there; includes brief, factual entries for three brands.

ozgur-pipe.z: A meerschaum pipe maker based in Eskişehir. By its own account carving block stone since 2008, it stands out for classic and figural pipes as well as replacement meerschaum bowls fitted to the Falcon and Kirsten systems.

velasco-smoking-pipes.z: A small workshop founded in Athens in 2009 by Michael Pipinis-Aliagas, producing freehand pipes from Greek briar and olive wood.

grechukhin-g-damgasi-ve-pipolari.b: Grechukhin: The G Stamp and Its Pipes
grechukhin-g-damgasi-ve-pipolari.z: The single-letter mark Russian master Vladimir Grechukhin uses on the pipes he produces in Saint Petersburg, the mark's origin in the Fyodorov workshop, and its anniversary series.

pipo-terimleri-sozlugu.z: An introductory entry explaining how the vocabulary of pipes and tobacco came together: term families, the origin of shape names, and commonly misunderstood concepts.

urup.z: Danish craftsman Arne Urup's workshop built on meerschaum and Baltic amber; known for lyre-shaped Congress pipes.

peter-fischer.z: German-born, working alone since the mid-1970s in the old town of Schaffhausen; known for his distinctive calabash interpretation and hunting pipes.

pipe-lon.z: A pipe shop that operated in the port of St. Thomas in the US Virgin Islands, serving as a bridge for Danish freehands entering America, and the stamp bearing its own name.

stefanou-pipex.z: A Greek family workshop founded near Epidaurus in 1981 by Georgios Stefanou, who had trained at the Brigham factory in Canada; today run together with his sons.

aristocob.z: An American system pipe with a replaceable corncob bowl fitted inside a metal shank; born in Michigan in the 1960s, production ended in 1983.

mamut-fildisinden-bir-sibirya-piposu-dun.b: A Siberian Pipe Made of Mammoth Ivory: From the Dunhill Museum to Auction
mamut-fildisinden-bir-sibirya-piposu-dun.z: The trail of a mammoth-ivory Siberian pipe from Alfred Dunhill's collection, pictured on the dust jacket of The Pipe Book, goes cold after the shop was bombed in 1941. The piece's recognition in the US and its arrival at auction in 2020 is a documented example of how provenance tracing actually works.

pipo-hakkinda-yanlis-bilinenler.z: A collection of errors frequently repeated in Turkish-language sources and in the pipe community: mistakes about the material's name, health misconceptions, filter expectations, and beliefs about what's in tobacco.

herbert-edward-dunhill.z: Alfred Dunhill's youngest brother and the company's financial mind. He joined the firm in 1912 and ran Dunhill by post from his homes in Italy and Monaco from 1928 until his death in 1950; his legacy became a charitable trust devoted to tuberculosis research.

saul-salzhauer.z: An American maker who, from 1951 on, hand-carved freehand pipes at the workshop of the Jelling tobacco shop in Newark, having learned the craft from his father during the Great Depression.

frank-burla-chicago-pipo-fuarinin-kurucu.b: Frank Burla: Founder of the Chicago Pipe Show
frank-burla-chicago-pipo-fuarinin-kurucu.z: Antique pipe collector and retired FBI agent Frank Burla's effort to grow one of the world's largest pipe shows out of a small gathering in his own front room.

eric-weaver.z: An American craftsman who works alone in the town of Washburn, Wisconsin, signing his pipes SeaSmoke and also making pottery in the same workshop.

alexander-tupitsyn.z: Russian pipe maker Alexander Tupitsyn, one of the three founders of PS Studio, is known for neoclassical shapes that combine Russian workshop discipline with the Danish line.

thuner-pipes.z: A one-man Swedish workshop founded in 2005 by Ronny Thunér, interpreting the Scandinavian freehand tradition through his signature Cobra shape and rustic surface work that extends onto the mouthpiece.

thurmann-piber.z: Thurmann Piber is the Danish workshop founded in 1976 by Bjørn Thurmann, son of a Copenhagen tobacconist family; trained on both London and Chicago counters, Thurmann is known for the pipe-making handbook he published in 1987 and for the production he kept up on the island of Bornholm after 2005.

liverpool.z: A straight pipe shape known for a long, round-sectioned shank paired with a short tapered mouthpiece; one of the four members of the Canadian family, counted among Billiard's long-shanked derivatives.

rudolfs-patent.z: A stamp made in England in the early twentieth century, whose layout closely echoes Peterson's patent pipes and which is known from only a handful of surviving examples with a forked-slot mouthpiece.

dg-pipe.z: The one-man workshop of Italian pipe maker Gabriele Dal Fiume, who works near Bologna and produces only a few dozen one-of-a-kind pipes a year.

stout-kaliforniyali-bir-tek-kisilik-tezg.z: Producing roughly a hundred pipes a year from Mark Stout's workshop in Southern California, moving between classic shapes and freehand work — a contemporary American signature.

en-eski-dunhill-hangisi.z: Tracing the oldest object to bear the Dunhill name, dating pipes from 1910-1918 by their mouthpiece stamps, and discussing the earliest known examples of the LB and ODA lines.

rostiak.z: A French pipe workshop run single-handedly by Joseph Rimbaud in the village of Les Crozets in the Jura; known for its light bodies and shapes that step outside classic molds.

19-yuzyil-pipo-harmanlari-tagsis-ve-tari.b: 19th-Century Pipe Blends: Adulteration and Recipe Books
19-yuzyil-pipo-harmanlari-tagsis-ve-tari.z: The pipe tobacco recipes found in Victorian-era trade manuals, the era's adulteration problem, and the first official inspection regulations that problem gave rise to.

svendborg-piber.z: Svendborg Piber is a Danish pipe brand founded in 1970 through the purchase of a closed factory on the island of Fyn; it grew from a partnership between two pipemakers and a banker, moved into mass production through a German wholesale connection, and changed hands several times after its founders left.

saint-claude.z: Saint-Claude, in France's Jura mountains, is a town that grew from a woodturners' settlement on a pilgrimage route into the world's pipe capital, and is known as the place where the briar pipe industry was established.

krska.z: The workshop of Czech master Karel Krška, who trained in Brno; known for freehands that bring out ring grain and for classic bulldog interpretations.

pipo-damgalari-ve-logolari.z: The stamps struck into the shank and the logos set into the stem are the primary evidence linking a pipe to its brand, quality grade, and period of manufacture. This entry explains the types of markings and how to read them.

pipo-sozcugunun-kokeni.b: The Origin of the Word Pipe
pipo-sozcugunun-kokeni.z: The pipe/pipa/Pfeife family in Western languages comes from a Latin verb imitating a bird's chirp, and the word originally named a musical instrument. Its attachment to the tobacco tool is documented only from the late 16th century.

armellini.z: An Italian family workshop operating in Barasso, in the province of Varese. The business Mauro Armellini founded in 1959 is carried on today by his daughter Vilma Armellini and grandson Matteo.

gabrieli-pipes-mutfaktan-tezgaha-gecen-b.b: Gabrieli Pipes: A Pennsylvania Maker Who Moved from the Kitchen to the Bench
gabrieli-pipes-mutfaktan-tezgaha-gecen-b.z: A one-person bench Dan Chlebove founded in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania; named after the master's son, known for pipes shaped without a lathe, no more than sixty a year.

pipo-sekillerinin-siniflandirilmasi.z: An entry explaining how pipe shapes are named, how they group by family logic, and how factory shape-number and group systems work.

pibe-dan.z: Opened in Copenhagen in 1943 and operating until 1991, Pibe-Dan is a shop and brand known for its own Shape-Reformed series, which carried most of postwar Denmark's pipe masters into its storefront.

japon-pipo-terimleri-sozlugu.z: The Japanese vocabulary surrounding the kiseru and its smoking set: the pipe's parts, types of case and pouch, the sections of the tabako-bon, and the names for the set hung from the sash.

dunhill-shell-briarin-tarihi.b: The History of the Dunhill Shell Briar
dunhill-shell-briarin-tarihi.z: The oil-curing method that sets Dunhill's sandblasted Shell finish apart, what the patent record says, and how the depth of the blast changed over a century.

karbon-tabakasi-ve-raybalama.z: A maintenance guide explaining the function of the protective carbon layer (cake) that builds up in a briar pipe bowl with smoking, its ideal thickness, and how to thin it with a reamer.

muzayededeki-bir-dunhill-es-kunye-ile-fo.b: A Dunhill ES at Auction: Where the Listing and the Photo Disagree
muzayededeki-bir-dunhill-es-kunye-ile-fo.z: An online auction listing described a pipe as a 1923 Dunhill ES, but the stem writing and the body's proportions did not match. The case is cited as an example of how far stamp reading can take you.

borkum-riff.z: An aromatic pipe tobacco brand born in Sweden and produced in Denmark, named after a lighthouse station in the North Sea.

rex-poggenpohl-amerikan-pipo-yapimcilari.b: Rex Poggenpohl: Compiler of the American Pipe Makers List
rex-poggenpohl-amerikan-pipo-yapimcilari.z: The record collector, amateur pipe maker, and show organizer J. Rex Poggenpohl's list documenting American pipe craftsmen one by one, and his long tenure at the Chicago show.

augsburger.z: An American maker who made pipes alone in Illinois from the late 1970s to the late 1980s. Production stayed small, and most of his pipes are unstamped.

savas-sonrasi-dunhill-oda-800-serisi.z: The ODA large-bowl pipes Dunhill introduced in 1950, and the place the 800-series shape numbers assigned to them hold in collecting.

london-castle-pipes.z: A small English pipe workshop that supplied a single London tobacconist throughout the twentieth century, with the customer choosing the stem for each pipe.

gustav-fischer.z: A pipe sculptor raised in Austria and settled in Boston, known for meerschaum carvings he left unsigned.

former.z: The nickname and brand of Hans Jonny Nielsen. After rising to workshop foreman at W. Ø. Larsen, he began producing under his own name in 1972, developed the Bentley line in Switzerland, and later returned to Denmark.

lepeltier.z: A small-scale American workshop in Vermont producing double-walled, glazed, and decorated clay pipes.

janpipes.z: The stamp Czech pipe maker Jan Klouček has used since 1999; a workshop drawing on the French tradition that runs classic series alongside original designs side by side.

bilye-hazneli-fransiz-art-deco-pipolari.b: French Art Deco Pipes with a Ball-Shaped Chamber
bilye-hazneli-fransiz-art-deco-pipolari.z: Small pipes made in Paris workshops in the first quarter of the twentieth century, featuring a removable silver or gold ball at the center. The cotton packed inside the ball was an early attempt at filtering.

jonsson.z: Swedish carpenter Lars Jönsson's workshop, which began with his meeting Tom Eltang in 1998 and became independent under the Lomma stamp in 2011.

roush.z: American maker Larry Roush's handmade briar pipes bearing his own name, produced in Ohio and known for silver and gold work from a jeweler's hand.

kharitonov-moskovadan-cagdas-bir-artisan.b: Kharitonov: A Contemporary Artisan Signature from Moscow
kharitonov-moskovadan-cagdas-bir-artisan.z: Moscow-based Andrey Kharitonov's move from pipe repair to pipemaking, the freehand shapes he builds without a lathe, and his style built on carved texture paired with contrast staining.

old-nellie-pipes-joe-nelsonin-wisconsin-.b: Old Nellie Pipes: Joe Nelson's Wisconsin Workshop
old-nellie-pipes-joe-nelsonin-wisconsin-.z: Old Nellie Pipes is the brand of Joe Nelson, a carpenter, luthier, and pipe maker working in the Fond du Lac area of Wisconsin. The precision he brings from guitar making shows in his clean lines and mother-of-pearl inlay signature.

pipo-kulupleri.z: How local pipe clubs operate, how they come together under national federations, and the structure of the international slow-smoking championships run under the CIPC umbrella.

pipe-tristan.z: A handmade pipe workshop in Ardèche, southeastern France, run singlehandedly by Tristan Lefebvre, known for its Granite and Ammonite finishes and its own Chestnut shape.

jobey.z: An American pipe brand of disputed origin whose ownership changed hands repeatedly over the twentieth century. Known for the screw-in Jobey Link fitting joining stem and shank, and for its Jobey Dansk line made in Denmark in the seventies.

isvec-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in Sweden or mentioned in the country's brand records, with short, factual entries for three brands.

bay-pipe.z: A Turkish workshop brand in Eskişehir that carves block meerschaum. Founded by Emre Mangaltepe, it is known for figural carving and portrait pipes worked from photographs.

siyahi.z: A name appearing in international pipe brand compilations as a Turkish-origin meerschaum pipe brand, but one that has left no documentation regarding its workshop or founding year. The only concrete detail on record is that some of its pipes were made on the Isle of Man.

parkin-danimarkaya-atfedilen-kimligi-bel.b: Parkin: A Pipe Stamp of Uncertain Identity Attributed to Denmark
parkin-danimarkaya-atfedilen-kimligi-bel.z: The Parkin stamp, encountered only on the secondhand market, with no known founder or workshop, generally classed in records as Danish in origin, and the examples known to survive.

design-by-franz.z: The brand of the workshop founded in 1998 in the canton of Aargau by Swiss architect Franz von Matt, known for its design-focused pipes. Production ended in summer 2007.

jud.z: A handmade pipe brand made under his own name by Daniel Jud, a physician living in the Swiss canton of Thurgau, known for its metal detailing.

steven-johnson-wanamaker-magazasinda-pip.b: Steven Johnson: The American Master Who Made Pipes at Wanamaker's
steven-johnson-wanamaker-magazasinda-pip.z: An American master who ran the Wilke branch inside Philadelphia's Wanamaker store in the 1970s and 1980s, signing his pipes with the S. JOHNSON stamp.

enricoro.z: The Italian pipe bench of watchmaker Enrico Marola, based in Vercelli, who names his craft after his profession and works classic shapes with hand tools.

estate-pipo-kavrami-terimin-anlami-ve-ta.b: The Concept of the Estate Pipe: Meaning and Debate of the Term
estate-pipo-kavrami-terimin-anlami-ve-ta.z: Covers the origin of the term "estate pipe" as used in the secondhand pipe trade, which pipes it covers, and the ongoing debate over whether the name is accurate.

adam-davidson.z: An American handmade briar pipe maker with a background in industrial design, based in South Carolina and known for rounded signature shapes such as the Fig and the Amoeba.

codger-harmanlari.z: The collective name for the Burley-based classic pipe tobaccos synonymous with US drugstore and supermarket shelves. Prince Albert, Carter Hall, Half and Half, and Captain Black are the family's best-known examples.

grunewald-pipes.z: A father-and-son bench Paul Greenwood founded in Indiana in 2022, known for its wooden-stemmed pipes inspired by The Lord of the Rings.

bertoldi.z: Bertoldi, founded by two brothers in 1984 in the town of Timbó in Santa Catarina state, is a family business that grew from a ten-pipe-a-day workshop into Brazil's best-known pipe maker.

avusturya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands of Austrian origin or noted in Austrian records, with short, factual entries for thirteen brands.

kumlama.z: A finishing method that uses pressurized abrasive to strip away briar's soft grain while leaving the harder grain standing; its history, workshop equipment, and application principles.

doctor-of-pipes-ve-master-of-pipes-odull.b: The Doctor of Pipes and Master of Pipes Awards
doctor-of-pipes-ve-master-of-pipes-odull.z: Two honors established by the Chicagoland Pipe Collectors Club in 1998 and 2017 are regarded as the only known regular program that recognizes lifetime contribution in the pipe community. Both being tied to a single club has made their continuity a subject of debate.

vardry-pipes.z: A small-scale American workshop operating out of Cleveland, South Carolina, finishing every pipe by hand as a one-of-a-kind piece.

martin-romijn.z: A Dutch craftsman who moved from decades of stonecutting into pipe making in 2016; known for organic freehand shapes guided by the material.

bowles-son-ltd.z: A family firm founded in 1888 that distributed wholesale and retail tobacco and pipes from Cardiff's Butetown district across South East Wales. It passed into history when sold in 1979.

dunhill-agizliklari-ozgunluk-belirtileri.b: Dunhill Mouthpieces: Marks of Authenticity and Their Limits
dunhill-agizliklari-ozgunluk-belirtileri.z: Why the mouthpiece is considered the distinguishing part of a Dunhill pipe, what the white dot and the registration number stamped on the mouthpiece can and cannot tell you, and why it is difficult to know whether a mouthpiece truly belongs to that pipe.

william-demuth-company.z: An American pipe firm founded in New York in 1862, known for its WDC stamp set inside an inverted triangle, which moved from meerschaum carving into series briar production.

coronilla-koku.z: A pipe material made from the root of the Scutia buxifolia tree, native to South America's Río de la Plata basin, exposed when riverbeds recede.

pipolarin-kralicesi-lule-tasinin-itibari.b: The Queen of Pipes: Meerschaum's Prestige and Antique Legacy
pipolarin-kralicesi-lule-tasinin-itibari.z: Meerschaum was regarded as the 'queen of pipes' throughout the 19th century. This entry examines what the title rested on, how the founding legend stands up against the archival record, how the golden age came to a close, and the history of antique collecting.

kw-pipes.z: The brand of Dane-influenced freehand pipes made part-time in the early 2000s by American maker Kirk Walden, who moved from pipe repair into carving.

bogni.z: An Italian family workshop founded in the town of Gavirate in Varese, known since 1963 for its rustic surface work. Also known for its pipes made from Calabrian olive wood.

aromatik-harmanlar.z: A family of pipe tobaccos in which flavors and scents outside tobacco itself — vanilla, cherry, caramel — are added. Aromatics are considered to make up the largest share of pipe tobacco sales worldwide.

briyar-devrimi-ve-saint-claude.z: The history of briar's rise as the primary pipemaking material in the mid-19th century in the French town of Saint-Claude, and its eclipsing of clay and meerschaum.

bartlett-pipe-co.z: An American patent pipe built around the idea of lighting the bowl from the bottom; its 1980 patent, US 4,235,252, was taken over by The Bartlett Pipe Company in the 1990s.

trever-talbertin-ince-bicimlendirme-yont.z: The intermediate stage where a drilled briar body takes on its final profile: how fine shaping — carried out with a sanding disc, carving machines, and hand files — is organized at Trever Talbert's workshop.

kalabas-pipo.z: A two-piece pipe made from a curved, dried gourd body fitted with a removable meerschaum bowl insert. Known for an exceptionally cool, dry smoke thanks to the large air chamber beneath the bowl.

one-cikan-sark-tutunu-harmanlari.z: A survey of pipe blends defined by Oriental leaf: the two main branches, with and without Latakia, their best-known examples, and the gap left by discontinued names.

mac-baren.z: A Danish pipe tobacco maker, tracing its roots to 1826 and known worldwide for its Mixture blend. It remained in the Halberg family for 137 years before joining the Scandinavian Tobacco Group in 2024.

amorelli.z: An Italian workshop founded in Caltanissetta by Salvatore "Totò" Amorelli, working exclusively with Sicilian briar and known for the gold band set between the shank and the mouthpiece.

ernie-markle-pipes.z: The signature of Ernie Markle, working out of a one-man home workshop in Scottsdale, Arizona; known for entirely hand-shaped briar pipes that lean close to the Danish line.

comoys-tarihi-ve-pipolarini-tarihlendirm.b: Comoy's History and a Guide to Dating Its Pipes
comoys-tarihi-ve-pipolarini-tarihlendirm.z: Comoy's pipes have no mark giving the production year directly; dating rests on the shape of the brand stamp, the origin stamp, the three-piece 'C' inlaid on the mouthpiece, and the series name.

ozark-mountain-briars-yedi-yillik-bir-am.b: Ozark Mountain Briars: Seven Years of an American Workshop
ozark-mountain-briars-yedi-yillik-bir-am.z: A small-scale American pipe workshop from the Ozark mountains, founded by David Johnson in 2004 after a workplace accident and closed in 2011 for health reasons.

erin-go-bragh-irlanda-sloganini-tasiyan-.b: Erin Go Bragh: A Pipe Series Bearing An Irish Slogan
erin-go-bragh-irlanda-sloganini-tasiyan-.z: How an old slogan meaning "Ireland forever" became a brand name in the pipe world, and the Italian-made Erin Go Bragh series reportedly introduced in 2020.

tanzanya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands associated with Tanzania; contains brief profiles for the two brands on record.

mauro-cateni.z: Long thought to be an Italian pipe maker, actually a German brand registered by a Hamburg wholesaler in 1979. Its pipes are believed to have been sourced from Italy.

japon-tutun-esyalari-kaynakcasi.z: A survey of the main articles, books, and exhibition catalogues written on the kiseru, pipe cases, tobacco pouches, and smoking trays; a reference list showing which journals and museum publications the field's literature has accumulated in.

adler.z: The story of the Adler workshop, which began in Óbuda and continued in Pest, producing Hungary's best-known meerschaum pipes across three generations.

chr-henrik.z: The name Danish advertising designer Henrik Christian Christensen used as a pipe maker; he produced a limited number of hand-shaped pipes from around 1965 until 1984.

todd-johnson.z: A contemporary American pipe maker trained in the Danish school and drawing on classical Greek aesthetics, whose workshop produced a large number of makers who went on to work under their own names.

rustication.z: A method of creating a rough, pitted texture on a pipe bowl and often the shank using hand tools; the classic way to make use of flawed briar and to give a pipe a different grip.

cavalier.z: A rare shape whose shank extends down beneath the bowl, collecting moisture through a removable cap at the end and letting the pipe stand upright on a table.

sutliff-tobacco.z: An American manufacturer founded, per industry records, in 1849 in San Francisco; it moved production to Richmond in 1953 and is regarded as the backbone of the bulk pipe tobacco market.

s-bang.z: A Danish pipe workshop opened in Copenhagen in 1968 that, despite bearing its founder's name, owed its reputation to two master carvers, and closed in 2019.

hedelson.z: The freehand pipes American cutter Glen Hedelson shaped in the 1970s at Michael Kabik's workshops were stamped under his own name; Hedelson thereby turned into a brand name of its own.

bs-pipes.z: An Istanbul briar pipe workshop signed with the initials of maker Birol Salman's own name. Salman is also known for preparing pipe tobacco blends sold under the Bosphorus name.

falk-ve-cift-kanalli-pipo-patenti.b: Falk and the Double-Flue Pipe Patent
falk-ve-cift-kanalli-pipo-patenti.z: American inventor George L. Falk's 1958 double-flue pipe design aimed to separate saliva from the smoke path and channel it into a separate reservoir.

jelling.z: An American tobacconist opened in Newark in 1919 that had pipes bearing its own name made by other workshops, closing in the mid-1970s.

bard-hansen.z: A pipemaker working under the name Tabago in Bergen, Norway, who carried the craft forward by taking over the bench of the Lillehammer pipe factory, which closed in 1979, and became known for pipes with briar mouthpieces.

kent-pipes.z: A Danish workshop in Aarhus run by Kent Rasmussen, who moved from contemporary art to the pipe bench, and whose pipes are graded with star and butterfly stamps.

h-jones-easyloader.z: A store-brand pipe line made in England for the American Tinder Box chain in the 1970s and 1980s, known for its broadly beveled bowl rim.

senlar.z: An American handmade pipe brand produced in Wally Larsen's Minnesota basement workshop, known for a rustic surface resembling tree bark.

abe-herbaugh.z: An American artisan who moved from electric guitar building to pipe making, raised in West Virginia and known for pipes bearing his own name.

nimrod-cakmaklari.z: A family of bolt-shaped pipe lighters patented in 1946 by a Cincinnati screw and lathe-parts manufacturer. Its history, working principle, and the difficulty of dating examples.

parks-pipes.z: Michael Parks's one-man workshop in Bowmanville, Ontario, Canada, producing a limited number of pipes that combine classic English shapes with exotic materials.

dr-grabow-efsanesi-bir-markanin-adini-al.b: The Dr. Grabow Legend: The Physician Behind The Brand Name
dr-grabow-efsanesi-bir-markanin-adini-al.z: The family story behind how one of America's most widely known mass-produced pipe brands, Dr. Grabow, took its name from a Chicago physician — and the verified brand history surrounding that story.

bacchiega.z: Giacomo Bacchiega, an Italian maker who makes pipes without running a commercial workshop, known in the community more for his collecting and his interest in Castello.

ted-bihlmaier.z: The brand of American maker Ted Bihlmaier, who took to the bench after encountering his father's pipe collection; known for hand-crafted briar pipes, each made individually and avoiding standard shapes.

castoldi.z: Italian pipes made individually by hand by Enrico Castoldi in his Milan workshop; a recent workshop built on classic shapes and small-to-medium sizes.

romanya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical index of pipe brands originating in Romania; contains a brief, factual entry for the single recorded workshop.

skoda-pipes.z: A one-man American workshop run by Joseph Skoda in New York state, known for its four-digit stamp numbering and Alpha grading.

cassano-pipes.z: An Italian mass-production pipe factory founded by the Ceresa family in the Lombardy town of Cassano Magnago, moving from contract manufacturing to its own brand and operating for more than a century.

charatan.z: An English pipe house founded in London in 1863. Counted among the legendary names of the English school for its 'Charatan's Make' stamp, symbolizing fully handmade production, and for the top grades of the Lane era.

grants-pipe-shop.z: The history of Grant's Pipe Shop, said to trace back to 1849 California Gold Rush and considered San Francisco's oldest tobacconist, and its 2012 lease dispute.

cornelius-manz.z: A self-taught German pipe maker working in Reutlingen, known for a deliberately small output, flawless mouthpiece work, and organic shapes close to the Danish school.

ib-olsen.z: A Danish pipe maker trained at the S. Bang bench whose work was stamped under his own name because it was considered too free-form, and of which very few examples remain today.

longchamp.z: A French brand Jean Cassegrain founded in Paris in 1948, known for pipes with bowls and shanks covered in leather. Pipe production was abandoned in the late 1970s, while the company continued in leather goods.

pipo-icicilerinin-hicivli-portreleri.z: The course of the print tradition that portrayed the pipe smoker as a ridiculous, disheveled, exaggerated figure, running from Flemish tavern scenes to the golden age of British caricature and 19th-century lithography.

comoys-sekil-numaralari.z: What the shape numbers stamped on Comoy's pipe shanks reveal, what the M, P, C, and F letters and size abbreviations following the number stand for, and the limits of collector shape charts.

iwan-ries-co.z: Founded in Chicago in 1857 as E. Hoffman & Co., reportedly held by the same family for five generations, and one of the most established tobacconists in the United States for commissioning pipes under its own name.

italyan-el-yapimi-piposunun-kisa-tarihi.b: A Short History of the Italian Handmade Pipe
italyan-el-yapimi-piposunun-kisa-tarihi.z: Thirty years stretching from the Castello workshop founded in Cantù in 1947 to the Caminetto, Ascorti, and Radice benches that multiplied in Cucciago; a summary of how the Italian workshop pipe built its own style through a chain of masters and apprentices.

mitchell-thomas-trading-co.z: A Memphis-based American import and distribution company founded in 1998; besides its own eponymous pipe line, it also owns older brands such as Aldo Velani and Sasieni.

danish-design.z: A phrase that is both a style name describing the Danish pipe aesthetic that formed in the mid-twentieth century and a stamp struck on some pipes, not tied to any single manufacturer.

latakia.z: An oriental tobacco that is sun-dried and then smoke-cured over aromatic wood and scrub for weeks. Its smoky, leathery, spiced notes make it the signature component of English blends.

reid-robertson.z: A brief profile of American pipe maker Reid Robertson, who set up his bench in North Carolina in 2021 and now works in New Mexico, and of the Robertson Pipes brand.

iyi-bir-briyar-pipoyu-ne-belirler-birinc.b: What Makes a Good Briar Pipe: Part One, Material
iyi-bir-briyar-pipoyu-ne-belirler-birinc.z: The material-focused first installment of a 1985 Pipe Smoker series: period criteria on the age and grain of the briar, the type of burl, curing time, and geographic origin.

holger-frickert.z: German pipe maker Holger Frickert, partner and designer at Dan Pipe, interprets classic shapes with Danish sensibility under the "Handcut by Holger" stamp.

samvel-mirijanyan.z: An independent Armenian master, coming from jewelry-making, who first repaired old pipes before turning to making his own briar pipes.

arthur-leonard.z: An American tobacco shop founded in Portland in 1936 and closed in 1989. It owed its reputation less to its customers than to the direct relationships it built with its suppliers, the great English pipe houses.

mickles.z: American handmade pipes bearing the mark of Clarence Mickles, who worked in Park Forest, Illinois; known for large bowls, rustic surfaces, and the maker's repair work.

butera.z: An American brand carrying the name of Michael Butera, who moved from insurance work to the pipe bench; regarded as one of the milestones of American handmade pipe making thanks to craftsmanship modeled on top European makers.

kenan-ahmet-pipes.z: A handmade briar pipe workshop run single-handedly by Kenan Ahmet in Küçükçekmece, Istanbul; known for its own-design shapes and accent materials, with most information about it based on the maker's own account.

aztek-seramik-pipolari.z: Fired-clay Aztec pipes from pre-conquest central Mexico. A tradition known from finds at the Tlatelolco excavations, distinguished by animal-shaped bowls and a one-piece shank.

dogal-finis-pipolar.z: A natural finish is a briar pipe finished by sanding and polishing alone, with no stain applied. This entry explains how the surface is prepared, how the light honey tone darkens over time, what staining actually does, and why putty fills stand out on a natural surface.

armentrout-col-kasabasindan-cikan-bir-am.b: Armentrout: An American Bench Out of a Desert Town
armentrout-col-kasabasindan-cikan-bir-am.z: The workshop of Nathan Armentrout, working in Lancaster, California, which grew from hobby scale into a one-man bench producing a limited number of handmade pipes.

g-batson-pipes.z: The American workshop Grant Batson runs in Nashville, having moved from guitar making to the pipe bench.

benni-pipes.z: The brand under which Danish maker Benni Jørgensen produces pipes under his own name. Jørgensen made straight-grain pipes for W. Ø. Larsen for more than twenty years, only moving to his own stamp after the shop closed.

manduela.z: The workshop of Danish maker Manduela Riger-Kusk, trained under Poul Ilsted and known for small-scale pipes with colorful stems.

hittite-meerschaum.z: A meerschaum pipe brand that operated from Istanbul's Ümraniye district in the mid-2010s, working mainly as a wholesaler that gathered the work of Eskişehir-based carvers under one name rather than carving in its own workshop.

moonlight.z: The signature of Czech pipe master Ondřej Bárta; known for figurative briar pipes drawing on nature, the industrial age, and mythology.

charles-hester-askerlikten-tezgaha-gecen.b: Charles Hester: The American Pipemaker Who Went from Soldier to Bench
charles-hester-askerlikten-tezgaha-gecen.z: A brief portrait of American maker Charles Richard Hester Jr., who took up carving briar pipes in Missouri after more than twenty years of infantry service and has published two books on the pipe.

seasmoke-pipes.z: A small one-man American workshop run by Eric Weaver in the town of Washburn, Wisconsin, producing a few dozen pipes a year.

dublin.z: A classic pipe shape known for its conical bowl that widens upward, with roots reaching back to clay pipes. It also forms the basis for variations such as the Zulu, cutty, and acorn.

bru-bu.z: A Swiss pipe factory that emerged from the workshop Josef Brunner founded in Kleinlützel in 1878, taking the name Bru-Bu after a 1932 partnership and known for its BBK mark.

kirsten-pipe-company.z: An American brand founded in Seattle in 1936 by aeronautics professor Frederick K. Kirsten; known for its aluminum bowl and valved, disassemblable pipes.

bir-pipo-nasil-yapilir.z: The production stages of a briar pipe, from raw material to finished product: block preparation, drilling, shaping, mouthpiece work, and finishing. Both factory and craftsman traditions are covered together.

sasieni-yan-markalari-ve-tarihlendirme.b: Sasieni's Subsidiary Brands and Their Dating
sasieni-yan-markalari-ve-tarihlendirme.z: The subsidiary lines the London firm Sasieni sold under separate names beneath its flagship Four Dot series, and how these pipes are dated from the distributor's name, shape number, finish name, and shank stamp.

paul-becker.z: The path from tobacconist shop to workshop of German pipe maker Paul Becker, who works alone in the town of Pinneberg, Germany, and the features of the pipes he makes under the name Paulpipes.

dunhill-tarihlendirmesi-yuzey-islemleri-.b: Dunhill Dating: Finishes, Series, and the Year Suffix
dunhill-tarihlendirmesi-yuzey-islemleri-.z: A method for narrowing a Dunhill pipe's production year by looking at when its finish name began, whether it carries a special series stamp, and the small year suffix struck on the shank.

kiseru.z: Japan's traditional tobacco pipe: a thimble-sized metal bowl, a stem of bamboo or metal, and hair-fine shredded kizami tobacco made it the most common smoking implement of the Edo period.

henry-leonard-thomas-inc.z: An American pipe company founded in New York in 1938 that later moved its production to Sparta, North Carolina. Known for the Royalton filter chamber, it acquired Dr. Grabow in 1953 and became one of the country's largest pipe manufacturers.

tanganyika-meerschaum-corporation.z: A company founded in East Africa in 1955 that worked the Sinya deposits at the foot of Kilimanjaro, producing African meerschaum pipes under a family of brands headed by Kiko and Kilimanjaro.

briar-art.z: The brand of Brian Ruthenberg, who moved from machinist work to the pipe bench in Michigan; known for its sandblasted surfaces, hand-cut mouthpieces, and Caliper top tier.

carsten-ringling.z: German pipe maker Carsten Ringling, working in Saarland, is known for a handmade output not exceeding forty pipes a year, deep sandblasts, and forward-leaning, flattened bulldog interpretations.

ascorti.z: An Italian pipe brand founded by Roberto Ascorti under his own name in Cucciago in 1980, carrying forward the legacy of the Caminetto workshop.

hayalet-aroma.z: Ghosting is when a pipe carries the flavor and smell of a previous tobacco into later smokes. This guide covers what causes ghosting, how it varies by material, and how to remove it.

altinay.z: A block meerschaum pipe workshop founded in Eskişehir in 1964, run by the same family for three generations. Known for producing classic smoking pipes rather than the figural decorative carving common in the region.

a-tale-of-two-latakias.z: An essay comparing the Syrian and Cypriot types of Latakia, signed by G.L. Pease and now a classic in the pipe community, along with the facts underlying it.

jrn-micke.z: A brief profile of Danish master Jørn Micke (1937-2005), who left his medical studies to settle on the island of Bornholm and made no more than about twenty pipes a year.

virginia.z: The most widely grown pipe tobacco type in the world. Its high natural sugar content gives it sweet, grassy, and citrus-like flavors, and it forms the backbone of most blends.

tmpipes.z: American artisan Thomas Martin's small-scale pipe bench, which became the joint venture The Pipe Cooperative in 2008.

iran-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating in Iran, with short, factual entries for two brands.

gezer.z: Gezer is the surname shared by three brothers — Şevket, Kudret, and Mesut Gezer — in meerschaum carving. Having worked at the same bench for a time, the brothers are known for figural bowls and dense floral ornamentation.

tsuge.z: A brand founded in Tokyo in 1936 that grew out of ivory mouthpiece craftsmanship into Japan's largest pipe manufacturer.

john-aylesbury.z: A tobacconists' association founded in Germany in 1974 by seven family businesses; under a fabricated name meant to sound English, it has its branded pipes made at various European workshops.

pipo-ve-tutun-kitaplarinda-yayinciligin-.b: The Shift in Publishing Pipe and Tobacco Books: Vanity Press, Print on Demand, and Self-Publishing
pipo-ve-tutun-kitaplarinda-yayinciligin-.z: How pipe and tobacco literature, which found a place in major publishers' catalogs in the mid-twentieth century, turned over the last fifty years into books printed at the author's own expense, and what this means for readers and researchers.

stummel-bir-terimin-kokeni-ve-anlam-degi.b: Stummel: The Origin and Shifting Meaning of a Term
stummel-bir-terimin-kokeni-ve-anlam-degi.z: In German, stummel means "stub, stump" — it first named a shape of German porcelain pipe, then became the American pipe industry's term for the shank; the word no longer carries this meaning in German today.

rjr-kupon-pipolari-r-j-reynolds-ve-dr-gr.b: RJR Coupon Pipes: The R.J. Reynolds and Dr. Grabow Partnership
rjr-kupon-pipolari-r-j-reynolds-ve-dr-gr.z: The history of the Westbrook, Berwyck, Emperor, and Sculptura lines, distributed via coupons inserted in R.J. Reynolds pipe-tobacco packages and produced at the Dr. Grabow factory in Sparta.

izmir-tutunu.z: A small-leaved, sun-cured oriental tobacco from the Aegean region. With its high sugar and low nicotine, it is considered a softening, sweetening element in blends.

erickson.z: The workshop of American pipemaker Ken Erickson, who started in Minnesota in the late 1960s and continued in California, known for his freehand shapes.

briyara-alternatif-aranan-agaclar.b: Woods Sought as Alternatives to Briar
briyara-alternatif-aranan-agaclar.z: Since briar entered pipe making, dozens of tree species have been tried as its replacement; trade-press lists, tariff disputes, and government reports document why this search never succeeded.

m-linkman-co.z: A U.S. company founded in Chicago in 1898 that made briar and meerschaum pipes, known for its Dr. Grabow pipes factory-broken-in before sale, and that changed hands in 1953.

sir-del-nobile.z: Founded in 1965 as the Tuscan European arm of the American company S. M. Frank & Co., this Italian workshop produces Medico filter pipes alongside its own premium line of briar pipes bearing its own name.

jacobean.z: The first brand name Leslie and Dolly Wood used at the workshop they founded after leaving Dunhill; short-lived Jacobean is regarded as the forerunner of Ferndown.

kurleme-ve-islem.z: How a briar block rests after cutting, and how the roughed-out stummel goes through further drying and boiling and gets its bowl coating, at workshop scale.

ehrlichs.z: An American tobacconist and pipe maker that stood in the heart of Boston for more than a century, known for the meerschaum carvers who worked in its shop window.

getz-pipes.z: A one-man workshop founded by Bulgarian designer Georgi Todorov in the late 1990s, long considered the sole internationally known representative of pipemaking in his country.

eclesias-pipes.z: The one-man workshop of Czech pipe maker Pavel Holub in Kašava; a contemporary artisan signature known for its deep, sharp sandblast textures.

baraccini.z: A pipe brand made in Italy for an American retailer under its own name, offered mainly as series lines.

pipo-ve-tutun-uzmanligi-kim-uzman-sayili.b: Pipe and Tobacco Expertise: Who Counts as an Expert?
pipo-ve-tutun-uzmanligi-kim-uzman-sayili.z: Ben Rapaport's February 2023 essay investigates who is granted the label "expert" in pipes and tobacco, and by what criterion. It sets the nameless experts of promotional language against the handful of names the community actually calls by name.

sixten-ivarsson.z: Swedish-born, Copenhagen-based pipe maker Sixten Ivarsson (1910-2001). He turned a trade begun in repair work into an independent craft, and through his freehand technique is considered the starting point of the Danish school.

mastro-de-paja.z: An Italian handmade pipe workshop founded by Giancarlo Guidi in Pesaro in 1972, which changed hands several times over the following years and passed into the management of Alberto Montini. Known for sun stamps marking grade.

dunhill-pipo-tutunleri-1907-1990.z: The eighty-year span of Alfred Dunhill's business, beginning with tobacco blended to order at the Duke Street counter, turning in 1912 into named blends in the catalogue, and closing in 1981 when blending passed to another manufacturer.

vitale.z: The handmade pipe workshop Italian master Piero Vitale founded in 2014, known for its wide-bowled, short-shanked designs and its work drawing the Bluebird and Proxima series.

hiroyuki-tokutominin-bicim-dili.z: Combining the measured discipline of the Danish school with Japanese aesthetic sensibilities, Hiroyuki Tokutomi built a design language that deliberately broke with the briar pipe's expectation of symmetry. This entry examines his approach to form, his biography, and his stamps.

paolo-becker.z: An Italian handmade pipe brand founded in Rome by Fritz Becker and his son Paolo Becker, carrying its own stamp since 1979. Known for its grading system named after playing cards.

bennwik.z: The one-man Swedish workshop of illustrator Andreas Bennwik, based in Stockholm, self-taught and known for briar pipes with classic proportions and little decoration.

dan-pipe.z: A German pipe and tobacco house founded in 1972 by Heiko Behrens to sell handmade Danish pipes by mail order; in 1991 it built its own tobacco factory (DTM) in Lauenburg and closed in 2023.

caminetto-marka-tarihi-seriler-ve-damga-.b: Caminetto: Brand History, Series, and Reading the Stamps
caminetto-marka-tarihi-seriler-ve-damga-.z: The founding of Caminetto in Cucciago in 1968, its break-up in 1979-80, and its production resuming in 1986; dating from the mustache emblem on the mouthpiece and the shank stamps.

agizlik-ara-katmanlari.z: The thin decorative slices glued at the end of a mouthpiece where it meets the shank: material selection, pin arrangement, joining with epoxy, and finishing on the lathe.

jobert.z: A one-person South African pipe workshop founded by Johan Slabbert in the early 2000s, working with native African woods. Its pipes are known by the JOBERT stamp on the shank.

nanna-ivarsson.z: Nanna Ivarsson (b. 1974) is a Danish pipe maker, granddaughter of Sixten Ivarsson and daughter of Lars Ivarsson. As the family's third-generation maker, she carries on her grandfather's bench, tools, and stamp.

abdulla.z: A British tobacco firm founded in London in 1902, best known for its Oriental-blend cigarettes, which also marketed briar pipes under its own name.

antoniewski.z: A briar pipe maker working in Poland's pipe town of Przemyśl since 1989, known for figural and portrait carving.

virginia-perique-harmani.z: A classic blend family in which Virginia tobacco is spiced with a small amount of Louisiana-grown Perique; known for its sweet-sour balance and its aptitude for aging.

clay.z: A collective look at clay pipe-making's production centers scattered country by country, the workshops that left their mark in those centers, and the small number of makers keeping the craft alive today.

w-larsen.z: A tobacconist founded in Copenhagen in 1864, which a century later became one of the training grounds of Danish pipe-making by opening its own pipe workshop, and closed in 2005.

guney-afrika-pipo-markalari-dizini.b: Directory of South African Pipe Brands
guney-afrika-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands from South Africa, containing brief, factual entries for two names.

dunhillin-ek-damgalari.z: The secondary stamps seen on the shank of Dunhill pipes beyond the shape and year code: the factory's own H.W, C, and 6 prefix conventions, plus extra year codes added at the point of sale or later, small squares, and strikes with no counterpart in the ledger.

murf-sculptured-pipes-heykel-gibi-oyulan.b: Murf Sculptured Pipes: Sculpted American Pipes
murf-sculptured-pipes-heykel-gibi-oyulan.z: Murf O'Dean's solo sculptural pipe bench in California. The first pipe was carved in 1973, a long hiatus followed a 1983 national carving award, and production resumed in 2016.

billiard.z: The Billiard is the straight shape considered the benchmark of classic pipe shapes, with its near-cylindrical bowl and balanced proportions; it's found in nearly every manufacturer's catalog.

custom-bilt.z: Custom-Bilt is a briar pipe brand founded in the US by Tracy Mincer in the 1930s, known for its large bowls and roughly carved surface; the name changed hands several times over half a century.

tophane-luleciligi.z: Tophane pipe-making is a craft tradition from Ottoman Istanbul producing red-clay chibouk and hookah bowls; in the 19th century it earned worldwide fame under the name "Tophane work."

paradis-pipes.z: A Canadian brand born of the pipe-making tradition of the Paradis family of Quebec, founded in 1978 by brothers Gilles and Fernand Paradis.

windjammer-pipes.z: A small US workshop run by Justin Bain in Philadelphia, stating that its pipes are shaped by hand without a lathe.

kittner.z: One of the select benches that launched freehand pipemaking in postwar Germany, signed with the name of Günter Kittner of Bremen.

kurt-huhn-rhode-islandli-bir-tezgah-usta.b: Kurt Huhn (Pipecrafter): A Bench Craftsman from Rhode Island
kurt-huhn-rhode-islandli-bir-tezgah-usta.z: Kurt A. Huhn is an American craftsman who began making handmade briar pipes under the name Pipecrafter in his Rhode Island workshop in the early 2000s. He is known for his experiments reversing the usual shaping order and for the connections he built through the online pipe community.

s-e-thile-pipes.z: An American handmade pipe workshop run by piano technician and musician Scott Thile in Kentucky, who groups his work into three lines named Étude, Opus and Freehand. Thile is also the founder of Pipedia.

pipo-doldurma-ve-icim-tekniklerinin-kayn.b: The Origins of Pipe Packing and Smoking Techniques
pipo-doldurma-ve-icim-tekniklerinin-kayn.z: An entry examining how pipe packing and smoking techniques came to form a shared vocabulary, whose names became attached to known methods, and the influence of competitive smoking on this body of knowledge.

uzun-boyunlular.z: A grouping name that brings together the Canadian, Lumberman, Liverpool, and Lovat shapes under one roof; a practical classification born not from catalogs but from the community's own shape literature.

tine-pipes.z: The personal pipe signature of Austrian architect Martin "Tine" Steinthaler, based in Klagenfurt; a design-driven, small-scale production that began in 1999 at Peter Matzhold's workshop.

meerqueen-meerschaum-pipes.z: The brand name used in the international market by a Turkish workshop that carves block meerschaum in Eskişehir. Known for carvings bearing a master's signature and a dual six-point grading scale.

scott-anderson.z: American pipe maker Scott J. Anderson, based in Northern California, is known for his low annual output, bamboo-shanked work, and small-scale pipes.

iyi-bir-briyar-pipoyu-ne-belirler.b: What Makes a Good Briar Pipe?
iyi-bir-briyar-pipoyu-ne-belirler.z: The criteria used to judge the quality of a briar pipe: the age and grain of the root, the curing method, workmanship on the stummel and mouthpiece, finishing, and tolerance for flaws.

colm-magner.z: Colm Magner, a Canadian pipe maker with a background in theater, began carving in 1998 and became known for his kidney-sectioned "Boxer" form.

pipe-making-for-the-rank-amateur.b: Pipe Making For The Rank Amateur
pipe-making-for-the-rank-amateur.z: An essay on amateur pipe making by Robert Everett. It addresses how a hobbyist without industrial-grade equipment can turn a briar block into a finished pipe using basic hand tools.

pipoya-baslangic-doldurma-yakma-ve-icim.b: Getting Started with a Pipe: Packing, Lighting, and Smoking
pipoya-baslangic-doldurma-yakma-ve-icim.z: A step-by-step basic guide to packing, lighting, and enjoying your first pipe. Common beginner mistakes and practical fixes.

kaufmann-bros-bondy.z: American pipe company founded in New York in 1851, which gave rise to the Kaywoodie and Yello-Bole brands before passing to S. M. Frank & Co. in 1955.

keens-steakhouse-tavana-asili-kil-pipo-k.b: Keens Steakhouse: The Clay Pipe Collection Hanging From the Ceiling
keens-steakhouse-tavana-asili-kil-pipo-k.z: Opened in New York in 1885, Keens Steakhouse is known for a collection of tens of thousands of clay pipes born from the custom of patrons leaving their pipes in the restaurant's keeping.

saladich.z: A Spanish workshop bearing the name of Catalan master Joan Saladich i Garriga, known for entirely hand-carved, made-to-order pipes.

ludwig-lorenz.z: The current workshop of the Lorenz family, who have made pipes for three generations in Austria's Tyrol region. The double-filter pipe the family developed is the brand's best-known signature.

golden-horn.z: Golden Horn is an export brand that carried Turkish meerschaum pipes to the United States; it is known as the first company to bring carver İsmet Bekler's work to the American market.

israil-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands made in Israel or documented as Israeli-made, with short, factual entries for five brands.

zeman.z: The name used on handmade briar pipes made in Jan Zeman's one-person workshop in Nelson, New Zealand; a signature known for its named series that today produces no new pieces.

pres-tutunler-ve-flake-piposu-kavrami.b: Pressed Tobaccos and the Concept of the Flake Pipe
pres-tutunler-ve-flake-piposu-kavrami.z: How tobaccos molded under pressure behave, and which bowl size and which pipe shape are considered well suited to them.

brentegani-pipe.z: The one-man workshop of Verona's Michele Brentegani; an Italian handmade pipe brand known for its lightweight bowls, shapes blending classic and Danish-school lines, and azure-blue vulcanite mouthpieces.

accademia-della-pipa.z: A non-profit craft school founded in 2020 by four Italian pipemakers during the pandemic lockdowns, built on a master-apprentice model.

erik-hesse.z: An American collector known for his collection focused on Dunhill pipes; his holdings, spanning the 1920s to the 2000s, are documented on Pipedia divided by period.

peretti.z: A pipe and blend brand carried under its own name by a Boston tobacconist founded in 1870 and run under the same name for four generations.

pipo-tutunu-saklama.z: How to keep pipe tobacco fresh over the short and medium term: choosing the right container, moisture and temperature conditions, reviving dried-out tobacco, and guarding against mold.

goussard-pipes.z: A South African workshop Charl Goussard runs in Cape Town, combining the flowing lines of the Danish school with briar as well as local woods.

yuzey-islemleri-smooth-sandblast-rustik.z: The three main surface finishes applied to briar pipes — smooth, sandblast, and rustic — presented with their techniques, histories, and practical differences.

j-b-priestley-romanci-ve-pipo-meraklisi.b: J. B. Priestley: Novelist and Pipe Enthusiast
j-b-priestley-romanci-ve-pipo-meraklisi.z: English novelist, playwright, and essayist J. B. Priestley (1894-1984) made the pipe part of his public identity and was one of the rare literary figures to write about tobacco. His archive in Bradford preserves more than seventy of his pipes.

ermenistan-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipe brands originating from Armenia; contains a short, factual entry for the single brand on record.

malezya-pipo-markalari-dizini.z: An alphabetical directory of pipemakers working in Malaysia, containing short profile entries for two documented brands.

tobias-kaffl.z: A German master working in the Bavarian town of Bad Feilnbach who moved from carpentry into pipe making and produces freehand pipes in the Danish line.

regis-mccafferty-naspcnin-kurucularindan.b: Regis McCafferty: A Founding Writer of the NASPC
regis-mccafferty-naspcnin-kurucularindan.z: American writer Regis McCafferty, who gave pipe-smoking characters a place in his stories and novels, and his standing in the community as one of the founders of the association established in 1993 that later became the NASPC.

jan-andersson.z: A Swedish writer, collector, and longtime secretary of Svenska Pipklubben who documented the Scandinavian handmade pipe tradition.

shellcraft.z: An American pipe series from the 1920s produced by Reiss-Premier, known for its hand-carved surface, marketed under the name "The Drinkless, Shellcraft."

chheda-pipes.z: An American handmade pipe brand made by Premal Chheda in the workshop of his family business, Smokers' Haven, in Columbus, Ohio.

clarin.z: A contemporary clay pipe workshop founded by Edna Bertin in Caxias do Sul, Brazil, finishing single-piece clay bodies through two separate firings and glazing.

yashtylov.z: The workshop Viktor Yashtylov of Saint Petersburg founded in 2005; counted among the most-cited names in contemporary Russian pipemaking for its freehand designs and its magnetic mouthpiece-to-shank connection.

pirkenhammer.z: A porcelain manufactory founded in 1803 in the Bohemian village of Pirkenhammer (today Březová); it produced porcelain pipes alongside tableware in its early years and is known for its crossed-hammers mark.

almanya-pipo-markalari-dizini-2.z: The second part of the alphabetical directory of pipe brands, workshops, and makers in Germany: eight entries from Volker Bier to Wunderlich.

christian-wolfsteiner.z: The small output of freeform pipes and the workshop method of Christian Wolfsteiner, a German pipe maker born in 1961 who worked in Ingolstadt under the Tarock Briar stamp.

ron-powell.z: An American maker known under the RDPipes signature, who moved from collecting to repair and then to the bench; his craftsmanship favors engineering over shape.

karl-erik.z: A Danish brand founded by Karl Erik Ottendahl (1942-2004); known for a production system that did not hide bench assistance, bringing freehand pipes within reach of the moderate-income smoker.

almanya-pipo-markalari-dizini-1.z: A briefly annotated directory of workshop, factory, and brand names that produced pipes in Germany; this part covers 90 entries between Aachen and Van Wandeir.

medico.z: An American pipe brand S. M. Frank & Co. built around an absorbent paper filter in 1933; its briar and Brylon bodies reached a broad public for decades.

good-bye-cigarettes-hello-pipe-sigaradan.b: Good-Bye Cigarettes, Hello Pipe: A Text on Switching from Cigarettes to the Pipe
good-bye-cigarettes-hello-pipe-sigaradan.z: The identity of the piece signed by Steve Fallon that appeared in the NASPC newsletter The Pipe Collector, the nicotine assumption behind it, and how it compares with today's public-health data.

zhesong-pipes.z: The Suzhou workshop of Li Zhesong, who left an architecture career for pipe making; counted among the earliest examples of contemporary handmade pipe production in China.

yaygin-acemi-hatalari.z: The mistakes most commonly made by pipe-smoking beginners, and the practical fix for each — from smoking too fast, to wet tobacco, incorrect packing, and neglected maintenance.

winslow.z: The workshop Poul Winsløw, who rose to foreman at Preben Holm's factory, set up in his home in Hvidovre after the factory closed. Known for colorful staining, shank inlays, and freehand bodies.

kimligi-belirsiz-markalar-pipo-markalari.b: Index of Pipe Brands of Unidentified Origin
kimligi-belirsiz-markalar-pipo-markalari.z: An alphabetical index of pipe stamps whose maker, country, or period has not been resolved; fifty-five entries from Allerton to Wilshire Club are gathered as short entries.

wimbledon.z: An American brand name whose pipes were overwhelmingly made at the Dr. Grabow factory in North Carolina; frequently misidentified because of a small number of English-made examples and a diamond-shaped mouthpiece stamp.

don-lou.z: The brand of the workshop Dominic Cazzetta ran alone in Brooklyn's Bensonhurst neighborhood; known for unpainted, unfilled briar pipes with a natural finish.

kiko.z: The best-known name among meerschaum pipes produced in Tanganyika; identified by its briar bowl lined with meerschaum, an elephant emblem, and a 'Made in Tanganyika' stamp.

dsh-pipes.z: The one-man workshop American maker David S. Huber founded in 2012; known for handmade briar pipes produced in a sculpture studio in Durham, combining Danish and Japanese lines.

luigi-pipes.z: A family business founded in 1910 in Avellaneda by Italian immigrant José Gaspar Arbotto, regarded as Argentina's first pipe factory.

1980lerin-sahte-dunhilleri.z: A small group of pipes made from genuine Dunhill briar yet stamped to appear decades older and far rarer than they were. The affair, uncovered at a pipe show in 1984, is considered the most talked-about forgery case in briar pipe collecting.

19-yuzyil-oyma-lule-tasi-pipolari.z: From roughly 1850 to 1920, workshops stretching from Vienna to New York carved figural meerschaum pipes one at a time by hand. This entry covers the material's possibilities, workshop organization, and examples shown at world fairs.

catlinite-argillite-ve-terrakota-pipolar.z: Three ancient bowl materials that stand in the shadow of briar and meerschaum: catlinite, the red pipestone of the North American plains; the black argillite of the North Pacific coast; and terracotta, spanning Mesoamerica to the Ottoman chibouk.

ingiliz-kutu-tutunlerinin-tarihlendirilm.z: Methods for narrowing the age of tinned pipe tobacco produced in Britain, using the ℮ mark, tax stamps, importer address, tin shape, and label wording.

caminetto.z: An Italian brand founded in Cucciago in 1968 by Giuseppe Ascorti and Luigi Radice, which drew great interest in America in the 1970s through Gianni Davoli's distribution. Known for its mustache emblem and rustic Business finish.

holtorp.z: A pipe maker who worked in 1960s Copenhagen around Pibe-Dan, standing apart from the fashion of the day with large, thick-lined bodies.

pipas-de-cochera.z: The name Mexican engineer Roberto González González gave to the pipes he made himself; known for amateur pipe-making notes published on a personal website in the early 2000s.

iki-erken-dunhill-damaged-damgasi-ve-esi.b: Two Early Dunhills: the 'DAMAGED' Stamp and the Equal-Length DUNHILL/LONDON Line
iki-erken-dunhill-damaged-damgasi-ve-esi.z: Through two small early-production Dunhill pipes, the place in dating held by the 'DAMAGED' stamp struck on flawed bodies and the equal-length DUNHILL/LONDON stamp briefly used in late 1918.
